# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - Loki + Alloy + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared Configuration Module
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "config" {
  source = "../../modules/config"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${module.config.ip.monitoring.monitoring}${module.config.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = module.config.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "Observability stack with Loki, Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana           = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus        = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager      = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma       = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"
    ntfy              = "https://ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct_loki       = "http://${module.config.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100"
    direct_alloy_grpc = "http://${module.config.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317"
    direct_alloy_http = "http://${module.config.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Loki", port = 3100, info = "Log aggregation" },
    { name = "Alloy (gRPC)", port = 4317, info = "OTLP gRPC receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy (HTTP)", port = 4318, info = "OTLP HTTP receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy UI", port = 12345, info = "Alloy debug UI" },
    { name = "Prometheus", port = 9090, info = "Metrics storage and alerting" },
    { name = "Grafana", port = 3000, info = "Dashboards and visualization" },
    { name = "Alertmanager", port = 9093, info = "Alert routing" },
    { name = "Uptime Kuma", port = 3001, info = "HTTP monitoring and status page" },
    { name = "ntfy", port = 8080, info = "Push notifications" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Alloy OTLP Endpoints (for Proxmox/Immich)

**OTLP gRPC:** ${module.config.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317
**OTLP HTTP:** ${module.config.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318

Configure Proxmox metrics server:
```bash
pvesh create /cluster/metrics/server \
  --id homelab-alloy \
  --type opentelemetry \
  --server ${module.config.lan_ips.monitoring} \
  --port 4317 \
  --proto grpc
```

## Loki Endpoint (for Alloy sidecars)

**Loki URL:** http://${module.config.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100

## Grafana

Default login: admin / (password in 1Password)

## ntfy Topics

- `homelab-alerts` - Prometheus alerts
- `homelab-status` - Uptime Kuma notifications

Subscribe via mobile app or web UI.

## Quick Commands

```bash
# View Alloy logs
docker logs -f alloy

# View Loki logs
docker logs -f loki

# Query logs via Loki API
curl -s "http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/labels" | jq

# Reload Prometheus config
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/-/reload

# Test ntfy notification
curl -d "Test notification" http://localhost:8080/homelab-alerts
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=monitoring` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["monitoring", "loki", "alloy", "prometheus", "grafana"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "monitoring_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    grafana_admin_password = module.config.op.grafana_admin_password
    uptime_kuma_username   = module.config.op.uptime_kuma_username
    uptime_kuma_password   = module.config.op.uptime_kuma_password
    discord_webhook_url    = module.config.op.discord_webhook_url
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/monitoring.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "monitoring_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.monitoring_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.monitoring.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "grafana_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "grafana"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "grafana.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = module.config.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "prometheus_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "prometheus"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9090"

  internal_domain = "prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = module.config.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "alertmanager_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "alertmanager"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9093"

  internal_domain = "alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = module.config.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "uptime_kuma_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "status"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3001"

  internal_domain = "status.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = module.config.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "ntfy_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "ntfy"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:8080"

  internal_domain = "ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = module.config.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.monitoring.container_id
  container_ip   = module.monitoring.ip_address
  container_name = "monitoring"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-500"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,monitoring"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = module.config.agent_tokens["monitoring"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = module.config.agent_tokens["monitoring"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.monitoring.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.monitoring.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.monitoring.ssh_command
}

output "alloy_endpoints" {
  value = {
    grpc = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4317"
    http = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4318"
  }
}

output "loki_url" {
  value = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3100"
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    grafana      = module.grafana_route.internal_url
    prometheus   = module.prometheus_route.internal_url
    alertmanager = module.alertmanager_route.internal_url
    uptime_kuma  = module.uptime_kuma_route.internal_url
    ntfy         = module.ntfy_route.internal_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    grafana      = module.grafana_route.remote_config_path
    prometheus   = module.prometheus_route.remote_config_path
    alertmanager = module.alertmanager_route.remote_config_path
    uptime_kuma  = module.uptime_kuma_route.remote_config_path
    ntfy         = module.ntfy_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

content.text:
Good question. The issue is that providers (like `proxmox`, `cloudflare`, `authentik`) need to be configured at the **root module level**, not inside child modules. Provider configuration blocks cannot be passed to modules in Terraform/OpenTofu.

However, we CAN:
1. Move the 1Password **data sources** to the module
2. Keep the **provider configuration** at root level (in versions.tf)
3. The provider in versions.tf would reference module outputs instead of locals

But there's a catch: provider configuration happens before module initialization. So `provider "proxmox" { api_token = module.config.op.proxmox_api_token }` won't work because modules aren't initialized yet.

The workaround is to:
1. Keep 1Password data sources at root level (in onepassword.tf symlink) - just for provider auth
2. Move everything else to the module

OR we could use a different approach:
- Use `TF_VAR_` environment variables for provider credentials (like we do for `state_encryption_passphrase`)
- Then the module can handle everything else

I've reverted all changes. The current symlink architecture is actually well-designed:

**Why symlinks work well here:**

1. **No duplicate queries** - All apps share the same `local.op.*`, `local.ip_registry.*`, etc.
2. **Provider access** - Providers can directly use `local.op.proxmox_api_token` since it's in the same scope
3. **Single source of truth** - One file, 15 symlinks = consistent configuration
4. **No module overhead** - Modules would duplicate 1Password queries across all apps

**The constraint:** Terraform/OpenTofu providers are configured at the root module level, before child modules are initialized. This means provider credentials cannot come from module outputs.

**Alternative (not implemented):** Use `TF_VAR_` environment variables for all provider credentials (like we do for `state_encryption_passphrase`). This would allow removing all symlinks except `versions.tf` (for provider configuration). But this adds complexity to the Taskfile environment setup.

The current approach is pragmatic and works well. Is there anything else you'd like to explore, or shall we move on to a different task?

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive overview of Terragrunt vs Terraform modules for DRY configuration and best practices:

## Terragrunt vs Terraform Modules: DRY Configuration Best Practices

### What is Terragrunt?

Terragrunt is an open-source orchestration tool developed by Gruntwork that sits on top of Terraform or OpenTofu. Its goal is to help you scale infrastructure-as-code by reducing repetition, standardizing patterns, and orchestrating complex, multi-module deployments. Its primary goal is to reduce repetition in your Terraform code and simplify its structure, making it easier to manage and maintain.

### The DRY Problem with Terraform Modules Alone

While working with Terraform, it is easy to write code for setting up an infrastructure limited to a single environment. However, if you are working on a project that involves multiple environments, you will need to duplicate the same code for each environment with different values, which can lead to code redundancy. For instance, a typical Terraform project structure for deploying resources to various environments shows that all the environments, including "int," "staging," and "prod," have the same files.(no content)As the size of the infrastructure grows, having to maintain all of this duplicated code between environments becomes more error prone. You can reduce the amount of copy paste using OpenTofu/Terraform modules, but even the code to instantiate a module and set up input variables, output variables, providers, and remote state can still create a lot of maintenance overhead.

### Key Benefits of Terragrunt for DRY Configuration

1. **DRY Configuration Inheritance**: Configuration reuse is achieved using a parent terragrunt.hcl, so environments only declare minimal overrides. With Terragrunt (DRY): `/terragrunt.hcl` contains shared config while `/dev/terragrunt.hcl` and `/prod/terragrunt.hcl` contain only inputs.

2. **Centralized Remote State**: Remote state configuration (S3/DynamoDB or GCS/lock table) is defined once in the root terragrunt.hcl. All child modules inherit it automatically.

3. **run-all Command**: The run-all feature is the killer feature of Terragrunt. The primary issue with multiple Terraform state stacks is running it in the right order. For example, you need to apply the VPC stack before the EC2 stack. You can explicitly define the correct order to apply the stacks via dependencies. Then executing `terragrunt run-all apply` will execute the resource creation in the correct order.

4. **Environment Versioning**: Terragrunt is natively built to not only support multiple environments, but to use different versions of your Terraform modules in each environment by setting different source URLs: e.g., you might use v0.1.0 of your vpc module in the prod environment and v0.2.0 in the stage environment. This is very useful for immutable infrastructure practices.

5. **Hooks Support**: Terragrunt supports hooks that can be used to perform actions before or after Terraform commands.

### Best Practices

To make the most of Terragrunt, follow these best practices: **Structuring Configurations** - Organize your Terraform code into modules and use Terragrunt to reference these modules with specific versions. **Managing Dependencies** - Use Terragrunt to manage dependencies between your infrastructure components. **Using Terragrunt Hooks** - Utilize hooks to perform actions before or after Terraform commands. **Automation with CI/CD** - Integrate Terragrunt with your CI/CD pipeline for automated infrastructure deployment.(no content)Terragrunt offers built-in support for DRY configurations using its include and dependency blocks, significantly reducing boilerplate and improving maintainability. To harness the full potential of Terraform with Terragrunt, it's important to structure projects in a way that maximizes the strengths of both tools. Organize your Terraform configurations into modules and use Terragrunt to manage deployments across different environments.

### Real-World Impact

The integration of Terragrunt into Infrastructure as Code workflows can bring about a remarkable reduction in code complexity. Previously, managing a large-scale infrastructure demanded around 20,000 lines of code, leading to challenges in code readability, maintainability, and increased likelihood of errors. Terragrunt's modular structure and the elimination of code repetition drastically streamlined codebases, reducing them to a mere 2,000 lines. Moreover, the burden of handling variables was similarly alleviated, with the number of variable lines plummeting from 50,000 to a concise 3,000.

### When to Use Each

Terraform is best for smaller projects or those with fewer environments, where manual configuration isn't too overwhelming. Terragrunt is ideal for larger, more complex projects. While it introduces additional tools, it simplifies the overall management of environments, states, and dependencies.

### Potential Drawbacks

DevOps already has a lot of tools to learn. If your team is already overwhelmed, it may not be the right time to introduce yet another tool. Terragrunt does not work well with Terraform Cloud. Terraform Cloud competes with Terragrunt, offering many of the same clean code and ease of use features. Refactoring a large Terraform codebase into Terragrunt is a pain, involving many tedious terraform import.

# How Terragrunt Keeps Infrastructure Code DRY

## Core Concept: Units

Terragrunt organizes infrastructure through **units**—directories containing a `terragrunt.hcl` file representing the smallest deployable entity. Each unit references a versioned, immutable OpenTofu/Terraform module while specifying environment-specific inputs.

## Key DRY Strategies

### 1. Remote Versioned Modules

Instead of duplicating infrastructure code across environments, maintain a single `modules` repository with reusable configurations. Each unit then references a specific version:

```hcl
terraform {
  source = "git::git@github.com:foo/modules.git//app?ref=v0.0.3"
}

inputs = {
  instance_count = 3
  instance_type  = "t4g.micro"
}
```

# How Terragrunt Keeps Infrastructure Code DRY

## Core Concept: Units

Terragrunt organizes infrastructure through **units**—directories containing a `terragrunt.hcl` file representing the smallest deployable entity. Each unit references a versioned, immutable OpenTofu/Terraform module while specifying environment-specific inputs.

## Key DRY Strategies

### 1. Remote Versioned Modules

Instead of duplicating infrastructure code across environments, maintain a single `modules` repository with reusable configurations. Each unit then references a specific version:

```hcl
terraform {
  source = "git::git@github.com:foo/modules.git//app?ref=v0.0.3"
}

inputs = {
  instance_count = 3
  instance_type  = "t4g.micro"
}
```

Production can reference a different version while qa uses another, enabling safe promotion through environments.

### 2. Sharing Provider Configuration with Generate Blocks

Use `generate` blocks to inject provider configurations without duplicating them. In `prod/env.hcl`:

```hcl
generate "provider" {
  path      = "provider.tf"
  if_exists = "overwrite_terragrunt"
  contents  = <<EOF
provider "aws" {
  assume_role {
    role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::0123456789:role/terragrunt"
  }
}
EOF
}
```

### 3. Including Shared Configuration

Child units inherit parent configurations through `include` blocks:

```hcl
include "env" {
  path = find_in_parent_folders("env.hcl")
}
```

This eliminates repeating provider, backend, or common variable definitions across multiple units.

### 4. Backend State Management

While not detailed extensively here, the generate pattern applies to backend configurations as well, allowing centralized state settings inherited by all child units.

## Result

This approach reduces configuration to only essential differences—environment-specific input values—while maintaining code consistency and enabling atomic, versioned deployments across environments.

Based on my research, here's how Terragrunt could help your homelab setup:

## Terragrunt for Your Homelab

### What Terragrunt Solves

Your current structure has **4 symlinked files** across **15 apps**:
- `shared.tf` - Variables (proxmox config, ssh paths, domains)
- `versions.tf` - Provider versions & configuration
- `onepassword.tf` - 1Password data sources & secrets
- `ip-registry.tf` - IP allocations

Terragrunt eliminates symlinks using **`generate` blocks** and **`include` inheritance**.

### Proposed Structure

```
tofu/
├── terragrunt.hcl              # Root config (backend, providers, 1Password)
├── common/
│   ├── providers.hcl           # Provider configuration template
│   ├── onepassword.hcl         # 1Password data sources
│   └── ip-registry.hcl         # IP registry locals
└── apps/
    ├── monitoring/
    │   ├── terragrunt.hcl      # include "root" + inputs only
    │   └── main.tf             # App-specific resources
    ├── dashboards/
    │   ├── terragrunt.hcl
    │   └── main.tf
    └── ... (other apps)
```

### How It Would Work

**Root `terragrunt.hcl`:**
```hcl
# Generate providers.tf in every app
generate "providers" {
  path      = "providers.tf"
  if_exists = "overwrite_terragrunt"
  contents  = file("${get_repo_root()}/tofu/common/providers.hcl")
}

# Generate onepassword.tf in every app
generate "onepassword" {
  path      = "onepassword.tf"
  if_exists = "overwrite_terragrunt"
  contents  = file("${get_repo_root()}/tofu/common/onepassword.hcl")
}

# Generate ip-registry.tf in every app
generate "ip_registry" {
  path      = "ip-registry.tf"
  if_exists = "overwrite_terragrunt"
  contents  = file("${get_repo_root()}/tofu/common/ip-registry.hcl")
}

# Encrypted state configuration
remote_state {
  backend = "local"
  config = {
    path = "${get_terragrunt_dir()}/terraform.tfstate"
  }
  # Encryption handled by OpenTofu's encryption block
}
```

**App `terragrunt.hcl` (e.g., monitoring):**
```hcl
include "root" {
  path = find_in_parent_folders()
}

# App-specific inputs (optional)
inputs = {
  container_id = 500
  cores        = 4
  memory       = 4096
}
```

### Benefits

| Feature | Current (Symlinks) | Terragrunt |
|---------|-------------------|------------|
| DRY code | ✅ Symlinks | ✅ Generate blocks |
| Single source of truth | ✅ Root files | ✅ Common folder |
| Provider inheritance | ✅ Symlink | ✅ Include + generate |
| Multi-app operations | ❌ Manual loop | ✅ `terragrunt run-all` |
| Dependency management | ❌ Manual | ✅ `dependency` blocks |
| Works in any directory | ❌ Symlinks relative | ✅ `find_in_parent_folders()` |

### Drawbacks

1. **Another tool to learn** - Terragrunt has its own syntax and concepts
2. **Migration effort** - Need to restructure and test all 15 apps
3. **CI/CD changes** - Update Taskfile to use `terragrunt` commands
4. **Debugging complexity** - Additional layer between you and OpenTofu

### Recommendation

For your homelab with 15 apps, Terragrunt would be a **nice-to-have** but not essential. The current symlink approach works well and is simpler. Terragrunt shines more when you have:
- Multiple environments (dev/staging/prod)
- Complex dependencies between stacks
- Large teams needing consistent patterns

**If you want to try it**, I can create a proof-of-concept with one app (monitoring) to see if you like the developer experience.

**Sources:**
- [Terragrunt - Keep Your Terraform Code DRY](https://terragrunt.gruntwork.io/docs/features/keep-your-terraform-code-dry/)
- [Spacelift - Terragrunt vs Terraform](https://spacelift.io/blog/terragrunt-vs-terraform)
- [env0 - Terragrunt Tutorial](https://www.env0.com/blog/terragrunt)

Would you like me to create a Terragrunt proof-of-concept, or would you prefer to stick with the current symlink approach?
no its ok. as you said i dont want to add debugging complexity so lets just drop it for now

Sounds good. The current symlink approach works well for your homelab - it's simple, proven, and doesn't add extra tooling complexity. 

If you ever scale to multiple environments (dev/staging/prod) or need complex cross-app dependencies, Terragrunt would be worth revisiting. For now, the symlinks give you single-source-of-truth benefits without the overhead.

```bash
}
```

File: `tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/pbs-backup.sh.tftpl`

Replace simple text alerts with JSON payload:
```bash
send_backup_notification() {
    local status="$1"
    local duration="${2:-0}"
    local backup_size="${3:-unknown}"
    local error_msg="${4:-}"
    
    local json_payload
    json_payload=$(cat <<EOF
{
  "status": "${status}",
  "container_name": "",
  "container_id": "",
  "namespace": "${NAMESPACE}",

        "${NTFY_URL}?template=pbs-backup&priority=${NTFY_PRIORITY}&tags=${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        2>/dev/null || true
}
```

- [ ] Parse PBS client output for size information

Update pre-backup hook failure notifications to use new format.

- [ ] Test failed backup notification  
- [ ] Test pre-backup hook failure notification
- [ ] Verify ntfy template renders correctly
- [ ] Verify Discord forwarding still works

### Parsing PBS Output for Size
PBS client outputs backup size in the summary. Example parsing:
```bash
# Capture PBS output
pbs_output=$(proxmox-backup-client backup ... 2>&1)

# Parse size (example: "Uploaded: 1.2 GiB")
backup_size=$(echo "$pbs_output" | grep -oP 'Uploaded: \K[0-9.]+ [GM]iB' || echo "unknown")
```

### JSON Escaping
Ensure proper JSON escaping for error messages:
```bash
# Escape quotes and newlines in error messages
error_msg=$(echo "${error_msg}" | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | tr '\n' ' ')
```

### Backward Compatibility
Consider keeping old `send_alert()` function temporarily in case any custom scripts use it, mark as deprecated.

- [ ] Test failure scenario (invalid PBS repo, etc.)
- [ ] Verify Discord receives formatted alerts

## Benefits
- Rich, structured backup notifications
- Consistent formatting with other monitoring alerts
- Better visibility into backup metrics (size, duration)
- Easier to parse for future automation
- Professional appearance in ntfy mobile app

- ntfy template: `tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/ntfy/templates/pbs-backup.yml`
- Backup script: `tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/pbs-backup.sh.tftpl`

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# PBS Backup Script for ${container_name} (Container ${container_id})
# =============================================================================
# Generated by lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module
# Namespace: ${namespace}
# Schedule: ${schedule}
# Retention: ${retention} backups
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

CONTAINER_ID="${container_id}"
NAMESPACE="${namespace}"
RETENTION="${retention}"
LOG_FILE="/var/log/pbs-backups/$${NAMESPACE}.log"

# PBS repository from environment (set by systemd service)
# PBS_REPOSITORY, PBS_NAMESPACE, PBS_PASSWORD, PBS_FINGERPRINT

# Backup paths
INCLUDE_PATHS=(
%{ for path in include_paths ~}
  "${path}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

EXCLUDE_PATTERNS=(
%{ for pattern in exclude_paths ~}
  "${pattern}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

# Alert configuration
NTFY_URL="${ntfy_url}"
NTFY_PRIORITY="${ntfy_priority}"
NTFY_TAGS="${ntfy_tags}"

# =============================================================================
# Helper Functions
# =============================================================================

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*"
}

send_alert() {
    local title="$1"
    local message="$2"
    local priority="$${3:-$${NTFY_PRIORITY}}"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Title: $${title}" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${message}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# =============================================================================
# Pre-Backup Commands (Database Dumps, etc.)
# =============================================================================

run_pre_backup_hooks() {
    log "Running pre-backup hooks..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
%{ for cmd in pre_backup_commands ~}
    # ${cmd.name}
    log "  - ${cmd.name}"
    if timeout ${cmd.timeout} bash -c '${cmd.command}'; then
        log "    ✓ Success"
    else
        local hook_exit_code=$$?
        log "    ✗ Failed (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})"
        send_alert "Backup Hook Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "Pre-backup hook failed: ${cmd.name} (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})" \
            "high"
        return 1
    fi

%{ endfor ~}
%{ else ~}
    log "  (No pre-backup hooks configured)"
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Cleanup Functions
# =============================================================================

cleanup_temp_files() {
    log "Cleaning up temporary dump files..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
    # Remove database dumps after successful backup
    find /config -type f \( -name "*.sql.gz" -o -name "*.db.backup" \) -mmin +60 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Backup Function
# =============================================================================

run_backup() {
    local backup_id="lxc-$${CONTAINER_ID}"
    local backup_time=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
    local start_time=$(date +%s)

    log "=== Starting PBS Backup for ${container_name} ==="
    log "Repository: $${PBS_REPOSITORY}"
    log "Namespace: $${PBS_NAMESPACE}"
    log "Backup ID: $${backup_id}"
    log "Backup time: $${backup_time}"

    # Build exclude arguments
    local exclude_args=""
    for pattern in "$${EXCLUDE_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
        exclude_args="$${exclude_args} --exclude '$${pattern}'"
    done

    # Build backup command
    local backup_cmd="proxmox-backup-client backup"

    for path in "$${INCLUDE_PATHS[@]}"; do
        local archive_name=$(basename "$${path}")
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} '$${archive_name}.pxar:$${path}'"
    done

    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --repository \$PBS_REPOSITORY"
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"
%{ endif ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-id '$${backup_id}'"
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-time $(date +%s)"

    if [ -n "$${exclude_args}" ]; then
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} $${exclude_args}"
    fi

    # Set PBS fingerprint environment variable for certificate verification
    export PBS_FINGERPRINT

    log "Command: $${backup_cmd}"

    # Run backup
    local backup_exit_code=0
    eval "$${backup_cmd}" || backup_exit_code=$$?

    if [ "$${backup_exit_code}" -eq 0 ]; then
        local end_time=$(date +%s)
        local duration=$((end_time - start_time))

        log "✓ Backup completed successfully in $${duration}s"

        # Prune old backups
        log "Pruning old backups (keep $${RETENTION})..."
        proxmox-backup-client prune "host/$${backup_id}" \
            --repository "$PBS_REPOSITORY" \
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
            --ns "$PBS_NAMESPACE" \
%{ endif ~}
            --keep-last "$${RETENTION}"

        log "✓ Prune completed"

        # Cleanup temporary files
        cleanup_temp_files

        log "=== Backup Completed Successfully ==="
        return 0
    else
        log "✗ Backup failed with exit code: $${backup_exit_code}"

        send_alert "Backup Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "PBS backup failed for ${container_name} (exit code: $${backup_exit_code})" \
            "high"

        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Execution
# =============================================================================

main() {
    log "========================================"
    log "PBS Backup: ${container_name}"
    log "Container ID: ${container_id}"
    log "Namespace: ${namespace}"
    log "========================================"

    # Run pre-backup hooks
    if ! run_pre_backup_hooks; then
        log "Pre-backup hooks failed, aborting backup"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Run backup
    if ! run_backup; then
        log "Backup failed"
        exit 1
    fi

    log "All tasks completed successfully"
    exit 0
}

# Run main function
main

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# PBS Backup Script for ${container_name} (Container ${container_id})
# =============================================================================
# Generated by lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module
# Namespace: ${namespace}
# Schedule: ${schedule}
# Retention: ${retention} backups
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

CONTAINER_ID="${container_id}"
NAMESPACE="${namespace}"
RETENTION="${retention}"
LOG_FILE="/var/log/pbs-backups/$${NAMESPACE}.log"

# PBS repository from environment (set by systemd service)
# PBS_REPOSITORY, PBS_NAMESPACE, PBS_PASSWORD, PBS_FINGERPRINT

# Backup paths
INCLUDE_PATHS=(
%{ for path in include_paths ~}
  "${path}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

EXCLUDE_PATTERNS=(
%{ for pattern in exclude_paths ~}
  "${pattern}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

# Alert configuration
NTFY_URL="${ntfy_url}"
NTFY_PRIORITY="${ntfy_priority}"
NTFY_TAGS="${ntfy_tags}"

# =============================================================================
# Helper Functions
# =============================================================================

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*"
}

send_alert() {
    local title="$1"
    local message="$2"
    local priority="$${3:-$${NTFY_PRIORITY}}"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Title: $${title}" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${message}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# =============================================================================
# Pre-Backup Commands (Database Dumps, etc.)
# =============================================================================

run_pre_backup_hooks() {
    log "Running pre-backup hooks..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
%{ for cmd in pre_backup_commands ~}
    # ${cmd.name}
    log "  - ${cmd.name}"
    if timeout ${cmd.timeout} bash -c '${cmd.command}'; then
        log "    ✓ Success"
    else
        local hook_exit_code=$$?
        log "    ✗ Failed (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})"
        send_alert "Backup Hook Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "Pre-backup hook failed: ${cmd.name} (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})" \
            "high"
        return 1
    fi

%{ endfor ~}
%{ else ~}
    log "  (No pre-backup hooks configured)"
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Cleanup Functions
# =============================================================================

cleanup_temp_files() {
    log "Cleaning up temporary dump files..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
    # Remove database dumps after successful backup
    find /config -type f \( -name "*.sql.gz" -o -name "*.db.backup" \) -mmin +60 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Backup Function
# =============================================================================

run_backup() {
    local backup_id="lxc-$${CONTAINER_ID}"
    local backup_time=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
    local start_time=$(date +%s)

    log "=== Starting PBS Backup for ${container_name} ==="
    log "Repository: $${PBS_REPOSITORY}"
    log "Namespace: $${PBS_NAMESPACE}"
    log "Backup ID: $${backup_id}"
    log "Backup time: $${backup_time}"

    # Build exclude arguments
    local exclude_args=""
    for pattern in "$${EXCLUDE_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
        exclude_args="$${exclude_args} --exclude '$${pattern}'"
    done

    # Build backup command
    local backup_cmd="proxmox-backup-client backup"

    for path in "$${INCLUDE_PATHS[@]}"; do
        local archive_name=$(basename "$${path}")
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} '$${archive_name}.pxar:$${path}'"
    done

    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --repository \$PBS_REPOSITORY"
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"
%{ endif ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-id '$${backup_id}'"
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-time $(date +%s)"

    if [ -n "$${exclude_args}" ]; then
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} $${exclude_args}"
    fi

    # Set PBS fingerprint environment variable for certificate verification
    export PBS_FINGERPRINT

    log "Command: $${backup_cmd}"

    # Run backup
    local backup_exit_code=0
    eval "$${backup_cmd}" || backup_exit_code=$$?

    if [ "$${backup_exit_code}" -eq 0 ]; then
        local end_time=$(date +%s)
        local duration=$((end_time - start_time))

        log "✓ Backup completed successfully in $${duration}s"

        # Prune old backups
        log "Pruning old backups (keep $${RETENTION})..."
        proxmox-backup-client prune "host/$${backup_id}" \
            --repository "$PBS_REPOSITORY" \
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
            --ns "$PBS_NAMESPACE" \
%{ endif ~}
            --keep-last "$${RETENTION}"

        log "✓ Prune completed"

        # Cleanup temporary files
        cleanup_temp_files

        log "=== Backup Completed Successfully ==="
        return 0
    else
        log "✗ Backup failed with exit code: $${backup_exit_code}"

        send_alert "Backup Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "PBS backup failed for ${container_name} (exit code: $${backup_exit_code})" \
            "high"

        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Execution
# =============================================================================

main() {
    log "========================================"
    log "PBS Backup: ${container_name}"
    log "Container ID: ${container_id}"
    log "Namespace: ${namespace}"
    log "========================================"

    # Run pre-backup hooks
    if ! run_pre_backup_hooks; then
        log "Pre-backup hooks failed, aborting backup"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Run backup
    if ! run_backup; then
        log "Backup failed"
        exit 1
    fi

    log "All tasks completed successfully"
    exit 0
}

# Run main function
main

}"

    # Set priority based on status
    local priority="$${NTFY_PRIORITY}"
    if [ "$${status}" = "failure" ]; then
        priority="high"
    fi

    log "Sending notification: status=$${status}, size=$${backup_size}, duration=$${duration}s"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${json_payload}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}?template=pbs-backup" 2>/dev/null || true
}

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The conversation is summarized below:
Analysis:
Let me analyze this conversation chronologically:

1. **Initial Context Recovery**: The session started as a continuation of a previous conversation about Tailscale DNS resolution issues. The DNS mode toggle (home/travel) was already implemented and committed.

2. **User's First Request - Symlinked Files to Module**: The user wanted to convert symlinked files across the tofu registry into a shared/common module. They wanted to change from `local.op.<secret_name>` to something like `module.common.op.<secret_name>`.

3. **Exploration Phase**: I explored the 4 symlinked files (shared.tf, versions.tf, onepassword.tf, ip-registry.tf) used across 15 apps. Key findings:
   - All apps use the same 4 symlinks
   - Providers in versions.tf reference `local.op.*` from onepassword.tf
   - Provider configuration happens before module initialization - this is a fundamental constraint

4. **Implementation Attempt**: I created a `tofu/modules/config/` module with:
   - versions.tf (required providers)
   - variables.tf (dns_mode, ssh_public_key_path)
   - main.tf (placeholder)
   - onepassword.tf (1Password data sources)
   - ip-registry.tf (IP registry)
   - outputs.tf (all exports)

5. **Testing on Monitoring App**: Modified monitoring/main.tf to use `module.config.*`. Encountered duplicate 1Password queries issue - both symlinked file and module would query same data.

6. **User Feedback - "Moving just 1 file is unwise"**: User said if we can't remove most symlinks, it's not worth it. This led to abandoning the module approach.

7. **Terragrunt Discussion**: User asked about Terragrunt. I researched and explained how it could help but also noted drawbacks (another tool to learn, debugging complexity). User decided to drop it: "no its ok. as you said i dont want to add debugging complexity"

8. **Pivot to Backup Tasks**: User wanted to look at backup-related beads. Found two:
   - proxmox-homelab-984: Update PBS backup scripts to use ntfy pbs-backup template
   - proxmox-homelab-9gr: Remove vzdump backup after PBS validation

9. **User's Rationale for 984**: User explained they need notifications for every backup during this critical setup phase to track consistent backups. Can be disabled later once confident.

10. **Current Work - Implementing PBS Notifications**: I started implementing bead 984:
   - Added `notify_on_success` and `notify_on_failure` to variables.tf
   - Updated pbs-backup.sh.tftpl with new `send_backup_notification()` function
   - Modified run_backup() to capture output, parse backup size, and send notifications
   - Updated main.tf to pass new variables to template

Files modified:
- `tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/variables.tf` - Added notify_on_success, notify_on_failure
- `tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/pbs-backup.sh.tftpl` - Added JSON notification function, size parsing, success/failure notifications
- `tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/main.tf` - Added new variables to template rendering

The module creation was reverted after user feedback. Current work is on backup notifications.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Initial (Abandoned)**: Convert symlinked Terraform files (shared.tf, versions.tf, onepassword.tf, ip-registry.tf) into a shared module with exports like `module.config.op.<secret_name>`. User abandoned this when it became clear moving just 1 file wouldn't reduce complexity enough.
   - **Terragrunt (Declined)**: User asked about Terragrunt as an alternative. After research, user declined: "no its ok. as you said i dont want to add debugging complexity"
   - **Current (In Progress)**: Implement bead proxmox-homelab-984 - Update PBS backup scripts to send structured JSON notifications to ntfy using pbs-backup template. User wants visibility into all backups during this setup phase, with ability to disable later.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - OpenTofu/Terraform module limitations with providers (providers configured before module init)
   - Symlinked .tf files for DRY configuration across 15 apps
   - Terragrunt as alternative to symlinks (decided against)
   - PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) client configuration
   - ntfy notifications with JSON templates
   - Systemd timers for scheduled backups
   - Beads workflow for task tracking

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/variables.tf`** - Added notification toggle options
     ```hcl
     # Alert settings
     ntfy_url           = optional(string, "http://10.100.5.100:8080/homelab-alerts")
     ntfy_priority      = optional(string, "default")
     ntfy_tags          = optional(string, "backup")
     notify_on_success  = optional(bool, true)   # Send notification on successful backup
     notify_on_failure  = optional(bool, true)   # Send notification on failed backup (recommended: always true)
     ```

   - **`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/pbs-backup.sh.tftpl`** - Added JSON notification function and backup size parsing
     ```bash
     # Alert configuration
     NTFY_URL="${ntfy_url}"
     NTFY_PRIORITY="${ntfy_priority}"
     NTFY_TAGS="${ntfy_tags}"
     NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS="${notify_on_success}"
     NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE="${notify_on_failure}"
     
     # Send structured JSON notification using ntfy pbs-backup template
     send_backup_notification() {
         local status="$1"
         local duration="${2:-0}"
         local backup_size="${3:-unknown}"
         local error_msg="${4:-}"

         # Check if notification should be sent based on status
         if [ "${status}" = "success" ] && [ "${NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS}" != "true" ]; then
             log "Success notification disabled, skipping"
             return 0
         fi
         if [ "${status}" = "failure" ] && [ "${NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE}" != "true" ]; then
             log "Failure notification disabled, skipping"
             return 0
         fi

         # Build JSON payload
         local json_payload="{
       \"status\": \"${status}\",
       \"container_name\": \"${container_name}\",
       \"container_id\": \"${container_id}\",
       \"namespace\": \"${NAMESPACE}\",
       \"duration\": ${duration},
       \"backup_size\": \"${backup_size}\",
       \"retention\": ${RETENTION},
       \"timestamp\": \"$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')\"${error_field}
     }"

         curl -sf \
             -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
             -H "Priority: ${priority}" \
             -H "Tags: ${NTFY_TAGS}" \
             -d "${json_payload}" \
             "${NTFY_URL}?template=pbs-backup" 2>/dev/null || true
     }
     ```
     Also modified `run_backup()` to capture output, parse backup size, and call `send_backup_notification()` for both success and failure.

   - **`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/main.tf`** - Added new variables to template rendering
     ```hcl
     backup_script       = templatefile("${path.module}/templates/pbs-backup.sh.tftpl", {
       # ... existing variables ...
       notify_on_success   = var.backup.notify_on_success
       notify_on_failure   = var.backup.notify_on_failure
     })
     ```

   - **`tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/ntfy/templates/pbs-backup.yml`** - Existing ntfy template (read-only, already exists)
     - Expected JSON payload format for structured backup notifications

4. Errors and Fixes:
   - **Module approach caused duplicate 1Password queries**: Both symlinked onepassword.tf and module would query same items, doubling API calls
   - **Provider configuration constraint**: Providers need secrets at init time, before modules are available - fundamental Terraform limitation
   - **User feedback**: "moving just 1 file out of 4 is unwise" - led to abandoning module approach entirely

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Solved**: Determined symlink approach is actually optimal for this use case (single source of truth, no duplicate queries, provider access)
   - **In Progress**: Implementing structured JSON notifications for PBS backups with toggleable success/failure alerts

# =============================================================================
# IP Address Registry
# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.
# This file serves as the single source of truth for IP assignments.
#
# Network Architecture:
#   - 192.168.1.0/24 (vmbr0): Home LAN - FIOS router, external access
#   - 10.100.0.0/16  (vmbr1): Container network - internal services
#
# IP Scheme (Container ID aligned with IP):
#   - 10.100.1.x:  Core services (LXC 100-149)
#   - 10.100.2.x:  Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249)
#   - 10.100.3.x:  Media - Photos (LXC 300-349)
#   - 10.100.4.x:  Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449)
#   - 10.100.5.x:  Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549)
#
# Dual-NIC Services (need 192.168.1.x for LAN compatibility):
#   - Traefik: Reverse proxy for LAN clients
#   - AdGuard: DNS for LAN devices
#   - Jellyfin: DLNA/casting
#   - Immich: Mobile app sync
# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  network = {
    # Home LAN (vmbr0)
    lan_gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    lan_netmask = "/24"
    lan_prefix  = "192.168.1"

    # Container network (vmbr1)
    container_gateway = "10.100.0.1"
    container_netmask = "/16"
    container_prefix  = "10.100"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - Container Network (10.100.x.x)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Pattern: 10.100.<category>.<container_id_suffix>
  # Example: LXC 304 -> 10.100.3.104 (category 3, suffix 04)

  ip_registry = {
    # Infrastructure (192.168.1.x only - not containers)
    infrastructure = {
      router  = "192.168.1.1"    # Verizon FIOS router
      proxmox = "192.168.1.215"  # Proxmox VE host (vmbr0)
      # Proxmox also has 10.100.0.1 on vmbr1 (gateway for containers)
    }

    # Core services (LXC 100-149) -> 10.100.1.x
    core = {
      network_services = "10.100.1.101"  # LXC 101 - AdGuard DNS + Tailscale
      pbs              = "10.100.1.102"  # LXC 102 - Proxmox Backup Server
      # 103 reserved for monitoring migration from 500
      container_mgmt   = "10.100.1.104"  # LXC 104 - Pulse + Arcane
    }

    # Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249) -> 10.100.2.x
    dashboards = {
      traefik    = "10.100.2.200"  # LXC 200 - Reverse proxy
      dashboards = "10.100.2.201"  # LXC 201 - Homepage + Dashy
      authelia   = "10.100.2.202"  # LXC 202 - SSO/Auth (deprecated - migrating to authentik)
      authentik  = "10.100.2.203"  # LXC 203 - Identity Provider (replaces Authelia)
    }

    # Media - Photos (LXC 300-349) -> 10.100.3.x
    photos = {
      immich_importer = "10.100.3.103"  # LXC 303 - Photo import
      immich          = "10.100.3.104"  # LXC 304 - Photo management
    }

    # Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449) -> 10.100.4.x
    media = {
      jellyfin         = "10.100.4.101"  # LXC 401 - Media server + Jellystat
      media_management = "10.100.4.102"  # LXC 402 - Arr stack
    }

    # Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549) -> 10.100.5.x
    monitoring = {
      monitoring    = "10.100.5.100"  # LXC 500 - Prometheus, Grafana, etc
      openwebui     = "10.100.5.101"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
      n8n           = "10.100.5.102"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
      obsidian_sync = "10.100.5.103"  # LXC 503 - Obsidian LiveSync (CouchDB)
      documents     = "10.100.5.104"  # LXC 504 - Paperless-ngx + Stirling-PDF
    }
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # LAN IPs for Dual-NIC Services (192.168.1.x)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # These services need direct LAN access for compatibility with home devices

  lan_ips = {
    traefik          = "192.168.1.235"  # LXC 200 - LAN clients access services
    authelia         = "192.168.1.225"  # LXC 202 - SSO/Auth
    dashboards       = "192.168.1.234"  # LXC 201 - Homepage + Dashy
    network_services = "192.168.1.196"  # LXC 101 - DNS for LAN devices
    jellyfin         = "192.168.1.226"  # LXC 401 - DLNA/casting
    immich           = "192.168.1.222"  # LXC 304 - Mobile app sync
    immich_importer  = "192.168.1.223"  # LXC 303 - Photo import
    monitoring       = "192.168.1.229"  # LXC 500 - Monitoring stack
    openwebui        = "192.168.1.221"  # LXC 501 - AI chat
    n8n              = "192.168.1.213"  # LXC 502 - Workflow automation
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Container ID to IP Mapping
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  container_ips = {
    # Core (100-149)
    101 = local.ip_registry.core.network_services
    102 = local.ip_registry.core.pbs
    104 = local.ip_registry.core.container_mgmt

    # Dashboards & Auth (200-249)
    200 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik
    201 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.dashboards
    202 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.authelia
    203 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.authentik

    # Photos (300-349)
    303 = local.ip_registry.photos.immich_importer
    304 = local.ip_registry.photos.immich

    # Media (400-449)
    401 = local.ip_registry.media.jellyfin
    402 = local.ip_registry.media.media_management

    # Monitoring & AI (500-549)
    500 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring
    501 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui
    502 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n
    503 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.obsidian_sync
    504 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.documents
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: Get IP with CIDR notation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in merge(
      local.ip_registry.core,
      local.ip_registry.dashboards,
      local.ip_registry.photos,
      local.ip_registry.media,
      local.ip_registry.monitoring,
    ) : name => "${ip}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  }

  lan_ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in local.lan_ips : name => "${ip}${local.network.lan_netmask}"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Convenience: Traefik IP for route modules
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Used by traefik-route modules to sync config to Traefik LXC via SSH
  # Must use LAN IP since container network isn't routable from local machine
  traefik_ip = local.lan_ips.traefik

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for validation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_container_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.dashboards),
    values(local.ip_registry.photos),
    values(local.ip_registry.media),
    values(local.ip_registry.monitoring),
  )

  _all_lan_ips = values(local.lan_ips)
}

# =============================================================================
# Outputs for CLI Usage
# =============================================================================

output "container_ips" {
  description = "All container IPs (10.100.x.x)"
  value       = local._all_container_ips
}

output "lan_ips" {
  description = "LAN IPs for dual-NIC services (192.168.1.x)"
  value       = local.lan_ips
}

output "ip_registry" {
  description = "Full IP registry organized by category"
  value       = local.ip_registry
}

output "network" {
  description = "Network configuration"
  value       = local.network
}

The issue is that the `proxmox_endpoint` and `proxmox_ssh_host` variables in `shared.tf` are hardcoded to the LAN IP. These need to use the dns_mode toggle.

# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.

#   - 192.168.1.0/24 (vmbr0): Home LAN - FIOS router, external access
#   - 10.100.0.0/16  (vmbr1): Container network - internal services

#   - 10.100.2.x:  Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249)
#   - 10.100.3.x:  Media - Photos (LXC 300-349)
#   - 10.100.4.x:  Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449)

#   - Traefik: Reverse proxy for LAN clients
#   - AdGuard: DNS for LAN devices
#   - Jellyfin: DLNA/casting
#   - Immich: Mobile app sync

    lan_netmask = "/24"

  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Container ID to IP Mapping
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  container_ips = {
    # Core (100-149)
    101 = local.ip_registry.core.network_services
    102 = local.ip_registry.core.pbs
    104 = local.ip_registry.core.container_mgmt

    # Dashboards & Auth (200-249)
    200 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik
    201 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.dashboards
    202 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.authelia
    203 = local.ip_registry.dashboards.authentik

    # Photos (300-349)
    303 = local.ip_registry.photos.immich_importer
    304 = local.ip_registry.photos.immich

    # Media (400-449)
    401 = local.ip_registry.media.jellyfin
    402 = local.ip_registry.media.media_management

    # Monitoring & AI (500-549)
    500 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring
    501 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui
    502 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n
    503 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.obsidian_sync
    504 = local.ip_registry.monitoring.documents
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: Get IP with CIDR notation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in merge(
      local.ip_registry.core,
      local.ip_registry.dashboards,
      local.ip_registry.photos,
      local.ip_registry.media,
      local.ip_registry.monitoring,
    ) : name => "${ip}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  }

  lan_ip_cidr = {
    for name, ip in local.lan_ips : name => "${ip}${local.network.lan_netmask}"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Convenience: Traefik IP for route modules
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Used by traefik-route modules to sync config to Traefik LXC via SSH
  # Must use LAN IP since container network isn't routable from local machine
  traefik_ip = local.lan_ips.traefik

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Flatten all allocated IPs for validation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  _all_container_ips = concat(
    values(local.ip_registry.core),
    values(local.ip_registry.dashboards),
    values(local.ip_registry.photos),
    values(local.ip_registry.media),
    values(local.ip_registry.monitoring),
  )

  _all_lan_ips = values(local.lan_ips)
}

# =============================================================================
# Outputs for CLI Usage
# =============================================================================

output "container_ips" {
  description = "All container IPs (10.100.x.x)"
  value       = local._all_container_ips
}

output "lan_ips" {
  description = "LAN IPs for dual-NIC services (192.168.1.x)"
  value       = local.lan_ips
}

output "ip_registry" {
  description = "Full IP registry organized by category"
  value       = local.ip_registry
}

output "network" {
  description = "Network configuration"
  value       = local.network
}

# Homelab Infrastructure Automation
# https://taskfile.dev

version: '3'

vars:
  PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.TASKFILE_DIR}}"
  TOFU_DIR: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/tofu"

env:
  # State encryption passphrase - MUST be TF_VAR because encryption runs before providers
  # All other secrets are now fetched via 1Password provider directly in OpenTofu
  TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase:
    sh: |
      if [ -n "$TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase" ]; then
        echo "$TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase"
      else
        op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password" 2>/dev/null || echo ""
      fi
  # SOPS age key for decrypting secrets (used by sops provider in OpenTofu)
  SOPS_AGE_KEY:
    sh: op read "op://homelab/sops-age-key/private_key" 2>/dev/null || echo ""

# =============================================================================
# Included Taskfiles (flattened into main namespace)
# =============================================================================
includes:
  tofu:
    taskfile: ./tasks/tofu.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  backup:
    taskfile: ./tasks/backup.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  cloud:
    taskfile: ./tasks/cloud.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  template:
    taskfile: ./tasks/template.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  pbs:
    taskfile: ./tasks/pbs.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  importer:
    taskfile: ./tasks/immich-importer.yml
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  beads:
    taskfile: ./tasks/beads.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"

tasks:
  # ===========================================================================
  # Desktop LXC (Temporary GUI for Downloads)
  # ===========================================================================

  desktop:create:
    desc: "Create temporary GUI desktop LXC for downloading Google Takeout"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/desktop-lxc/create.sh

  desktop:destroy:
    desc: "Destroy temporary GUI desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/desktop-lxc/destroy.sh

  desktop:info:
    desc: "Show VNC connection info for desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - |
        IP=$(ssh root@homelab "pct exec 600 -- ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep inet | awk '{print \$2}' | cut -d/ -f1" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -z "$IP" ]; then
          echo "Desktop LXC (600) is not running or does not exist."
          echo "Run 'task desktop:create' first."
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "=== Desktop LXC VNC Connection ==="
        echo ""
        echo "VNC Host: $IP:5901"
        echo ""
        echo "macOS: Open Finder, Cmd+K, enter vnc://$IP:5901"
        echo ""
        echo "Downloads save to: /downloads (mounted to /tank/photo-import)"

  desktop:restart-vnc:
    desc: "Restart VNC server on desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - |
        echo "Restarting VNC server..."
        ssh root@homelab "pct exec 600 -- bash -c 'vncserver -kill :1 2>/dev/null || true; vncserver :1 -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24 -localhost no'"
        echo "VNC server restarted on display :1"

  # ===========================================================================
  # AdGuard DNS Operations
  # ===========================================================================

  adguard:test:
    desc: "Test DNS resolution for homelab domains"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/sync/adguard-sync.sh test

  # ===========================================================================
  # Cleanup & Maintenance
  # ===========================================================================

  cleanup:
    desc: "Clean up temporary files, backups, and cruft (dry run)"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/cleanup.sh

  cleanup:run:
    desc: "Clean up temporary files, backups, and cruft (actually delete)"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/cleanup.sh --run

  # ===========================================================================
  # Local Development
  # ===========================================================================

  dev:dashboards:up:
    desc: "Start Homepage and Dashy locally for testing configs"
    dir: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/dev/dashboards"
    cmds:
      - docker compose up -d
      - |
        echo ""
        echo "=== Dashboard Dev Environment ==="
        echo ""
        echo "Homepage: http://localhost:3000"
        echo "Dashy:    http://localhost:4001"
        echo ""
        echo "Config files are mounted from tofu/apps/dashboards/deploy/"
        echo "Edit configs and refresh browser to see changes."
        echo "(Dashy may need container restart for config changes)"
        echo ""
        echo "Stop with: task dev:dashboards:down"

  dev:dashboards:down:
    desc: "Stop local dashboard dev environment"
    dir: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/dev/dashboards"
    cmds:
      - docker compose down

  dev:dashboards:logs:
    desc: "View logs from local dashboard containers"
    dir: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/dev/dashboards"
    cmds:
      - docker compose logs -f {{.SERVICE}}
    vars:
      SERVICE: '{{.SERVICE | default ""}}'

  dev:dashboards:restart:
    desc: "Restart local dashboard containers (useful after config changes)"
    dir: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/dev/dashboards"
    cmds:
      - docker compose restart {{.SERVICE}}
      - echo "Restarted. Dashy takes ~40s to fully start."
    vars:
      SERVICE: '{{.SERVICE | default ""}}'

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# PBS Backup Script for n8n (Container 502)
# =============================================================================
# Generated by lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module
# Namespace: lxc-502
# Schedule: daily
# Retention: 7 backups
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

CONTAINER_ID="502"
NAMESPACE="lxc-502"
RETENTION="7"
LOG_FILE="/var/log/pbs-backups/${NAMESPACE}.log"

# PBS repository from environment (set by systemd service)
# PBS_REPOSITORY, PBS_NAMESPACE, PBS_PASSWORD, PBS_FINGERPRINT

# Backup paths
INCLUDE_PATHS=(
  "/config"
  "/var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data"
)

EXCLUDE_PATTERNS=(
  "/var/lib/docker/overlay2"
)

# Alert configuration
NTFY_URL="http://10.100.5.100:8080/homelab-alerts"
NTFY_PRIORITY="default"
NTFY_TAGS="backup,n8n"
NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS="true"
NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE="true"

# =============================================================================
# Helper Functions
# =============================================================================

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*"
}

# Legacy alert function (simple text) - kept for pre-backup hook failures
send_alert() {
    local title="$1"
    local message="$2"
    local priority="${3:-${NTFY_PRIORITY}}"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Title: ${title}" \
        -H "Priority: ${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: ${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "${message}" \
        "${NTFY_URL}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Send structured JSON notification using ntfy pbs-backup template
send_backup_notification() {
    local status="$1"
    local duration="${2:-0}"
    local backup_size="${3:-unknown}"
    local error_msg="${4:-}"

    # Check if notification should be sent based on status
    if [ "${status}" = "success" ] && [ "${NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Success notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${status}" = "failure" ] && [ "${NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Failure notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0
    fi

---
# =============================================================================
# Configure PBS Backup Client in LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# This playbook is generated by the lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module.
# It configures proxmox-backup-client for zero-downtime incremental backups.
# =============================================================================

- name: Configure PBS backup for ${container_name}
  hosts: ${container_name}
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    container_id: ${container_id}
    namespace: ${namespace}
    schedule: ${schedule}
    retention: ${retention}
    pbs_server: ${pbs_server}
    pbs_datastore: ${pbs_datastore}
    pbs_user: ${pbs_user}
    pbs_password_cmd: ${pbs_password_cmd}
    pbs_repository: ${pbs_user}@${pbs_server}:${pbs_datastore}

    backup_script_dir: /usr/local/bin/pbs-backup
    backup_script_path: /usr/local/bin/pbs-backup/backup-${container_id}.sh
    log_dir: /var/log/pbs-backups
    log_file: /var/log/pbs-backups/${namespace}.log

    systemd_service_name: pbs-backup-${container_id}.service
    systemd_timer_name: pbs-backup-${container_id}.timer

    ntfy_url: ${ntfy_url}
    ntfy_priority: ${ntfy_priority}
    ntfy_tags: ${ntfy_tags}

  tasks:
    # =========================================================================
    # Install proxmox-backup-client
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Check if proxmox-backup-client is already installed
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: which proxmox-backup-client
      register: pbs_client_check
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Install proxmox-backup-client dependencies
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name:
          - curl
          - ca-certificates
        state: present
        update_cache: true
      when: pbs_client_check.rc != 0

    - name: Download proxmox-backup-client binary
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: https://cloud-pbs.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/proxmox-backup-client
        dest: /usr/local/bin/proxmox-backup-client
        mode: '0755'
        checksum: sha256:85b477e2f17b86947f332cfe71ccfc365e1c9821a7a748899b13fcffbcd0c8f9
      when: pbs_client_check.rc != 0

    - name: Verify proxmox-backup-client installation
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: proxmox-backup-client version
      register: pbs_version_check
      changed_when: false

    - name: Display proxmox-backup-client version
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "{{ pbs_version_check.stdout }}"

    # =========================================================================
    # Configure PBS Password
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create PBS encryption key directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /root/.config/proxmox-backup
        state: directory
        mode: '0700'

    - name: Get PBS certificate fingerprint
      ansible.builtin.shell:
        cmd: |
          ssh root@{{ pbs_server }} "proxmox-backup-manager cert info" | \
          grep "Fingerprint (sha256):" | \
          awk '{print $NF}'
      register: pbs_fingerprint
      changed_when: false
      delegate_to: localhost

    - name: Get PBS password from 1Password
      ansible.builtin.shell:
        cmd: ${pbs_password_cmd}
      register: pbs_password
      changed_when: false
      delegate_to: localhost
      no_log: true

    - name: Store PBS password and fingerprint in environment file
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          PBS_REPOSITORY={{ pbs_repository }}
          PBS_NAMESPACE={{ namespace }}
          PBS_PASSWORD={{ pbs_password.stdout }}
          PBS_FINGERPRINT={{ pbs_fingerprint.stdout }}
        dest: /root/.pbs-backup-env
        mode: '0600'
      no_log: true

    # =========================================================================
    # Create PBS Namespace (if specified and doesn't exist)
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create PBS namespace
      ansible.builtin.shell:
        cmd: |
          set -a
          source /root/.pbs-backup-env
          set +a
          proxmox-backup-client namespace create {{ namespace }} --repository {{ pbs_repository }}
        executable: /bin/bash
      register: namespace_create
      changed_when: "'created namespace' in namespace_create.stdout or namespace_create.rc == 0"
      failed_when: false
      no_log: true
      when: namespace != ""

    # =========================================================================
    # Create Backup Script
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create backup script directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ backup_script_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Create log directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ log_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Deploy backup script
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          ${indent(10, backup_script)}
        dest: "{{ backup_script_path }}"
        mode: '0755'

    # =========================================================================
    # Create Systemd Service & Timer
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create systemd service
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          [Unit]
          Description=PBS Backup for ${container_name} (${namespace})
          After=network-online.target
          Wants=network-online.target

          [Service]
          Type=oneshot
          EnvironmentFile=/root/.pbs-backup-env
          ExecStart={{ backup_script_path }}
          StandardOutput=append:{{ log_file }}
          StandardError=append:{{ log_file }}

          # Resource limits
          CPUQuota=50%
          MemoryMax=1G

          [Install]
          WantedBy=multi-user.target
        dest: /etc/systemd/system/{{ systemd_service_name }}
        mode: '0644'
      register: service_file

    - name: Determine systemd timer schedule
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        timer_oncalendar: |-
          {%- if schedule == "daily" -%}
          daily
          {%- elif schedule | regex_search('^[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$') -%}
          *-*-* {{ schedule }}
          {%- else -%}
          {{ schedule }}
          {%- endif -%}

    - name: Create systemd timer
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          [Unit]
          Description=Timer for PBS Backup of ${container_name}

          [Timer]
          OnCalendar={{ timer_oncalendar }}
          Persistent=true
          RandomizedDelaySec=5min

          [Install]
          WantedBy=timers.target
        dest: /etc/systemd/system/{{ systemd_timer_name }}
        mode: '0644'
      register: timer_file

    - name: Reload systemd daemon
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        daemon_reload: true
      when: service_file is changed or timer_file is changed

    - name: Enable and start timer
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        name: "{{ systemd_timer_name }}"
        enabled: true
        state: started

    # =========================================================================
    # Verify Configuration
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Check timer status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: systemctl status {{ systemd_timer_name }}
      register: timer_status
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Display configuration summary
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "=== PBS Backup Configured for ${container_name} ==="
          - ""
          - "Container ID: ${container_id}"
          - "Namespace: ${namespace}"
          - "Schedule: {{ timer_oncalendar }}"
          - "Repository: {{ pbs_repository }}"
          - "Log file: {{ log_file }}"
          - ""
          - "Manual trigger:"
          - "  systemctl start {{ systemd_service_name }}"
          - ""
          - "Check timer:"
          - "  systemctl list-timers {{ systemd_timer_name }}"
          - ""
          - "View logs:"
          - "  tail -f {{ log_file }}"

Interesting! `$${var}` becomes `${var}` but `$$(cmd)` stays as `$$(cmd)`. The `$$` escaping only works before `{` not before `(`. 

For command substitution `$(...)` in bash, we need a different approach. In Terraform templatefile, `$` followed by anything other than `{` is passed through literally. So `$$(` stays as `$$(`.

The solution is to use `$${` for variables but for command substitution we just use `$(` directly - no escaping needed since it's not followed by `{`.
