#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# PBS Backup Script for ${container_name} (Container ${container_id})
# =============================================================================
# Generated by lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module
# Namespace: ${namespace}
# Schedule: ${schedule}
# Retention: ${retention} backups
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

CONTAINER_ID="${container_id}"
NAMESPACE="${namespace}"
RETENTION="${retention}"
LOG_FILE="/var/log/pbs-backups/$${NAMESPACE}.log"

# PBS repository from environment (set by systemd service)
# PBS_REPOSITORY, PBS_NAMESPACE, PBS_PASSWORD, PBS_FINGERPRINT

# Backup paths
INCLUDE_PATHS=(
%{ for path in include_paths ~}
  "${path}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

EXCLUDE_PATTERNS=(
%{ for pattern in exclude_paths ~}
  "${pattern}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

# Alert configuration
NTFY_URL="${ntfy_url}"
NTFY_PRIORITY="${ntfy_priority}"
NTFY_TAGS="${ntfy_tags}"
NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS="${notify_on_success}"
NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE="${notify_on_failure}"

# =============================================================================
# Helper Functions
# =============================================================================

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*"
}

# Legacy alert function (simple text) - kept for pre-backup hook failures
send_alert() {
    local title="$1"
    local message="$2"
    local priority="$${3:-$${NTFY_PRIORITY}}"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Title: $${title}" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${message}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Send structured JSON notification using ntfy pbs-backup template
send_backup_notification() {
    local status="$1"
    local duration="$${2:-0}"
    local backup_size="$${3:-unknown}"
    local error_msg="$${4:-}"

    # Check if notification should be sent based on status
    if [ "$${status}" = "success" ] && [ "$${NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Success notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "$${status}" = "failure" ] && [ "$${NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Failure notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0
    fi

    # Escape error message for JSON (replace quotes and newlines)
    if [ -n "$${error_msg}" ]; then
        error_msg=$$(echo "$${error_msg}" | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | tr '\n' ' ')
    fi

    # Build JSON payload
    local error_field=""
    if [ -n "$${error_msg}" ]; then
        error_field=",
  \"error_message\": \"$${error_msg}\""
    fi

    local json_payload="{
  \"status\": \"$${status}\",
  \"container_name\": \"${container_name}\",
  \"container_id\": \"${container_id}\",
  \"namespace\": \"$${NAMESPACE}\",
  \"duration\": $${duration},
  \"backup_size\": \"$${backup_size}\",
  \"retention\": $${RETENTION},
  \"timestamp\": \"$$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')\"$${error_field}
}"

    # Set priority based on status
    local priority="$${NTFY_PRIORITY}"
    if [ "$${status}" = "failure" ]; then
        priority="high"
    fi

    log "Sending notification: status=$${status}, size=$${backup_size}, duration=$${duration}s"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${json_payload}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}?template=pbs-backup" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# =============================================================================
# Pre-Backup Commands (Database Dumps, etc.)
# =============================================================================

run_pre_backup_hooks() {
    log "Running pre-backup hooks..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
%{ for cmd in pre_backup_commands ~}
    # ${cmd.name}
    log "  - ${cmd.name}"
    if timeout ${cmd.timeout} bash -c '${cmd.command}'; then
        log "    ✓ Success"
    else
        local hook_exit_code=$$?
        log "    ✗ Failed (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})"
        send_alert "Backup Hook Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "Pre-backup hook failed: ${cmd.name} (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})" \
            "high"
        return 1
    fi

%{ endfor ~}
%{ else ~}
    log "  (No pre-backup hooks configured)"
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Cleanup Functions
# =============================================================================

cleanup_temp_files() {
    log "Cleaning up temporary dump files..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
    # Remove database dumps after successful backup
    find /config -type f \( -name "*.sql.gz" -o -name "*.db.backup" \) -mmin +60 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Backup Function
# =============================================================================

run_backup() {
    local backup_id="lxc-$${CONTAINER_ID}"
    local backup_time=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
    local start_time=$(date +%s)

    log "=== Starting PBS Backup for ${container_name} ==="
    log "Repository: $${PBS_REPOSITORY}"
    log "Namespace: $${PBS_NAMESPACE}"
    log "Backup ID: $${backup_id}"
    log "Backup time: $${backup_time}"

    # Build exclude arguments
    local exclude_args=""
    for pattern in "$${EXCLUDE_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
        exclude_args="$${exclude_args} --exclude '$${pattern}'"
    done

    # Build backup command
    local backup_cmd="proxmox-backup-client backup"

    for path in "$${INCLUDE_PATHS[@]}"; do
        local archive_name=$(basename "$${path}")
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} '$${archive_name}.pxar:$${path}'"
    done

    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --repository \$PBS_REPOSITORY"
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"
%{ endif ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-id '$${backup_id}'"
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-time $(date +%s)"

    if [ -n "$${exclude_args}" ]; then
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} $${exclude_args}"
    fi

    # Set PBS fingerprint environment variable for certificate verification
    export PBS_FINGERPRINT

    log "Command: $${backup_cmd}"

    # Run backup and capture output for size parsing
    local backup_exit_code=0
    local backup_output=""
    backup_output=$$(eval "$${backup_cmd}" 2>&1) || backup_exit_code=$$?

    local end_time=$(date +%s)
    local duration=$((end_time - start_time))

    # Parse backup size from output (looks for "Uploaded: X.XX MiB" or "GiB")
    local backup_size="unknown"
    if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then
        # Try to extract uploaded size from PBS output
        backup_size=$$(echo "$${backup_output}" | grep -oP 'Uploaded:\s*\K[0-9.]+\s*[GMK]iB' | tail -1 || echo "unknown")
        if [ -z "$${backup_size}" ] || [ "$${backup_size}" = "unknown" ]; then
            # Fallback: try to get total size
            backup_size=$$(echo "$${backup_output}" | grep -oP 'total\s+\K[0-9.]+\s*[GMK]iB' | tail -1 || echo "unknown")
        fi
    fi

    # Log the backup output
    echo "$${backup_output}" | while IFS= read -r line; do
        log "  $${line}"
    done

    if [ "$${backup_exit_code}" -eq 0 ]; then
        log "✓ Backup completed successfully in $${duration}s (size: $${backup_size})"

        # Prune old backups
        log "Pruning old backups (keep $${RETENTION})..."
        proxmox-backup-client prune "host/$${backup_id}" \
            --repository "$PBS_REPOSITORY" \
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
            --ns "$PBS_NAMESPACE" \
%{ endif ~}
            --keep-last "$${RETENTION}"

        log "✓ Prune completed"

        # Cleanup temporary files
        cleanup_temp_files

        # Send success notification
        send_backup_notification "success" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}"

        log "=== Backup Completed Successfully ==="
        return 0
    else
        log "✗ Backup failed with exit code: $${backup_exit_code}"

        # Capture error message (last few lines of output)
        local error_msg=""
        if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then
            error_msg=$$(echo "$${backup_output}" | tail -5)
        fi

        # Send failure notification
        send_backup_notification "failure" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}" "Exit code: $${backup_exit_code}. $${error_msg}"

        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Execution
# =============================================================================

main() {
    log "========================================"
    log "PBS Backup: ${container_name}"
    log "Container ID: ${container_id}"
    log "Namespace: ${namespace}"
    log "========================================"

    # Run pre-backup hooks
    if ! run_pre_backup_hooks; then
        log "Pre-backup hooks failed, aborting backup"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Run backup
    if ! run_backup; then
        log "Backup failed"
        exit 1
    fi

    log "All tasks completed successfully"
    exit 0
}

# Run main function
main

        return 0
    else
        log "✗ Backup failed with exit code: $${backup_exit_code}"

        # Capture error message (last few lines of output)
        local error_msg=""
        if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then
            error_msg=$$(echo "$${backup_output}" | tail -5)
        fi

main() {

NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE="${notify_on_failure}"

send_backup_notification() {
    local status="$1"
    local duration="$${2:-0}"
    local backup_size="$${3:-unknown}"
    local error_msg="$${4:-}"

    if [ "$${status}" = "success" ] && [ "$${NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Success notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0

    if [ "$${status}" = "failure" ] && [ "$${NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE}" != "true" ]; then

%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"
%{ endif ~}

        cleanup_temp_files

        return 0
    else

        # Capture error message (last few lines of output)
        local error_msg=""
        if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then

        fi

        send_backup_notification "failure" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}" "Exit code: $${backup_exit_code}. $${error_msg}"

        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Execution
# =============================================================================

}

# Send structured JSON notification using ntfy pbs-backup template
send_backup_notification() {
    local status="$1"
    local duration="$${2:-0}"
    local backup_size="$${3:-unknown}"
    local error_msg="$${4:-}"

    # Check if notification should be sent based on status
    if [ "$${status}" = "success" ] && [ "$${NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Success notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "$${status}" = "failure" ] && [ "$${NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Failure notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0
    fi

    # Escape error message for JSON (replace quotes and newlines)
    if [ -n "$${error_msg}" ]; then
        error_msg=$(echo "$${error_msg}" | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | tr '\n' ' ')
    fi

    # Build JSON payload
    local error_field=""
    if [ -n "$${error_msg}" ]; then
        error_field=",
  \"error_message\": \"$${error_msg}\""
    fi

    local json_payload="{
  \"status\": \"$${status}\",
  \"container_name\": \"${container_name}\",
  \"container_id\": \"${container_id}\",
  \"namespace\": \"$${NAMESPACE}\",
  \"duration\": $${duration},
  \"backup_size\": \"$${backup_size}\",
  \"retention\": $${RETENTION},
  \"timestamp\": \"$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')\"$${error_field}
}"

    # Set priority based on status
    local priority="$${NTFY_PRIORITY}"
    if [ "$${status}" = "failure" ]; then
        priority="high"
    fi

    log "Sending notification: status=$${status}, size=$${backup_size}, duration=$${duration}s"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${json_payload}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}?template=pbs-backup" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# =============================================================================
# Pre-Backup Commands (Database Dumps, etc.)
# =============================================================================

run_pre_backup_hooks() {
    log "Running pre-backup hooks..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
%{ for cmd in pre_backup_commands ~}
    # ${cmd.name}
    log "  - ${cmd.name}"
    if timeout ${cmd.timeout} bash -c '${cmd.command}'; then
        log "    ✓ Success"
    else
        local hook_exit_code=$$?
        log "    ✗ Failed (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})"
        send_alert "Backup Hook Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "Pre-backup hook failed: ${cmd.name} (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})" \
            "high"
        return 1
    fi

%{ endfor ~}
%{ else ~}
    log "  (No pre-backup hooks configured)"
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Cleanup Functions
# =============================================================================

cleanup_temp_files() {
    log "Cleaning up temporary dump files..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
    # Remove database dumps after successful backup
    find /config -type f \( -name "*.sql.gz" -o -name "*.db.backup" \) -mmin +60 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Backup Function
# =============================================================================

run_backup() {
    local backup_id="lxc-$${CONTAINER_ID}"
    local backup_time=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
    local start_time=$(date +%s)

    log "=== Starting PBS Backup for ${container_name} ==="
    log "Repository: $${PBS_REPOSITORY}"
    log "Namespace: $${PBS_NAMESPACE}"
    log "Backup ID: $${backup_id}"
    log "Backup time: $${backup_time}"

    # Build exclude arguments
    local exclude_args=""
    for pattern in "$${EXCLUDE_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
        exclude_args="$${exclude_args} --exclude '$${pattern}'"
    done

    # Build backup command
    local backup_cmd="proxmox-backup-client backup"

    for path in "$${INCLUDE_PATHS[@]}"; do
        local archive_name=$(basename "$${path}")
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} '$${archive_name}.pxar:$${path}'"
    done

    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --repository \$PBS_REPOSITORY"
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"
%{ endif ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-id '$${backup_id}'"
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-time $(date +%s)"

    if [ -n "$${exclude_args}" ]; then
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} $${exclude_args}"
    fi

    # Set PBS fingerprint environment variable for certificate verification
    export PBS_FINGERPRINT

    log "Command: $${backup_cmd}"

    # Run backup and capture output for size parsing
    local backup_exit_code=0
    local backup_output=""
    backup_output=$(eval "$${backup_cmd}" 2>&1) || backup_exit_code=$?

    local end_time=$(date +%s)
    local duration=$((end_time - start_time))

    # Parse backup size from output (looks for "Uploaded: X.XX MiB" or "GiB")
    local backup_size="unknown"
    if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then
        # Try to extract uploaded size from PBS output
        backup_size=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | grep -oP 'Uploaded:\s*\K[0-9.]+\s*[GMK]iB' | tail -1 || echo "unknown")
        if [ -z "$${backup_size}" ] || [ "$${backup_size}" = "unknown" ]; then
            # Fallback: try to get total size
            backup_size=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | grep -oP 'total\s+\K[0-9.]+\s*[GMK]iB' | tail -1 || echo "unknown")
        fi
    fi

    # Log the backup output
    echo "$${backup_output}" | while IFS= read -r line; do
        log "  $${line}"
    done

    if [ "$${backup_exit_code}" -eq 0 ]; then
        log "✓ Backup completed successfully in $${duration}s (size: $${backup_size})"

        # Prune old backups
        log "Pruning old backups (keep $${RETENTION})..."
        proxmox-backup-client prune "host/$${backup_id}" \
            --repository "$PBS_REPOSITORY" \
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
            --ns "$PBS_NAMESPACE" \
%{ endif ~}
            --keep-last "$${RETENTION}"

        log "✓ Prune completed"

        # Cleanup temporary files
        cleanup_temp_files

        # Send success notification
        send_backup_notification "success" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}"

        log "=== Backup Completed Successfully ==="
        return 0
    else
        log "✗ Backup failed with exit code: $${backup_exit_code}"

        # Capture error message (last few lines of output)
        local error_msg=""
        if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then
            error_msg=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | tail -5)
        fi

        # Send failure notification
        send_backup_notification "failure" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}" "Exit code: $${backup_exit_code}. $${error_msg}"

        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Execution
# =============================================================================

main() {
    log "========================================"
    log "PBS Backup: ${container_name}"
    log "Container ID: ${container_id}"
    log "Namespace: ${namespace}"
    log "========================================"

    # Run pre-backup hooks
    if ! run_pre_backup_hooks; then
        log "Pre-backup hooks failed, aborting backup"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Run backup
    if ! run_backup; then
        log "Backup failed"
        exit 1
    fi

    log "All tasks completed successfully"
    exit 0
}

# Run main function
main

# Homelab Infrastructure

OpenTofu-managed homelab on Proxmox. All commands run from local machine.

## Beads - AI Issue Tracking

This repo uses [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) for AI-native issue tracking. Beads helps AI agents manage complex, multi-step tasks by tracking dependencies between work items.
BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: run 'bd onboard' and follow the instructions

### Quick Commands

```bash
# Find ready work (no blockers)
task beads:ready

# List all issues
task beads:list
task beads:list STATUS=in_progress

# Create an issue
task beads:create TITLE="Add new LXC container for XYZ"

# View issue details
task beads:show ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Update status
task beads:update ID=proxmox-homelab-1 STATUS=in_progress
task beads:update ID=proxmox-homelab-1 STATUS=done

# Close completed work
task beads:close ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Add dependencies (FROM blocks TO)
task beads:dep FROM=proxmox-homelab-1 TO=proxmox-homelab-2

# View dependency tree
task beads:dep:tree ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Sync with git
task beads:sync
```

### For AI Agents

When starting work on this repo:

1. Run `bd ready` to see available tasks
2. Pick an issue and run `bd update <id> --status in_progress`
3. Complete the work
4. Run `bd close <id>` when done

Use `bd prime` to generate context for your session. Dependencies are tracked automatically - issues marked as "blocking" others will show up in the `bd ready` output once completed.

## Quick Reference

```bash
# OpenTofu workflow
task tofu:init APP=dashboards
task tofu:plan APP=dashboards
task tofu:apply APP=dashboards

# Desktop LXC (temporary GUI for downloads)
task desktop:create
task desktop:info
task desktop:destroy

# Backup operations
task backup:status                 # View backup status
task backup:now APP=immich         # Manual backup
task backup:all                    # Backup all containers
task backup:list APP=immich        # List backups
task backup:restore BACKUP=file TARGET_ID=305
task backup:immich:db              # Dump Immich database

# IP address management
task ip:next                       # Get next available IP for new LXC
task ip:list                       # Show all allocated IPs

# Beads issue tracking
task beads:ready                   # Show ready work (no blockers)
task beads:list                    # List all issues
task beads:create TITLE="..."      # Create new issue
task beads:show ID=...             # View issue details
task beads:close ID=...            # Complete an issue
```

## Architecture

- **Proxmox Host**: 192.168.1.215 (SSH: `ssh root@homelab`)
- **Traefik LXC**: 192.168.1.162 (ID: 200)
- **Monitoring LXC**: 192.168.1.229 (ID: 500)
- **IaC**: OpenTofu with bpg/proxmox provider
- **Secrets**: 1Password CLI (`op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"`)

## Documentation

- **[MIGRATION.md](tofu/MIGRATION.md)** - Guide for migrating apps to docker-lxc module pattern
- **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** - This file (project overview and quick reference)

## Project Structure

```text
tofu/
├── MIGRATION.md       # Migration guide for docker-lxc pattern
├── apps/              # Per-app configs with own state
│   ├── dashboards/    # Homepage + Dashy (ID: 201)
│   ├── immich/        # Photo management (ID: 304)
│   ├── monitoring/    # Prometheus + Grafana + Alerting (ID: 500)
│   ├── network-services/  # AdGuard DNS (ID: 101)
│   ├── openwebui/     # AI chat (ID: 501)
│   └── traefik/       # Reverse proxy (ID: 200)
├── configs/traefik/dynamic/  # Generated route configs
├── modules/           # Reusable modules
└── shared.tf          # Common vars (symlinked)
```

## Key Modules

- **lxc-base**: Base LXC container with static IP support
- **docker-host**: LXC + Docker + compose deployment
- **file-sync**: Rsync file transfers to LXCs
- **proxmox-notes**: Update LXC description in Proxmox UI

## IP Address Management

All static IPs are tracked in `tofu/ip-registry.tf` (symlinked to all apps).

### IP Ranges

| Range | Purpose |
| ----- | ------- |
| 192.168.1.1-99 | Infrastructure (router, Proxmox, switches) |
| 192.168.1.150-199 | LXC containers (apps) - **preferred for new deployments** |
| 192.168.1.200-224 | Reserved for manual/temporary use |
| 192.168.1.225-254 | Special services & overflow |

### Deploying a New Service

1. Get the next available IP:

   ```bash
   task ip:next
   # Output: Next available IP: 192.168.1.150
   # For lxc-base module: ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
   ```

2. Add the IP to `tofu/ip-registry.tf`:

   ```hcl
   apps = {
     # ... existing entries ...
     my_new_service = "192.168.1.150"  # LXC XXX - Description
   }
   ```

3. Use in your app's main.tf:

   ```hcl
   module "lxc" {
     source = "../../modules/lxc-base"
     # ...
     ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
     gateway    = "192.168.1.1"
   }
   ```

### Viewing All Allocations

```bash
task ip:list
```

## Network Domains

- `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` - Internal (Traefik websecure)
- `*.rambtech.dev` - Public (Cloudflare tunnel via web entrypoint)

## Monitoring Stack

The monitoring LXC (ID: 500, IP: 192.168.1.229) runs:

| Component | Port | Purpose |
| --------- | ---- | ------- |
| OpenTelemetry Collector | 4317/4318 | OTLP receiver (gRPC/HTTP) |
| Prometheus | 9090 | Metrics storage + alerting |
| Alertmanager | 9093 | Alert routing (ntfy + Discord) |
| Grafana | 3000 | Dashboards |
| Uptime Kuma | 3001 | HTTP monitoring |
| ntfy | 8080 | Push notifications |

### Key URLs

- Grafana: `https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Prometheus: `https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Alertmanager: `https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Uptime Kuma: `https://status.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- ntfy: `https://ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev`

### Syncing Monitoring Config

```bash
rsync -avz tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/ root@192.168.1.229:/config/
ssh root@192.168.1.229 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
```

## 1Password Integration

Secrets are managed via the 1Password OpenTofu provider (`1password/onepassword`).

### Key Files

- `tofu/onepassword.tf` - Data sources + `local.op` helper (symlinked to apps)
- `tofu/versions.tf` - Provider configs using `local.op.*`

### Available Secrets

```hcl
local.op.proxmox_api_token       # Proxmox API authentication
local.op.cloudflare_api_token    # Cloudflare DNS/tunnel API
local.op.cloudflare_tunnel_token # Cloudflare tunnel token
local.op.grafana_admin_password  # Grafana admin password
local.op.discord_webhook_url     # Discord alertmanager webhook
```

### Adding New Secrets

1. Create item in 1Password `homelab` vault
2. Add data source to `tofu/onepassword.tf`:

   ```hcl
   data "onepassword_item" "myservice" {
     vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
     title = "myservice"
   }
   ```

3. Add to `local.op` map in same file:

   ```hcl
   op = {
     myservice_password = data.onepassword_item.myservice.password
     # For section fields, flatten first then lookup:
     myservice_api_key = lookup(local._myservice_fields, "api_key", "")
   }
   ```

4. Use in modules: `local.op.myservice_password`

### Field Access Patterns

```hcl
# Main password field
data.onepassword_item.myitem.password

# Credential field (API keys)
data.onepassword_item.myitem.credential

# Custom fields in sections (must flatten):
locals {
  _myitem_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.myitem.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)
}
# Then: lookup(local._myitem_fields, "field_label", "")
```

### Why TF_VAR for State Encryption

State encryption runs before providers initialize, so it cannot use the 1Password provider:

```yaml
# Taskfile.yml
env:
  TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase:
    sh: op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"
```

### 1Password Items (homelab vault)

| Item | Fields |
|------|--------|
| `opentofu` | password, proxmox_api_token (section) |
| `Cloudflare` | tunnel_token, ddns_api_token (sections) |
| `grafana` | password |
| `discord-alertmanager-webhook` | credential |

## Important Notes

- SSH to Proxmox: `ssh root@homelab`
- SSH to Monitoring: `ssh root@192.168.1.229`
- Use IP addresses in provisioners (not hostnames)
- State files are encrypted and committed to git
- Each app has independent state in `tofu/apps/<app>/`
- 1Password CLI v2.23.0+ required (uses biometric auth)

## Taskfile Usage

**ALWAYS prefer running tasks from the Taskfile over direct commands.**

This repository uses a Taskfile for all common operations. Before running any command directly, check if there's a task for it using `task --list`.

Examples:

- Use `task tofu:apply APP=immich` instead of `cd tofu && tofu apply`
- Use `task tofu:plan APP=monitoring` instead of running tofu plan directly
- Use `task backup:status` instead of SSH commands to check backups

## OpenTofu/Terraform Workflow

**CRITICAL: OpenTofu commands must ALWAYS follow this sequence with NO skips:**

1. `task tofu:init APP=<app>` - Initialize the workspace
2. `task tofu:plan APP=<app>` - Generate and review the execution plan
3. `task tofu:apply APP=<app>` - Apply the changes

Never skip steps. Always run init, then plan, then apply - even if you think init has already been run.

## File Transfer Restrictions

**CRITICAL: You are strictly forbidden to transfer files over to any remote server under any circumstance unless the user has explicitly given you permission.**

This includes but is not limited to:

- SSH file transfers (scp, rsync, sftp)
- Copying files to LXC containers
- Uploading files to cloud services
- Any form of remote file deployment

You must always ask for explicit permission before transferring any files to remote systems.

# =============================================================================
# IP Address Registry
# =============================================================================
# Central registry of all static IP allocations in the homelab.
# This file serves as the single source of truth for IP assignments.
#
# Network Architecture:
#   - 192.168.1.0/24 (vmbr0): Home LAN - FIOS router, external access
#   - 10.100.0.0/16  (vmbr1): Container network - internal services
#
# IP Scheme (Container ID aligned with IP):
#   - 10.100.1.x:  Core services (LXC 100-149)
#   - 10.100.2.x:  Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249)
#   - 10.100.3.x:  Media - Photos (LXC 300-349)
#   - 10.100.4.x:  Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449)
#   - 10.100.5.x:  Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549)
#
# Dual-NIC Services (need 192.168.1.x for LAN compatibility):
#   - Traefik: Reverse proxy for LAN clients
#   - AdGuard: DNS for LAN devices
#   - Jellyfin: DLNA/casting
#   - Immich: Mobile app sync
# =============================================================================

locals {
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Network Configuration
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  network = {
    # Home LAN (vmbr0)
    lan_gateway = "192.168.1.1"
    lan_netmask = "/24"
    lan_prefix  = "192.168.1"

    # Container network (vmbr1)
    container_gateway = "10.100.0.1"
    container_netmask = "/16"
    container_prefix  = "10.100"
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IP Registry - Container Network (10.100.x.x)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Pattern: 10.100.<category>.<container_id_suffix>
  # Example: LXC 304 -> 10.100.3.104 (category 3, suffix 04)

  ip_registry = {
    # Infrastructure (192.168.1.x only - not containers)

# Homelab Infrastructure

OpenTofu-managed homelab on Proxmox. All commands run from local machine.

## Beads - AI Issue Tracking

This repo uses [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) for AI-native issue tracking. Beads helps AI agents manage complex, multi-step tasks by tracking dependencies between work items.
BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: run 'bd onboard' and follow the instructions

### Quick Commands

```bash
# Find ready work (no blockers)
bd ready

# List all issues
bd list
bd list --status=in_progress

# Create an issue
bd create --title="Add new LXC container for XYZ" --type=task --priority=2

# View issue details
bd show <id>

# Update status
bd update <id> --status=in_progress
bd update <id> --status=done

# Close completed work
bd close <id>
bd close <id1> <id2> ...  # Close multiple at once

# Add dependencies (issue depends on depends-on)
bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>

# Sync with git
bd sync
```

### For AI Agents

When starting work on this repo:

1. Run `bd ready` to see available tasks
2. Pick an issue and run `bd update <id> --status in_progress`
3. Complete the work
4. Run `bd close <id>` when done

Use `bd prime` to generate context for your session. Dependencies are tracked automatically - issues marked as "blocking" others will show up in the `bd ready` output once completed.

## Quick Reference

```bash
# OpenTofu workflow
task tofu:init APP=dashboards
task tofu:plan APP=dashboards
task tofu:apply APP=dashboards

# PBS Backups (Proxmox Backup Server - incremental, in-container)
task pbs:backup APP=n8n          # Trigger manual PBS backup
task pbs:backup:all              # Backup all apps
task pbs:backup:list APP=n8n     # List PBS snapshots
task pbs:backup:status APP=n8n   # Show backup status
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n SNAPSHOT=latest  # Restore from PBS

# Legacy vzdump backups (full container snapshots)
task backup:status               # View backup status
task backup:now APP=immich       # Manual backup
task backup:list APP=immich      # List backups

# DNS mode (for remote access via Tailscale)
task dns:status                  # Show current mode
task dns:travel                  # Switch to travel mode (Tailscale IPs)
task dns:home                    # Switch to home mode (LAN IPs)

# Desktop LXC (temporary GUI for downloads)
task desktop:create
task desktop:info
task desktop:destroy

# Beads issue tracking
bd ready                         # Show ready work (no blockers)
bd list                          # List all issues
bd create --title="..."          # Create new issue
bd show <id>                     # View issue details
bd close <id>                    # Complete an issue
```

## Architecture

### Network Topology

```
Internet
    │
    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Verizon FIOS Router (192.168.1.1)                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    │
    ├── vmbr0 (192.168.1.0/24) ─── Home LAN
    │       │
    │       └── Proxmox Host: 192.168.1.215
    │           └── Dual-NIC LXCs get LAN IPs for device compatibility
    │
    └── vmbr1 (10.100.0.0/16) ─── Container Network
            │
            └── Gateway: 10.100.0.1 (Proxmox)
                └── All LXC containers: 10.100.x.x
```

### IP Scheme (Container ID aligned with IP)

| Range | Purpose | Example |
|-------|---------|---------|
| 10.100.1.x | Core services (LXC 100-149) | LXC 101 → 10.100.1.101 |
| 10.100.2.x | Dashboards & Auth (LXC 200-249) | LXC 200 → 10.100.2.200 |
| 10.100.3.x | Media - Photos (LXC 300-349) | LXC 304 → 10.100.3.104 |
| 10.100.4.x | Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449) | LXC 401 → 10.100.4.101 |
| 10.100.5.x | Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549) | LXC 500 → 10.100.5.100 |

### LXC Containers

| ID | Name | Container IP | LAN IP | Purpose |
|----|------|--------------|--------|---------|
| 101 | network-services | 10.100.1.101 | 192.168.1.196 | AdGuard DNS + Tailscale |
| 102 | pbs | 10.100.1.102 | - | Proxmox Backup Server |
| 104 | container-mgmt | 10.100.1.104 | - | Pulse + Arcane |
| 200 | traefik | 10.100.2.200 | 192.168.1.235 | Reverse proxy |
| 201 | dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | 192.168.1.234 | Homepage + Dashy |
| 202 | authelia | 10.100.2.202 | 192.168.1.225 | SSO/Auth (deprecated) |
| 203 | authentik | 10.100.2.203 | - | Identity Provider |
| 303 | immich-importer | 10.100.3.103 | 192.168.1.223 | Photo import + iCloud sync |
| 304 | immich | 10.100.3.104 | 192.168.1.222 | Photo management |
| 401 | jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 | 192.168.1.226 | Media server + Jellystat |
| 402 | media-management | 10.100.4.102 | - | Arr stack (Sonarr, Radarr, etc) |
| 500 | monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | 192.168.1.229 | Prometheus, Grafana, ntfy |
| 501 | openwebui | 10.100.5.101 | 192.168.1.221 | AI chat |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | - | Workflow automation |
| 503 | obsidian-sync | 10.100.5.103 | - | Obsidian LiveSync (CouchDB) |
| 504 | documents | 10.100.5.104 | - | Paperless-ngx + Stirling-PDF |

### Key Infrastructure

- **Proxmox Host**: 192.168.1.215 (SSH: `ssh root@homelab`)
- **Container Gateway**: 10.100.0.1 (Proxmox vmbr1)
- **IaC**: OpenTofu with bpg/proxmox provider
- **Secrets**: 1Password CLI (`op read "op://homelab/..."`)
- **Identity**: Authentik (LXC 203) with Google OAuth
- **Backups**: PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) for incremental docker volume backups

## DNS Mode (Travel vs Home)

When working remotely via Tailscale, switch to travel mode:

```bash
# Check current mode
task dns:status

# Switch to travel mode (uses 10.100.x.x IPs via Tailscale)
task dns:travel

# Switch back to home mode (uses 192.168.1.x LAN IPs)
task dns:home
```

Travel mode changes:
- Proxmox API endpoint: 10.100.0.1:8006 (instead of 192.168.1.215:8006)
- SSH connections route through Tailscale
- Traefik route syncs use container IPs

The mode is controlled by `TF_VAR_dns_mode` in Taskfile.yml (default: `travel`).

## Project Structure

```text
tofu/
├── apps/                  # Per-app configs with independent state
│   ├── authentik/         # Identity provider (ID: 203)
│   ├── container-mgmt/    # Pulse + Arcane (ID: 104)
│   ├── dashboards/        # Homepage + Dashy (ID: 201)
│   ├── documents/         # Paperless-ngx (ID: 504)
│   ├── immich/            # Photo management (ID: 304)
│   ├── immich-importer/   # iCloud sync (ID: 303)
│   ├── jellyfin/          # Media server (ID: 401)
│   ├── media-management/  # Arr stack (ID: 402)
│   ├── monitoring/        # Prometheus + Grafana (ID: 500)
│   ├── n8n/               # Workflow automation (ID: 502)
│   ├── network-services/  # AdGuard DNS (ID: 101)
│   ├── obsidian-sync/     # LiveSync (ID: 503)
│   ├── openwebui/         # AI chat (ID: 501)
│   └── traefik/           # Reverse proxy (ID: 200)
├── modules/               # Reusable modules
│   ├── cloudflare-tunnel/ # Cloudflare tunnel config
│   ├── common/            # Shared utilities
│   ├── docker-lxc/        # LXC + Docker + compose deployment
│   ├── lxc-base/          # Base LXC container
│   ├── lxc-sidecars/      # PBS backup, DIUN configs
│   └── traefik-route/     # Traefik dynamic routes
├── configs/traefik/dynamic/  # Generated route configs
├── ip-registry.tf         # Central IP allocation (symlinked)
├── onepassword.tf         # 1Password data sources (symlinked)
├── shared.tf              # Common variables (symlinked)
└── versions.tf            # Provider configs (symlinked)
```

## Key Modules

- **docker-lxc**: Creates LXC + installs Docker + deploys compose stack
- **lxc-base**: Base LXC container with static IP, dual-NIC support
- **lxc-sidecars**: Configures PBS backup client, DIUN for container updates
- **traefik-route**: Generates and syncs Traefik dynamic route configs
- **cloudflare-tunnel**: Configures Cloudflare tunnel for public access

## PBS Backups (Proxmox Backup Server)

PBS provides incremental, deduplicated backups of docker volumes from within containers.

### How it works

1. `lxc-sidecars` module installs `proxmox-backup-client` in each container
2. Creates systemd timer for scheduled backups (default: daily)
3. Backs up docker volumes to PBS (LXC 102) with deduplication
4. Sends notifications to ntfy `backup-alerts` channel

### Configuration (in app's main.tf)

```hcl
module "sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "02:00"      # Daily at 2 AM
    retention = 7            # Keep 7 backups
    include_paths = ["/config"]
    pre_backup_commands = [
      {
        name    = "Dump PostgreSQL"
        command = "docker exec postgres pg_dump -U user db > /config/db.sql"
        timeout = "5m"
      }
    ]
    notify_on_success = true
    notify_on_failure = true
  }
}
```

### Manual Operations

```bash
# Trigger backup
task pbs:backup APP=n8n

# List snapshots
task pbs:backup:list APP=n8n

# Restore (stops container, restores data, restarts)
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n SNAPSHOT=latest
```

## Network Domains

- `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` - Internal services (Traefik websecure)
- `*.rambtech.dev` - Public services (Cloudflare tunnel)

## Monitoring Stack

The monitoring LXC (ID: 500, IP: 10.100.5.100) runs:

| Component | Port | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| Prometheus | 9090 | Metrics storage + alerting |
| Alertmanager | 9093 | Alert routing (ntfy + Discord) |
| Grafana | 3000 | Dashboards |
| Uptime Kuma | 3001 | HTTP monitoring |
| ntfy | 8080 | Push notifications |

### Key URLs

- Grafana: `https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Prometheus: `https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Alertmanager: `https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Uptime Kuma: `https://status.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- ntfy: `https://ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev`

### ntfy Channels

| Channel | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `homelab-alerts` | Prometheus/Alertmanager alerts |
| `backup-alerts` | PBS backup notifications |

## 1Password Integration

Secrets are managed via the 1Password OpenTofu provider.

### Key Files

- `tofu/onepassword.tf` - Data sources + `local.op` helper (symlinked to apps)
- `tofu/versions.tf` - Provider configs using `local.op.*`

### Available Secrets

```hcl
local.op.proxmox_api_token       # Proxmox API authentication
local.op.cloudflare_api_token    # Cloudflare DNS/tunnel API
local.op.cloudflare_tunnel_token # Cloudflare tunnel token
local.op.grafana_admin_password  # Grafana admin password
local.op.discord_webhook_url     # Discord alertmanager webhook
```

### Adding New Secrets

1. Create item in 1Password `homelab` vault
2. Add data source to `tofu/onepassword.tf`
3. Add to `local.op` map in same file
4. Use in modules: `local.op.myservice_password`

### Why TF_VAR for State Encryption

State encryption runs before providers initialize, so it cannot use the 1Password provider:

```yaml
# Taskfile.yml
env:
  TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase:
    sh: op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"
```

## Important Notes

- SSH to Proxmox: `ssh root@homelab`
- Use container IPs (10.100.x.x) in provisioners when in travel mode
- State files are encrypted and committed to git
- Each app has independent state in `tofu/apps/<app>/`
- 1Password CLI v2.23.0+ required (uses biometric auth)

## Taskfile Usage

**ALWAYS prefer running tasks from the Taskfile over direct commands.**

This repository uses a Taskfile for all common operations. Before running any command directly, check if there's a task for it using `task --list`.

Examples:

- Use `task tofu:apply APP=immich` instead of `cd tofu && tofu apply`
- Use `task pbs:backup APP=n8n` instead of SSH commands to trigger backups
- Use `task dns:travel` instead of manually editing TF_VAR_dns_mode

## OpenTofu/Terraform Workflow

**CRITICAL: OpenTofu commands must ALWAYS follow this sequence with NO skips:**

1. `task tofu:init APP=<app>` - Initialize the workspace
2. `task tofu:plan APP=<app>` - Generate and review the execution plan
3. `task tofu:apply APP=<app>` - Apply the changes

Never skip steps. Always run init, then plan, then apply - even if you think init has already been run.

## File Transfer Restrictions

**CRITICAL: You are strictly forbidden to transfer files over to any remote server under any circumstance unless the user has explicitly given you permission.**

This includes but is not limited to:

- SSH file transfers (scp, rsync, sftp)
- Copying files to LXC containers
- Uploading files to cloud services
- Any form of remote file deployment

You must always ask for explicit permission before transferring any files to remote systems.

# Homelab Infrastructure

OpenTofu-managed homelab on Proxmox. All commands run from local machine.

## Beads - AI Issue Tracking

This repo uses [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) for AI-native issue tracking. Beads helps AI agents manage complex, multi-step tasks by tracking dependencies between work items.
BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: run 'bd onboard' and follow the instructions

### Quick Commands

```bash
# Find ready work (no blockers)
bd ready

# List all issues
bd list
bd list --status=in_progress

# Create an issue
bd create --title="Add new LXC container for XYZ" --type=task --priority=2

# View issue details
bd show <id>

# Update status
bd update <id> --status=in_progress
bd update <id> --status=done

# Close completed work
bd close <id>
bd close <id1> <id2> ...  # Close multiple at once

# Add dependencies (issue depends on depends-on)
bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>

# Sync with git
bd sync
```

### For AI Agents

When starting work on this repo:

1. Run `bd ready` to see available tasks
2. Pick an issue and run `bd update <id> --status in_progress`
3. Complete the work
4. Run `bd close <id>` when done

Use `bd prime` to generate context for your session. Dependencies are tracked automatically - issues marked as "blocking" others will show up in the `bd ready` output once completed.

## Quick Reference

```bash
# OpenTofu workflow
task tofu:init APP=dashboards
task tofu:plan APP=dashboards
task tofu:apply APP=dashboards

# PBS Backups (Proxmox Backup Server - incremental, in-container)
task pbs:backup APP=n8n          # Trigger manual PBS backup
task pbs:backup:all              # Backup all apps
task pbs:backup:list APP=n8n     # List PBS snapshots
task pbs:backup:status APP=n8n   # Show backup status
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n SNAPSHOT=latest  # Restore from PBS

# Legacy vzdump backups (full container snapshots)
task backup:status               # View backup status
task backup:now APP=immich       # Manual backup
task backup:list APP=immich      # List backups

# DNS mode (for remote access via Tailscale)
task dns:status                  # Show current mode
task dns:travel                  # Switch to travel mode (Tailscale IPs)
task dns:home                    # Switch to home mode (LAN IPs)

# Desktop LXC (temporary GUI for downloads)
task desktop:create
task desktop:info
task desktop:destroy

# Beads issue tracking
bd ready                         # Show ready work (no blockers)
bd list                          # List all issues
bd create --title="..."          # Create new issue
bd show <id>                     # View issue details
bd close <id>                    # Complete an issue
```

## Architecture

### Network Topology

```
Internet
    │
    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Verizon FIOS Router (192.168.1.1)                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    │
    ├── vmbr0 (192.168.1.0/24) ─── Home LAN
    │       │
    │       └── Proxmox Host: 192.168.1.215
    │           └── Dual-NIC LXCs get LAN IPs for device compatibility
    │
    └── vmbr1 (10.100.0.0/16) ─── Container Network
            │
            └── Gateway: 10.100.0.1 (Proxmox)
                └── All LXC containers: 10.100.x.x
```

### IP Scheme (Container ID aligned with IP)

| Range | Purpose | Example |
|-------|---------|---------|
| 10.100.1.x | Core services (LXC 100-149) | LXC 101 → 10.100.1.101 |

| 10.100.4.x | Media - Streaming (LXC 400-449) | LXC 401 → 10.100.4.101 |
| 10.100.5.x | Monitoring & AI (LXC 500-549) | LXC 500 → 10.100.5.100 |

### LXC Containers

|----|------|--------------|--------|---------|

| 102 | pbs | 10.100.1.102 | - | Proxmox Backup Server |

### Key Infrastructure

- **Proxmox Host**: 192.168.1.215 (SSH: `ssh root@homelab`)
- **Container Gateway**: 10.100.0.1 (Proxmox vmbr1)
- **IaC**: OpenTofu with bpg/proxmox provider
- **Secrets**: 1Password CLI (`op read "op://homelab/..."`)
- **Identity**: Authentik (LXC 203) with Google OAuth
- **Backups**: PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) for incremental docker volume backups

## DNS Mode (Travel vs Home)

When working remotely via Tailscale, switch to travel mode:

```bash
# Check current mode
task dns:status

# Switch to travel mode (uses 10.100.x.x IPs via Tailscale)
task dns:travel

# Switch back to home mode (uses 192.168.1.x LAN IPs)
task dns:home
```

Travel mode changes:
- Proxmox API endpoint: 10.100.0.1:8006 (instead of 192.168.1.215:8006)
- SSH connections route through Tailscale
- Traefik route syncs use container IPs

The mode is controlled by `TF_VAR_dns_mode` in Taskfile.yml (default: `travel`).

## Project Structure

```text
tofu/
├── apps/                  # Per-app configs with independent state
│   ├── authentik/         # Identity provider (ID: 203)
│   ├── container-mgmt/    # Pulse + Arcane (ID: 104)
│   ├── dashboards/        # Homepage + Dashy (ID: 201)
│   ├── documents/         # Paperless-ngx (ID: 504)
│   ├── immich/            # Photo management (ID: 304)
│   ├── immich-importer/   # iCloud sync (ID: 303)
│   ├── jellyfin/          # Media server (ID: 401)
│   ├── media-management/  # Arr stack (ID: 402)
│   ├── monitoring/        # Prometheus + Grafana (ID: 500)
│   ├── n8n/               # Workflow automation (ID: 502)
│   ├── network-services/  # AdGuard DNS (ID: 101)
│   ├── obsidian-sync/     # LiveSync (ID: 503)
│   ├── openwebui/         # AI chat (ID: 501)
│   └── traefik/           # Reverse proxy (ID: 200)
├── modules/               # Reusable modules
│   ├── cloudflare-tunnel/ # Cloudflare tunnel config
│   ├── common/            # Shared utilities
│   ├── docker-lxc/        # LXC + Docker + compose deployment
│   ├── lxc-base/          # Base LXC container
│   ├── lxc-sidecars/      # PBS backup, DIUN configs
│   └── traefik-route/     # Traefik dynamic routes
├── configs/traefik/dynamic/  # Generated route configs
├── ip-registry.tf         # Central IP allocation (symlinked)
├── onepassword.tf         # 1Password data sources (symlinked)
├── shared.tf              # Common variables (symlinked)
└── versions.tf            # Provider configs (symlinked)
```

## Key Modules

- **docker-lxc**: Creates LXC + installs Docker + deploys compose stack
- **lxc-base**: Base LXC container with static IP, dual-NIC support
- **lxc-sidecars**: Configures PBS backup client, DIUN for container updates
- **traefik-route**: Generates and syncs Traefik dynamic route configs
- **cloudflare-tunnel**: Configures Cloudflare tunnel for public access

## PBS Backups (Proxmox Backup Server)

PBS provides incremental, deduplicated backups of docker volumes from within containers.

### How it works

1. `lxc-sidecars` module installs `proxmox-backup-client` in each container
2. Creates systemd timer for scheduled backups (default: daily)
3. Backs up docker volumes to PBS (LXC 102) with deduplication
4. Sends notifications to ntfy `backup-alerts` channel

### Configuration (in app's main.tf)

```hcl
module "sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "02:00"      # Daily at 2 AM
    retention = 7            # Keep 7 backups
    include_paths = ["/config"]
    pre_backup_commands = [
      {
        name    = "Dump PostgreSQL"
        command = "docker exec postgres pg_dump -U user db > /config/db.sql"
        timeout = "5m"
      }
    ]
    notify_on_success = true
    notify_on_failure = true
  }
}
```

### Manual Operations

```bash
# Trigger backup
task pbs:backup APP=n8n

# List snapshots
task pbs:backup:list APP=n8n

# Restore (stops container, restores data, restarts)
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n SNAPSHOT=latest
```

## Network Domains

- `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` - Internal services (Traefik websecure)
- `*.rambtech.dev` - Public services (Cloudflare tunnel)

## Monitoring Stack

The monitoring LXC (ID: 500, IP: 10.100.5.100) runs:

| Component | Port | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| Prometheus | 9090 | Metrics storage + alerting |
| Alertmanager | 9093 | Alert routing (ntfy + Discord) |
| Grafana | 3000 | Dashboards |
| Uptime Kuma | 3001 | HTTP monitoring |
| ntfy | 8080 | Push notifications |

### Key URLs

- Grafana: `https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Prometheus: `https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Alertmanager: `https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Uptime Kuma: `https://status.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- ntfy: `https://ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev`

### ntfy Channels

| Channel | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `homelab-alerts` | Prometheus/Alertmanager alerts |
| `backup-alerts` | PBS backup notifications |

## 1Password Integration

Secrets are managed via the 1Password OpenTofu provider.

### Key Files

- `tofu/onepassword.tf` - Data sources + `local.op` helper (symlinked to apps)
- `tofu/versions.tf` - Provider configs using `local.op.*`

### Available Secrets

```hcl
local.op.proxmox_api_token       # Proxmox API authentication
local.op.cloudflare_api_token    # Cloudflare DNS/tunnel API
local.op.cloudflare_tunnel_token # Cloudflare tunnel token
local.op.grafana_admin_password  # Grafana admin password
local.op.discord_webhook_url     # Discord alertmanager webhook
```

### Adding New Secrets

1. Create item in 1Password `homelab` vault
2. Add data source to `tofu/onepassword.tf`
3. Add to `local.op` map in same file
4. Use in modules: `local.op.myservice_password`

### Why TF_VAR for State Encryption

State encryption runs before providers initialize, so it cannot use the 1Password provider:

```yaml
# Taskfile.yml
env:
  TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase:
    sh: op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"
```

## Important Notes

- SSH to Proxmox: `ssh root@homelab`
- Use container IPs (10.100.x.x) in provisioners when in travel mode
- State files are encrypted and committed to git
- Each app has independent state in `tofu/apps/<app>/`
- 1Password CLI v2.23.0+ required (uses biometric auth)

## Taskfile Usage

**ALWAYS prefer running tasks from the Taskfile over direct commands.**

This repository uses a Taskfile for all common operations. Before running any command directly, check if there's a task for it using `task --list`.

Examples:

- Use `task tofu:apply APP=immich` instead of `cd tofu && tofu apply`
- Use `task pbs:backup APP=n8n` instead of SSH commands to trigger backups
- Use `task dns:travel` instead of manually editing TF_VAR_dns_mode

## OpenTofu/Terraform Workflow

**CRITICAL: OpenTofu commands must ALWAYS follow this sequence with NO skips:**

1. `task tofu:init APP=<app>` - Initialize the workspace
2. `task tofu:plan APP=<app>` - Generate and review the execution plan
3. `task tofu:apply APP=<app>` - Apply the changes

Never skip steps. Always run init, then plan, then apply - even if you think init has already been run.

## File Transfer Restrictions

**CRITICAL: You are strictly forbidden to transfer files over to any remote server under any circumstance unless the user has explicitly given you permission.**

This includes but is not limited to:

- SSH file transfers (scp, rsync, sftp)
- Copying files to LXC containers
- Uploading files to cloud services
- Any form of remote file deployment

You must always ask for explicit permission before transferring any files to remote systems.

# Homelab Infrastructure

OpenTofu-managed homelab on Proxmox. All commands run from local machine.

## Beads - AI Issue Tracking

This repo uses [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) for AI-native issue tracking. Beads helps AI agents manage complex, multi-step tasks by tracking dependencies between work items.
BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: run 'bd onboard' and follow the instructions

### Quick Commands

```bash
# Find ready work (no blockers)
task beads:ready

# List all issues
task beads:list
task beads:list STATUS=in_progress

# Create an issue
task beads:create TITLE="Add new LXC container for XYZ"

# View issue details
task beads:show ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Update status
task beads:update ID=proxmox-homelab-1 STATUS=in_progress
task beads:update ID=proxmox-homelab-1 STATUS=done

# Close completed work
task beads:close ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Add dependencies (FROM blocks TO)
task beads:dep FROM=proxmox-homelab-1 TO=proxmox-homelab-2

# View dependency tree
task beads:dep:tree ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Sync with git
task beads:sync
```

### For AI Agents

When starting work on this repo:

1. Run `bd ready` to see available tasks
2. Pick an issue and run `bd update <id> --status in_progress`
3. Complete the work
4. Run `bd close <id>` when done

Use `bd prime` to generate context for your session. Dependencies are tracked automatically - issues marked as "blocking" others will show up in the `bd ready` output once completed.

## Quick Reference

```bash
# OpenTofu workflow
task tofu:init APP=dashboards
task tofu:plan APP=dashboards
task tofu:apply APP=dashboards

# Desktop LXC (temporary GUI for downloads)
task desktop:create
task desktop:info
task desktop:destroy

# Backup operations
task backup:status                 # View backup status
task backup:now APP=immich         # Manual backup
task backup:all                    # Backup all containers
task backup:list APP=immich        # List backups
task backup:restore BACKUP=file TARGET_ID=305
task backup:immich:db              # Dump Immich database

# IP address management
task ip:next                       # Get next available IP for new LXC
task ip:list                       # Show all allocated IPs

# Beads issue tracking
task beads:ready                   # Show ready work (no blockers)
task beads:list                    # List all issues
task beads:create TITLE="..."      # Create new issue
task beads:show ID=...             # View issue details
task beads:close ID=...            # Complete an issue
```

## Architecture

- **Proxmox Host**: 192.168.1.215 (SSH: `ssh root@homelab`)
- **Traefik LXC**: 192.168.1.162 (ID: 200)
- **Monitoring LXC**: 192.168.1.229 (ID: 500)
- **IaC**: OpenTofu with bpg/proxmox provider
- **Secrets**: 1Password CLI (`op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"`)

## Documentation

- **[MIGRATION.md](tofu/MIGRATION.md)** - Guide for migrating apps to docker-lxc module pattern
- **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** - This file (project overview and quick reference)

## Project Structure

```text
tofu/
├── MIGRATION.md       # Migration guide for docker-lxc pattern
├── apps/              # Per-app configs with own state
│   ├── dashboards/    # Homepage + Dashy (ID: 201)
│   ├── immich/        # Photo management (ID: 304)
│   ├── monitoring/    # Prometheus + Grafana + Alerting (ID: 500)
│   ├── network-services/  # AdGuard DNS (ID: 101)
│   ├── openwebui/     # AI chat (ID: 501)
│   └── traefik/       # Reverse proxy (ID: 200)
├── configs/traefik/dynamic/  # Generated route configs
├── modules/           # Reusable modules
└── shared.tf          # Common vars (symlinked)
```

## Key Modules

- **lxc-base**: Base LXC container with static IP support
- **docker-host**: LXC + Docker + compose deployment
- **file-sync**: Rsync file transfers to LXCs
- **proxmox-notes**: Update LXC description in Proxmox UI

## IP Address Management

All static IPs are tracked in `tofu/ip-registry.tf` (symlinked to all apps).

### IP Ranges

| Range | Purpose |
| ----- | ------- |
| 192.168.1.1-99 | Infrastructure (router, Proxmox, switches) |
| 192.168.1.150-199 | LXC containers (apps) - **preferred for new deployments** |
| 192.168.1.200-224 | Reserved for manual/temporary use |
| 192.168.1.225-254 | Special services & overflow |

### Deploying a New Service

1. Get the next available IP:

   ```bash
   task ip:next
   # Output: Next available IP: 192.168.1.150
   # For lxc-base module: ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
   ```

2. Add the IP to `tofu/ip-registry.tf`:

   ```hcl
   apps = {
     # ... existing entries ...
     my_new_service = "192.168.1.150"  # LXC XXX - Description
   }
   ```

3. Use in your app's main.tf:

   ```hcl
   module "lxc" {
     source = "../../modules/lxc-base"
     # ...
     ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
     gateway    = "192.168.1.1"
   }
   ```

### Viewing All Allocations

```bash
task ip:list
```

## Network Domains

- `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` - Internal (Traefik websecure)
- `*.rambtech.dev` - Public (Cloudflare tunnel via web entrypoint)

## Monitoring Stack

The monitoring LXC (ID: 500, IP: 192.168.1.229) runs:

| Component | Port | Purpose |
| --------- | ---- | ------- |
| OpenTelemetry Collector | 4317/4318 | OTLP receiver (gRPC/HTTP) |
| Prometheus | 9090 | Metrics storage + alerting |
| Alertmanager | 9093 | Alert routing (ntfy + Discord) |
| Grafana | 3000 | Dashboards |
| Uptime Kuma | 3001 | HTTP monitoring |
| ntfy | 8080 | Push notifications |

### Key URLs

- Grafana: `https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Prometheus: `https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Alertmanager: `https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Uptime Kuma: `https://status.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- ntfy: `https://ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev`

### Syncing Monitoring Config

```bash
rsync -avz tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/ root@192.168.1.229:/config/
ssh root@192.168.1.229 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
```

## 1Password Integration

Secrets are managed via the 1Password OpenTofu provider (`1password/onepassword`).

### Key Files

- `tofu/onepassword.tf` - Data sources + `local.op` helper (symlinked to apps)
- `tofu/versions.tf` - Provider configs using `local.op.*`

### Available Secrets

```hcl
local.op.proxmox_api_token       # Proxmox API authentication
local.op.cloudflare_api_token    # Cloudflare DNS/tunnel API
local.op.cloudflare_tunnel_token # Cloudflare tunnel token
local.op.grafana_admin_password  # Grafana admin password
local.op.discord_webhook_url     # Discord alertmanager webhook
```

### Adding New Secrets

1. Create item in 1Password `homelab` vault
2. Add data source to `tofu/onepassword.tf`:

   ```hcl
   data "onepassword_item" "myservice" {
     vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
     title = "myservice"
   }
   ```

3. Add to `local.op` map in same file:

   ```hcl
   op = {
     myservice_password = data.onepassword_item.myservice.password
     # For section fields, flatten first then lookup:
     myservice_api_key = lookup(local._myservice_fields, "api_key", "")
   }
   ```

4. Use in modules: `local.op.myservice_password`

### Field Access Patterns

```hcl
# Main password field
data.onepassword_item.myitem.password

# Credential field (API keys)
data.onepassword_item.myitem.credential

# Custom fields in sections (must flatten):
locals {
  _myitem_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.myitem.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)
}
# Then: lookup(local._myitem_fields, "field_label", "")
```

### Why TF_VAR for State Encryption

State encryption runs before providers initialize, so it cannot use the 1Password provider:

```yaml
# Taskfile.yml
env:
  TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase:
    sh: op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"
```

### 1Password Items (homelab vault)

| Item | Fields |
|------|--------|
| `opentofu` | password, proxmox_api_token (section) |
| `Cloudflare` | tunnel_token, ddns_api_token (sections) |
| `grafana` | password |
| `discord-alertmanager-webhook` | credential |

## Important Notes

- SSH to Proxmox: `ssh root@homelab`
- SSH to Monitoring: `ssh root@192.168.1.229`
- Use IP addresses in provisioners (not hostnames)
- State files are encrypted and committed to git
- Each app has independent state in `tofu/apps/<app>/`
- 1Password CLI v2.23.0+ required (uses biometric auth)

## Taskfile Usage

**ALWAYS prefer running tasks from the Taskfile over direct commands.**

This repository uses a Taskfile for all common operations. Before running any command directly, check if there's a task for it using `task --list`.

Examples:

- Use `task tofu:apply APP=immich` instead of `cd tofu && tofu apply`
- Use `task tofu:plan APP=monitoring` instead of running tofu plan directly
- Use `task backup:status` instead of SSH commands to check backups

## OpenTofu/Terraform Workflow

**CRITICAL: OpenTofu commands must ALWAYS follow this sequence with NO skips:**

1. `task tofu:init APP=<app>` - Initialize the workspace
2. `task tofu:plan APP=<app>` - Generate and review the execution plan
3. `task tofu:apply APP=<app>` - Apply the changes

Never skip steps. Always run init, then plan, then apply - even if you think init has already been run.

## File Transfer Restrictions

**CRITICAL: You are strictly forbidden to transfer files over to any remote server under any circumstance unless the user has explicitly given you permission.**

This includes but is not limited to:

- SSH file transfers (scp, rsync, sftp)
- Copying files to LXC containers
- Uploading files to cloud services
- Any form of remote file deployment

You must always ask for explicit permission before transferring any files to remote systems.

content.content:
proxmox-homelab-45r: Epic: Migrate from Authelia to Authentik
Status: in_progress
Priority: P1
Type: epic
Created: 2025-12-21 00:15
Updated: 2025-12-21 01:16

Description:
Complete migration from Authelia to Authentik as the centralized identity provider.

## Overview
Replace Authelia with Authentik to gain:
- Native Google/GitHub OAuth federation
- OIDC provider capabilities for apps with native SSO support
- Forward auth for apps without native OAuth
- Centralized user/group management
- Jellyfin SSO plugin compatibility

## Phases

### Phase 1: Infrastructure
- Deploy Authentik alongside Traefik in LXC 200
- Configure Google OAuth source
- Setup forward auth middleware in Traefik

### Phase 2: Dashboard & Utility Apps (Forward Auth)
- Homepage, Dashy, Pulse, Arcane, Stirling-PDF
- Prometheus, Alertmanager

### Phase 3: Media & Network Apps (Forward Auth)
- Uptime Kuma, qBittorrent
- Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, SABnzbd
- AdGuard, Traefik Dashboard, ntfy

### Phase 4: Native OIDC Apps
- Grafana, OpenWebUI, Paperless-ngx, n8n, Jellyseerr

### Phase 5: Media Apps (Native OIDC)
- Immich, Jellyfin

### Phase 6: Cleanup
- Decommission Authelia

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All services authenticated via Authentik
- [ ] Google OAuth login working for all users
- [ ] Authelia fully decommissioned
- [ ] All configuration managed as code (OpenTofu/Ansible)

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] All services authenticated via Authentik

- [ ] Authelia fully decommissioned
- [ ] All configuration managed as code (OpenTofu/Ansible)

# Common Traefik middlewares and transports for homelab
http:
  # ServersTransport for backends with self-signed certificates
  serversTransports:
    insecure:
      insecureSkipVerify: true

  middlewares:
    security-headers:
      headers:
        browserXssFilter: true
        contentTypeNosniff: true
        forceSTSHeader: true
        stsIncludeSubdomains: true
        stsPreload: true
        stsSeconds: 31536000
        customFrameOptionsValue: "SAMEORIGIN"
        referrerPolicy: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

    public-security:
      headers:
        browserXssFilter: true
        contentTypeNosniff: true
        customFrameOptionsValue: "SAMEORIGIN"
        referrerPolicy: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

    # Internal-only: Allow only local network, container network, and Tailscale
    internal-only:
      ipAllowList:
        sourceRange:
          - "192.168.1.0/24"    # Local LAN
          - "10.100.0.0/16"     # Container network (LXC containers)
          - "172.16.0.0/12"     # Docker bridge networks (172.16-31.x.x)
          - "100.64.0.0/10"     # Tailscale CGNAT range
          - "127.0.0.1/32"      # Localhost

    # Authelia forward auth middleware
    authelia:
      forwardAuth:
        address: "http://10.100.2.202:9091/api/authz/forward-auth"
        trustForwardHeader: true
        authResponseHeaders:
          - "Remote-User"
          - "Remote-Groups"
          - "Remote-Email"
          - "Remote-Name"

    # Ollama API basic auth
    ollama-auth:
      basicAuth:
        users:
          - "ollama-api:$2y$05$DmLSIME.Uvr6TZEr.qSRK.Nwt9bzfSOV5RXPly9tD8hlQwSGhQz0i"
        realm: "Ollama API"

# =============================================================================
# Authentik LXC - Identity Provider (SSO/OIDC)
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 203
#
# Replaces Authelia with a more feature-rich identity provider:
#   - Native Google/GitHub OAuth federation
#   - OIDC provider for apps with native SSO support
#   - Forward auth for apps without native OAuth
#   - Centralized user/group management
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Authentik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 203
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 4096  # Authentik recommended minimum
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 16
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "authentik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "authentik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only - Traefik handles external access)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.dashboards.authentik}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude .env template files (we generate .env from template)
  exclude_patterns = ["^\\.env"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Authentik"
  service_description = "Identity Provider - SSO, OIDC, and forward auth for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {
    admin    = "https://auth.${var.domain_internal}/if/admin/"
    user     = "https://auth.${var.domain_internal}/if/user/"
    direct   = "http://${local.ip_registry.dashboards.authentik}:9000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Authentik HTTP", port = 9000, info = "Web UI and API" },
    { name = "Authentik HTTPS", port = 9443, info = "HTTPS (self-signed)" },
    { name = "PostgreSQL", port = 5432, info = "Database (internal only)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Initial Setup

1. Access the admin interface at https://auth.${var.domain_internal}/if/admin/
2. Login with credentials from 1Password (item: authentik)
3. Configure Google OAuth source for SSO

## Forward Auth Endpoint

Add this middleware to Traefik routes for protected services:
```yaml
middlewares:
  authentik:
    forwardAuth:
      address: http://${local.ip_registry.dashboards.authentik}:9000/outpost.goauthentik.io/auth/traefik
      trustForwardHeader: true
      authResponseHeaders:
        - X-authentik-username
        - X-authentik-groups
        - X-authentik-email
        - X-authentik-name
        - X-authentik-uid
        - X-authentik-jwt
        - X-authentik-meta-jwks
        - X-authentik-meta-outpost
        - X-authentik-meta-provider
        - X-authentik-meta-app
        - X-authentik-meta-version
```

## Quick Commands

```bash
# View server logs
docker logs -f authentik-server

# View worker logs
docker logs -f authentik-worker

# Database backup
docker exec authentik-postgres pg_dump -U authentik authentik > backup.sql

# Restart services
cd /config && docker compose restart
```

## OIDC Configuration

For apps with native OIDC support, create a Provider in Authentik:
1. Admin → Providers → Create OAuth2/OIDC Provider
2. Set redirect URI for the app
3. Create Application linking to the provider
4. Use client_id and client_secret in the app config

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=authentik` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["authentik", "auth", "sso", "oidc", "identity"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "authentik_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    postgres_password = local.op.authentik_postgres_password
    secret_key        = local.op.authentik_secret_key
    admin_email       = "admin@${var.domain_internal}"
    admin_password    = local.op.authentik_admin_password
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/authentik.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "authentik_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.authentik_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.authentik.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.authentik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Route - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "authentik_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "authentik"
  backend_url = "http://${module.authentik.ip_address}:9000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  # Using "auth" subdomain to match Authelia for easier migration
  internal_domain = "auth.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Public route for external access (Google OAuth redirect)
  public_domain = "auth.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # No auth middleware on the auth service itself!
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]
  # Use "web" entrypoint for public - Cloudflare handles TLS and forwards HTTP to origin
  public_entrypoint    = ["web"]

  depends_on = [module.authentik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Forward Auth Middleware
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generates the forwardAuth middleware config and syncs to Traefik

resource "local_file" "traefik_middleware" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/traefik-middleware.yml.tpl", {
    authentik_ip = module.authentik.ip_address
  })
  filename = "${path.module}/.terraform/authentik-middleware.yml"
}

resource "filesync_file" "traefik_middleware" {
  source      = local_file.traefik_middleware.filename
  destination = "/config/dynamic/authentik-middleware.yml"
  host        = local.traefik_ip

  mode = "0644"

  depends_on = [module.authentik, local_file.traefik_middleware]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Terraform API Token - Non-expiring
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates a non-expiring API token for Terraform to manage authentik.
# The token value is stored in 1Password and used by the provider.
#
# Bootstrap: Create a short-lived token in UI first, run tofu apply,
# then update 1Password with the new token value from the output.

data "authentik_user" "akadmin" {
  username = "akadmin"
}

resource "authentik_token" "terraform" {
  identifier   = "terraform-api"
  user         = data.authentik_user.akadmin.id
  intent       = "api"
  expiring     = false  # Never expires
  description  = "API token for OpenTofu/Terraform - managed by IaC"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Google OAuth Source - SSO via Google Account
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Allows users to login with their Google account
# Credentials stored in 1Password (authentik item)

data "authentik_flow" "default_source_authentication" {
  slug = "default-source-authentication"
}

resource "authentik_source_oauth" "google" {
  name                = "Google"
  slug                = "google"
  authentication_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_source_authentication.id

  # No enrollment flow - users must be pre-created in authentik
  # This prevents unauthorized users from self-registering
  enrollment_flow = ""

  provider_type   = "google"
  consumer_key    = local.op.authentik_google_client_id
  consumer_secret = local.op.authentik_google_client_secret

  # Match users by email identifier
  user_matching_mode = "identifier"

  # Policy engine mode
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Link Google OAuth to Login Flow
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# NOTE: The Google source must be manually added to the identification stage
# in the authentik admin UI:
#   1. Go to Flows & Stages → Stages
#   2. Edit "default-authentication-identification"
#   3. Add "Google" to the Sources field
#   4. Save
#
# This is required because the stage already exists and can't be recreated
# via Terraform without importing it first.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Users - Managed via SOPS encrypted file
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Users who can login via Google OAuth. Email must match their Google account.
# Edit with: sops edit tofu/apps/authentik/users.sops.yaml

data "sops_file" "users" {
  source_file = "${path.module}/users.sops.yaml"
}

locals {
  # User data is encrypted at rest but not truly secret - it's just user info
  # Using nonsensitive() so we can iterate with for_each
  authentik_users = nonsensitive(yamldecode(data.sops_file.users.raw).authentik_users)
}

resource "authentik_user" "users" {
  for_each = local.authentik_users

  username = each.key
  email    = each.value.email
  name     = each.value.name

  # Users authenticate via Google OAuth, no local password needed
  # They can set one later if desired via the user portal
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client + Sidecars
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "authentik_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.authentik.container_id
  container_ip   = module.authentik.ip_address
  container_name = "authentik"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-203"

    # Dump PostgreSQL before backup
    pre_backup_commands = [
      {
        name    = "Backup PostgreSQL database"
        command = "docker exec authentik-postgres pg_dump -U authentik authentik > /config/authentik-db-backup.sql"
        timeout = 120
      }
    ]

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,authentik"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["authentik"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["authentik"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.authentik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.authentik.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.authentik.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.authentik.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    admin  = "https://auth.${var.domain_internal}/if/admin/"
    user   = "https://auth.${var.domain_internal}/if/user/"
    direct = "http://${module.authentik.ip_address}:9000"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  description = "Path to Traefik config on Traefik LXC"
  value       = module.authentik_route.remote_config_path
}

output "terraform_api_token" {
  description = "API token for Terraform - update 1Password with this value"
  value       = authentik_token.terraform.key
  sensitive   = true
}

output "forward_auth_url" {
  description = "URL for Traefik forwardAuth middleware"
  value       = "http://${module.authentik.ip_address}:9000/outpost.goauthentik.io/auth/traefik"
}
