# =============================================================================
# Authentik Providers - OAuth Sources, Forward Auth, OIDC Providers
# =============================================================================
# This file contains all Authentik provider configurations:
#   - Google OAuth source (SSO via Google)
#   - Forward auth provider for Traefik
#   - OIDC providers for apps with native SSO support (future)
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Terraform API Token - Non-expiring
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates a non-expiring API token for Terraform to manage authentik.
# The token value is stored in 1Password and used by the provider.
#
# Bootstrap: Create a short-lived token in UI first, run tofu apply,
# then update 1Password with the new token value from the output.

data "authentik_user" "akadmin" {
  username = "akadmin"
}

resource "authentik_token" "terraform" {
  identifier   = "terraform-api"
  user         = data.authentik_user.akadmin.id
  intent       = "api"
  expiring     = false  # Never expires
  description  = "API token for OpenTofu/Terraform - managed by IaC"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Google OAuth Source - SSO via Google Account
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Allows users to login with their Google account
# Credentials stored in 1Password (authentik item)

data "authentik_flow" "default_source_authentication" {
  slug = "default-source-authentication"
}

resource "authentik_source_oauth" "google" {
  name                = "Google"
  slug                = "google"
  authentication_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_source_authentication.id

  # No enrollment flow - users must be pre-created in authentik
  # This prevents unauthorized users from self-registering
  enrollment_flow = ""

  provider_type   = "google"
  consumer_key    = local.op.authentik_google_client_id
  consumer_secret = local.op.authentik_google_client_secret

  # Match users by email identifier
  user_matching_mode = "identifier"

  # Policy engine mode
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Link Google OAuth to Login Flow
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# NOTE: The Google source must be manually added to the identification stage
# in the authentik admin UI:
#   1. Go to Flows & Stages → Stages
#   2. Edit "default-authentication-identification"
#   3. Add "Google" to the Sources field
#   4. Save
#
# This is required because the stage already exists and can't be recreated
# via Terraform without importing it first.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Forward Auth Provider - For protecting services via Traefik
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates a Proxy Provider in forward auth mode for protecting services
# that don't have native OIDC support. The embedded outpost handles the auth.

data "authentik_flow" "default_authorization" {
  slug = "default-provider-authorization-implicit-consent"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_invalidation" {
  slug = "default-provider-invalidation-flow"
}

resource "authentik_provider_proxy" "forward_auth" {
  name               = "Traefik Forward Auth"
  mode               = "forward_single"  # Single application mode for forward auth
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
  invalidation_flow  = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id

  # External host - Traefik sends X-Forwarded-* headers with the original request
  external_host = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"

  # Cookie settings for SSO across all subdomains
  # Must be the root domain to work with both *.homelab.rambtech.dev and auth.rambtech.dev
  cookie_domain = var.domain_public
}

resource "authentik_application" "forward_auth" {
  name              = "Homelab Forward Auth"
  slug              = "homelab-forward-auth"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id

  meta_description = "Forward authentication for homelab services protected by Traefik"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab Infrastructure"

  # Open to all authenticated users
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# Update the embedded outpost to include the forward auth provider
# Note: The embedded outpost is managed by authentik, we just update its providers
resource "authentik_outpost" "embedded" {
  name               = "authentik Embedded Outpost"
  type               = "proxy"
  protocol_providers = [authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id]

  config = jsonencode({
    # Internal URL for outpost-to-authentik communication
    authentik_host          = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"
    # Browser URL - what users see (HTTPS via Cloudflare)
    authentik_host_browser  = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"
    authentik_host_insecure = false
    log_level               = "info"
  })

  lifecycle {
    # The embedded outpost already exists, we're just updating it
    ignore_changes = [service_connection]
  }
}

   - User reported errors about mixed content (HTTP vs HTTPS)

   c. Created forward auth application linked to provider
   d. Imported existing embedded outpost
   e. Updated middleware to use internal HTTP address
   f. Updated Traefik to trust Cloudflare forwarded headers
   g. Added AUTHENTIK_COOKIE__SECURE=true to Authentik env
   h. Set authentik_host_browser for HTTPS browser redirects

5. **Files Modified**:
   - `tofu/apps/authentik/main.tf` - Refactored, now contains container, env, routes, sidecars
   - `tofu/apps/authentik/providers.tf` - NEW: OAuth sources, forward auth provider

   - `tofu/apps/dashboards/main.tf` - Added authentik middleware to Homepage route

   - `authentik_outpost` data source doesn't exist - used resource instead with lifecycle ignore
   - Outpost already exists - imported with `tofu import`
   - Mixed content errors (HTTP vs HTTPS) - multiple fixes attempted
   - 404 from outpost for forward auth - changed mode from `forward_single` to `forward_domain`

7. **Current Issue**: The outpost was returning 404 for `/outpost.goauthentik.io/auth/traefik` because `forward_single` mode requires exact host matching. Changed to `forward_domain` mode to protect all subdomains.

8. **Last Action**: Applied change from `forward_single` to `forward_domain` mode for the proxy provider. User hasn't confirmed if this fixed the issue yet.

1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Continue work on Authentik migration epic (proxmox-homelab-45r)

   - Use public domain `auth.rambtech.dev` for authentication (not internal domain)
   - Use internal HTTP communication between Traefik and Authentik for performance
   - Split large main.tf into manageable chunks

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Authentik forward auth with Traefik middleware
   - Proxy Provider modes: `forward_single` vs `forward_domain`
   - Embedded outpost configuration
   - Cookie domain for cross-subdomain SSO
   - Cloudflare TLS termination and forwarded headers
   - Mixed content issues (HTTP/HTTPS)
   - OpenTofu resource import for existing resources
   - SOPS-encrypted user management

     resource "authentik_provider_proxy" "forward_auth" {

```javascript
api: {
    base: "http://auth.rambtech.dev/",

The API base URL is set to **HTTP** but your browser is on **HTTPS**. This causes mixed content blocking - the browser won't allow HTTPS pages to make HTTP API calls.

# Common Traefik middlewares and transports for homelab
http:
  # ServersTransport for backends with self-signed certificates
  serversTransports:
    insecure:
      insecureSkipVerify: true

  middlewares:
    security-headers:
      headers:
        browserXssFilter: true
        contentTypeNosniff: true
        forceSTSHeader: true
        stsIncludeSubdomains: true
        stsPreload: true
        stsSeconds: 31536000
        customFrameOptionsValue: "SAMEORIGIN"
        referrerPolicy: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

    public-security:
      headers:
        browserXssFilter: true
        contentTypeNosniff: true
        customFrameOptionsValue: "SAMEORIGIN"
        referrerPolicy: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

    # Internal-only: Allow only local network, container network, and Tailscale
    internal-only:
      ipAllowList:
        sourceRange:
          - "192.168.1.0/24"    # Local LAN
          - "10.100.0.0/16"     # Container network (LXC containers)
          - "172.16.0.0/12"     # Docker bridge networks (172.16-31.x.x)
          - "100.64.0.0/10"     # Tailscale CGNAT range
          - "127.0.0.1/32"      # Localhost

    # Authelia forward auth middleware
    authelia:
      forwardAuth:
        address: "http://10.100.2.202:9091/api/authz/forward-auth"
        trustForwardHeader: true
        authResponseHeaders:
          - "Remote-User"
          - "Remote-Groups"
          - "Remote-Email"
          - "Remote-Name"

    # Ollama API basic auth
    ollama-auth:
      basicAuth:
        users:
          - "ollama-api:$2y$05$DmLSIME.Uvr6TZEr.qSRK.Nwt9bzfSOV5RXPly9tD8hlQwSGhQz0i"
        realm: "Ollama API"

# =============================================================================
# Authentik LXC - Identity Provider (SSO/OIDC)
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 203
#
# Replaces Authelia with a more feature-rich identity provider:
#   - Native Google/GitHub OAuth federation
#   - OIDC provider for apps with native SSO support
#   - Forward auth for apps without native OAuth
#   - Centralized user/group management
#
# File Structure:
#   - main.tf:      Container, env, routes, sidecars
#   - providers.tf: OAuth sources, forward auth, OIDC providers
#   - users.tf:     User management (SOPS-encrypted)
#   - outputs.tf:   All outputs
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Authentik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 203
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 4096  # Authentik recommended minimum
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 16
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "authentik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "authentik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only - Traefik handles external access)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.dashboards.authentik}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude .env template files (we generate .env from template)
  exclude_patterns = ["^\\.env"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Authentik"
  service_description = "Identity Provider - SSO, OIDC, and forward auth for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {
    admin    = "https://auth.${var.domain_internal}/if/admin/"
    user     = "https://auth.${var.domain_internal}/if/user/"
    direct   = "http://${local.ip_registry.dashboards.authentik}:9000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Authentik HTTP", port = 9000, info = "Web UI and API" },
    { name = "Authentik HTTPS", port = 9443, info = "HTTPS (self-signed)" },
    { name = "PostgreSQL", port = 5432, info = "Database (internal only)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Initial Setup

1. Access the admin interface at https://auth.${var.domain_internal}/if/admin/
2. Login with credentials from 1Password (item: authentik)
3. Configure Google OAuth source for SSO

## Forward Auth Endpoint

Add this middleware to Traefik routes for protected services:
```yaml
middlewares:
  authentik:
    forwardAuth:
      address: https://auth.${var.domain_public}/outpost.goauthentik.io/auth/traefik
      trustForwardHeader: true
      authResponseHeaders:
        - X-authentik-username
        - X-authentik-groups
        - X-authentik-email
        - X-authentik-name
        - X-authentik-uid
        - X-authentik-jwt
        - X-authentik-meta-jwks
        - X-authentik-meta-outpost
        - X-authentik-meta-provider
        - X-authentik-meta-app
        - X-authentik-meta-version
```

## Quick Commands

```bash
# View server logs
docker logs -f authentik-server

# View worker logs
docker logs -f authentik-worker

# Database backup
docker exec authentik-postgres pg_dump -U authentik authentik > backup.sql

# Restart services
cd /config && docker compose restart
```

## OIDC Configuration

For apps with native OIDC support, create a Provider in Authentik:
1. Admin → Providers → Create OAuth2/OIDC Provider
2. Set redirect URI for the app
3. Create Application linking to the provider
4. Use client_id and client_secret in the app config

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=authentik` to update.

}

  internal_domain = "auth.${var.domain_internal}"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "authentik_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.authentik.container_id
  container_ip   = module.authentik.ip_address
  container_name = "authentik"

content.text:
The issue is `user_matching_mode = "identifier"`. This requires users to have their Google account linked as an "identifier" in Authentik. But for first-time OAuth login, the user needs to be matched by email.

The fix is to change `user_matching_mode` to `"email_link"` - this will match users by email and automatically link the OAuth source to them on first login.

input.new_string:
# Match users by email and link OAuth source on first login
  # "email_link" matches by email and creates the link automatically
  user_matching_mode = "email_link"

  # Must be the root domain to work with both *.homelab.rambtech.dev and auth.rambtech.dev
  cookie_domain = var.domain_public
}

resource "authentik_application" "forward_auth" {
  name              = "Homelab Forward Auth"
  slug              = "homelab-forward-auth"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id

  meta_description = "Forward authentication for homelab services protected by Traefik"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab Infrastructure"

  # Open to all authenticated users
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# Update the embedded outpost to include the forward auth provider
# Note: The embedded outpost is managed by authentik, we just update its providers
resource "authentik_outpost" "embedded" {
  name               = "authentik Embedded Outpost"
  type               = "proxy"
  protocol_providers = [authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id]

  config = jsonencode({
    # Internal URL for outpost-to-authentik communication
    authentik_host          = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"
    # Browser URL - what users see (HTTPS via Cloudflare)
    authentik_host_browser  = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"
    authentik_host_insecure = false
    log_level               = "info"
  })

  lifecycle {
    # The embedded outpost already exists, we're just updating it
    ignore_changes = [service_connection]
  }
}

## Authentik Terraform Provider - Brand and Flow Customization

### Terraform Provider Overview
The Authentik Terraform Provider allows you to manage your Authentik instance with infrastructure as code.(no content)The provider's version is based on the authentik version it's tested against. For example, Provider version 2021.8.1 is tested against 2021.8.x.

### Flow Configuration
Users can decide if they already have everything they need with the default flows or if they want to create their own custom flow, using the Admin interface, Terraform, or via the API.(no content)A flow is a method of describing a sequence of stages. A stage represents a single verification or logic step. By connecting a series of stages within a flow (and optionally attaching policies as needed) you can build a highly flexible process for authenticating users, enrolling them, and more.

### Brand and Flow Relationship
To determine which flow should be used, authentik will first check which default authentication flow is configured in the active Brand. If no default is configured there, the policies in all flows with the matching designation are checked, and the first flow with matching policies sorted by slug will be used.

### Flow Customization Options
Since flows can be executed authenticated or unauthenticated, the default settings can be set via brands attributes. Configure the base color scheme. Defaults to automatic, which switches between dark and light mode based on the users' browsers' preference.

This overrides any default background image configured in the Branding settings.(no content)Alternatively, you can create a custom invalidation flow, with a branded background image.

### 2024 Updates
RBAC support for blueprints and Terraform: Permissions can now be assigned and automated using both blueprints and Terraform.(no content)Several resources in the Terraform provider have been renamed to align with new functionality. This mainly applies to property mapping-related resources. With the authentik version 2024.8.1 of the Terraform provider, both the old and new resources are available, and resources can be moved to the new name using terraform state mv.

### Provider Setup Example
Using version 2024.12.0 of the provider, rather than hardcoding credentials in your Terraform configuration (which would be a security risk), you can use environment variables to authenticate with Authentik using AUTHENTIK_URL and AUTHENTIK_TOKEN.(no content)The Authentik Terraform provider allows you to manage nearly all aspects of your Authentik configuration: Applications, Providers (OAuth2, SAML, LDAP, etc.), Sources (identity sources like social login providers), and Flows (create and customize authentication flows).

  consumer_key    = local.op.authentik_google_client_id

  # "email_link" matches by email and creates the link automatically
  user_matching_mode = "email_link"

  # Policy engine mode
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# NOTE: The Google source must be manually added to the identification stage

# =============================================================================
# Authentik Branding - Custom login page appearance
# =============================================================================
# Customizes the login page with:
#   - Custom title and logo
#   - Simplified login flow (Google OAuth focused)
#   - 7-day session duration
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Custom Brand Configuration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "authentik_brand" "homelab" {
  domain           = var.domain_public
  default          = true
  branding_title   = "Homelab"
  branding_favicon = "/static/dist/assets/icons/icon.png"
  branding_logo    = "/static/dist/assets/icons/icon_left_brand.svg"

  # Use custom authentication flow (Google OAuth focused)
  flow_authentication = authentik_flow.authentication.id
  flow_invalidation   = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Custom Authentication Flow - Google OAuth focused
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates a simplified authentication flow that shows Google login prominently

resource "authentik_flow" "authentication" {
  name               = "Homelab Authentication"
  title              = "Welcome to Homelab"
  slug               = "homelab-authentication"
  designation        = "authentication"
  policy_engine_mode = "any"

  # Use sidebar layout for cleaner appearance
  layout = "sidebar_right"

  # Custom background (optional - uses default if not set)
  # background = "/static/dist/assets/images/flow_background.jpg"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flow Stages
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Stage 1: Identification - Show login options
resource "authentik_stage_identification" "login" {
  name = "homelab-identification"

  user_fields = ["email"]  # Allow email-based identification

  # Show Google OAuth source on the identification page
  sources = [authentik_source_oauth.google.uuid]

  # Show password field for fallback (optional)
  password_stage = authentik_stage_password.password.id

  # Don't show "forgot password" for simplicity
  show_source_labels = true
}

# Stage 2: Password (for fallback local login)
resource "authentik_stage_password" "password" {
  name     = "homelab-password"
  backends = ["authentik.core.auth.InbuiltBackend"]
}

# Stage 3: User Login (creates session)
resource "authentik_stage_user_login" "login" {
  name                     = "homelab-user-login"
  session_duration         = "days=7"  # Stay logged in for 7 days
  remember_me_offset       = "days=30" # Remember me for 30 days
  terminate_other_sessions = false
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flow Stage Bindings - Connect stages to flow
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "authentik_flow_stage_binding" "identification" {
  target = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  stage  = authentik_stage_identification.login.id
  order  = 10
}

resource "authentik_flow_stage_binding" "password" {
  target = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  stage  = authentik_stage_password.password.id
  order  = 20
}

resource "authentik_flow_stage_binding" "user_login" {
  target = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  stage  = authentik_stage_user_login.login.id
  order  = 30
}

# =============================================================================
# Authentik Branding - Custom login page appearance
# =============================================================================
# Customizes the login page with:
#   - Custom title and logo
#   - Simplified login flow (Google OAuth focused)
#   - 7-day session duration
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Custom Brand Configuration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Import existing default brand and customize it
# Import with: tofu import authentik_brand.default authentik-default
resource "authentik_brand" "default" {
  domain           = "authentik-default"
  default          = true
  branding_title   = "Homelab"
  branding_favicon = "/static/dist/assets/icons/icon.png"
  branding_logo    = "/static/dist/assets/icons/icon_left_brand.svg"

  # Use custom authentication flow (Google OAuth focused)
  flow_authentication = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  flow_invalidation   = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Custom Authentication Flow - Google OAuth focused
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates a simplified authentication flow that shows Google login prominently

resource "authentik_flow" "authentication" {
  name               = "Homelab Authentication"
  title              = "Welcome to Homelab"
  slug               = "homelab-authentication"
  designation        = "authentication"
  policy_engine_mode = "any"

  # Use sidebar layout for cleaner appearance
  layout = "sidebar_right"

  # Custom background (optional - uses default if not set)
  # background = "/static/dist/assets/images/flow_background.jpg"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flow Stages
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Stage 1: Identification - Show login options
resource "authentik_stage_identification" "login" {
  name = "homelab-identification"

  user_fields = ["email"]  # Allow email-based identification

  # Show Google OAuth source on the identification page
  sources = [authentik_source_oauth.google.uuid]

  # Show password field for fallback (optional)
  password_stage = authentik_stage_password.password.id

  # Don't show "forgot password" for simplicity
  show_source_labels = true
}

# Stage 2: Password (for fallback local login)
resource "authentik_stage_password" "password" {
  name     = "homelab-password"
  backends = ["authentik.core.auth.InbuiltBackend"]
}

# Stage 3: User Login (creates session)
resource "authentik_stage_user_login" "login" {
  name                     = "homelab-user-login"
  session_duration         = "days=7"  # Stay logged in for 7 days
  remember_me_offset       = "days=30" # Remember me for 30 days
  terminate_other_sessions = false
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flow Stage Bindings - Connect stages to flow
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "authentik_flow_stage_binding" "identification" {
  target = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  stage  = authentik_stage_identification.login.id
  order  = 10
}

resource "authentik_flow_stage_binding" "password" {
  target = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  stage  = authentik_stage_password.password.id
  order  = 20
}

resource "authentik_flow_stage_binding" "user_login" {
  target = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  stage  = authentik_stage_user_login.login.id
  order  = 30
}

file.content:
# =============================================================================
# Authentik Branding - Custom login page appearance
# =============================================================================
# Customizes the login page with:
#   - Custom title and logo
#   - Simplified login flow (Google OAuth focused)
#   - 7-day session duration
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Custom Brand Configuration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Create brand for our public domain
# This brand will be used when accessing via auth.rambtech.dev
resource "authentik_brand" "homelab" {
  domain           = var.domain_public
  default          = false  # Don't conflict with authentik-default
  branding_title   = "Homelab"
  branding_favicon = "/static/dist/assets/icons/icon.png"
  branding_logo    = "/static/dist/assets/icons/icon_left_brand.svg"

  # Use custom authentication flow (Google OAuth focused)
  flow_authentication = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  flow_invalidation   = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Custom Authentication Flow - Google OAuth focused
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates a simplified authentication flow that shows Google login prominently

resource "authentik_flow" "authentication" {
  name               = "Homelab Authentication"
  title              = "Welcome to Homelab"
  slug               = "homelab-authentication"
  designation        = "authentication"
  policy_engine_mode = "any"

  # Use sidebar layout for cleaner appearance
  layout = "sidebar_right"

  # Custom background (optional - uses default if not set)
  # background = "/static/dist/assets/images/flow_background.jpg"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flow Stages
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Stage 1: Identification - Show login options
resource "authentik_stage_identification" "login" {
  name = "homelab-identification"

  user_fields = ["email"]  # Allow email-based identification

  # Show Google OAuth source on the identification page
  sources = [authentik_source_oauth.google.uuid]

  # Show password field for fallback (optional)
  password_stage = authentik_stage_password.password.id

  # Don't show "forgot password" for simplicity
  show_source_labels = true
}

# Stage 2: Password (for fallback local login)
resource "authentik_stage_password" "password" {
  name     = "homelab-password"
  backends = ["authentik.core.auth.InbuiltBackend"]
}

# Stage 3: User Login (creates session)
resource "authentik_stage_user_login" "login" {
  name                     = "homelab-user-login"
  session_duration         = "days=7"  # Stay logged in for 7 days
  remember_me_offset       = "days=30" # Remember me for 30 days
  terminate_other_sessions = false
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flow Stage Bindings - Connect stages to flow
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "authentik_flow_stage_binding" "identification" {
  target = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  stage  = authentik_stage_identification.login.id
  order  = 10
}

resource "authentik_flow_stage_binding" "password" {
  target = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  stage  = authentik_stage_password.password.id
  order  = 20
}

resource "authentik_flow_stage_binding" "user_login" {
  target = authentik_flow.authentication.uuid
  stage  = authentik_stage_user_login.login.id
  order  = 30
}

## Key Findings

### Automatic Redirect to OAuth Source
If you configure your identification stage to have no user field and only one source, it will redirect to it automatically. This is useful when you want to skip the login screen entirely and go directly to an external OAuth provider.

If you configure your identification stage to have no user field and only one source, it will redirect to it automatically. See PR #5583. There's also additional documentation at tekonline.com.au about "direct social authentication without login form."

### Common Redirect Issues

There are several known issues with authentik redirects:

1. The problem some users face is that when the user is returned after authenticating with an external provider and the configured Authentication Flow is triggered, the user isn't redirected to the application they requested to be authenticated for. Instead, they are directed to the Dashboard which isn't accessible to them, due to their nature as an external user.

2. When visiting an app behind domain level forward auth, authentik sometimes does the authentication but then redirects to the authentik main page (app overview) instead of the application originally wanted to visit.

### OAuth Provider Redirect URI Configuration
When using an OAuth 2.0 provider in authentik, the OP must validate the provided redirect URI by the RP. An authentik admin can configure a list in the Redirect URI field on the Provider.(no content)When you create a new OAuth 2.0 provider and app in authentik and you leave the Redirect URI field empty, then the first time a user opens that app, authentik uses that URL as the saved redirect URL.

### Logout Redirect Customization
When using an external type of account to perform the log-out function, authentik does not redirect back to the origin website. Users have asked how to set authentik to redirect after logout.

For more specific guidance on skipping loading pages or customizing post-authentication redirects, you may want to check the authentik documentation on Flows and Stages, or look into creating custom redirect stages in your authentication flow.

# Redirect Behavior in authentik Flows

Based on the documentation, here are the relevant settings for redirect behavior:

## Denied Action Setting

The flow configuration includes a **Denied action** option that controls redirect behavior when access is denied by a policy:

> "Configure what happens when access to a flow is denied by a policy. By default, authentik will redirect to a `?next` parameter if set, and otherwise show an error message."

The available options are:
- `MESSAGE_CONTINUE`: Display a message if no `?next` parameter exists; otherwise redirect
- `MESSAGE`: Always display error message
- `CONTINUE`: Always redirect to `?next` if available, otherwise to the default interface

## Redirect Stage

The documentation mentions a **Redirect stage** as an available component. One authentication option states that "the flow can only be started after being redirected by a [Redirect stage](/add-secure-apps/flows-stages/stages/redirect/)."

However, the provided content doesn't detail the Redirect stage's specific functionality or how it handles automatic redirects after authentication.

## Customizing Authentik Branding

### Accessing Brand Settings
To create or modify a brand, open the Admin interface and navigate to System > Brands.(no content)You can configure several differently "branded" options depending on the associated domain, even though objects such as applications, providers, etc, are still global. This can be handy to use the same authentik instance, but branded differently for different domains.

### Changing Logos and Icons
Changing the icons requires you to edit the docker-compose.yml to mount the new images. You can add volume mounts like:
- `./branding/brand_icon.png:/web/dist/assets/icons/icon_left_brand.png`
- `./branding/favicon.ico:/web/dist/assets/icons/favicon.ico`(no content)You can create a branding folder for example and put your branding images in there. Then you can restart Authentik and go to the admin interface > System > Brands location and edit authentik-default and update the new logos to the following location:
- logo: `/static/dist/assets/icons/icon_left_brand.png`
- favicon: `/static/dist/assets/icons/icon.png`

### Theme-Based Logo Support (2024.6.2+)
Starting with authentik 2024.6.2, the placeholder %(theme)s can be used in the logo configuration option, which will be replaced with the active theme.

### Known Issues
For brands in authentik, custom logos may be defined in the brand settings by providing a URL. Starting with authentik 2024.6.2, these URLs may contain the placeholder %(theme)s, which should be substituted with the currently active theme (light/dark) when used. This works for the most part, but not in some interfaces, like the 'Not Found' Screen.

### Additional Customization Options
Default flow background (authentik 2025.4.0+): Default background image for the flow executor, can be overridden per flow. Custom CSS (authentik 2025.4.0+): Add custom CSS to further customize the look of authentik.(no content)To change text in the login screen, go to admin interface > Flows and Stages > Flows and edit the default authentication flow with the edit button.(no content)When you use images and icons for a brand's logo, favicon, etc., be aware of the following optimization tips: Use an SVG version of the image. Trim excess whitespace from around the logo.

# Authentik - Identity Provider (SSO/OIDC)
# https://goauthentik.io/
#
# Version: 2025.10.3 (Redis removed, Postgres-only)

name: authentik

services:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # PostgreSQL Database
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  postgresql:
    image: docker.io/library/postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: authentik-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file:
      - .env
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${PG_DB:-authentik}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${PG_USER:-authentik}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${PG_PASS:?database password required}
    volumes:
      - database:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -d $${POSTGRES_DB} -U $${POSTGRES_USER}"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 20s

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Authentik Server (Web UI + API)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  server:
    image: ${AUTHENTIK_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/goauthentik/server}:${AUTHENTIK_TAG:-2025.10.3}
    container_name: authentik-server
    command: server
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      postgresql:
        condition: service_healthy
    env_file:
      - .env
    environment:
      AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__HOST: postgresql
      AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__NAME: ${PG_DB:-authentik}
      AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__USER: ${PG_USER:-authentik}
      AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__PASSWORD: ${PG_PASS}

# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Homepage API Keys
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "homepage" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "homepage"
}

locals {
  # Flatten all section fields from homepage item
  _homepage_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.homepage.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Homepage widget API keys
  homepage_env = {
    adguard_user   = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "adguard_user", "admin")
    adguard_pass   = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "adguard_pass", "")
    immich_key     = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "immich_key", "")
    jellyfin_key   = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "jellyfin_key", "")
    jellyseerr_key = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "jellyseerr_key", "")
    sonarr_key     = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "sonarr_key", "")
    radarr_key     = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "radarr_key", "")
    sabnzbd_key    = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "sabnzbd_key", "")
    qbit_user      = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "qbit_user", "admin")
    qbit_pass      = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "qbit_pass", "")
  }
}

# Generate the homepage.env file from 1Password secrets
resource "local_sensitive_file" "homepage_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/homepage.env"
  content  = <<-EOT
# Homepage Widget API Keys
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten

# AdGuard Home: Web UI credentials
HOMEPAGE_VAR_ADGUARD_USER=${local.homepage_env.adguard_user}
HOMEPAGE_VAR_ADGUARD_PASS=${local.homepage_env.adguard_pass}

# Immich: Account Settings > API Keys
HOMEPAGE_VAR_IMMICH_KEY=${local.homepage_env.immich_key}

# Jellyfin: Dashboard > API Keys
HOMEPAGE_VAR_JELLYFIN_KEY=${local.homepage_env.jellyfin_key}

# Jellyseerr: Settings > General
HOMEPAGE_VAR_JELLYSEERR_KEY=${local.homepage_env.jellyseerr_key}

# Sonarr: Settings > General
HOMEPAGE_VAR_SONARR_KEY=${local.homepage_env.sonarr_key}

# Radarr: Settings > General
HOMEPAGE_VAR_RADARR_KEY=${local.homepage_env.radarr_key}

# SABnzbd: Config > General
HOMEPAGE_VAR_SABNZBD_KEY=${local.homepage_env.sabnzbd_key}

# qBittorrent: Web UI credentials
HOMEPAGE_VAR_QBIT_USER=${local.homepage_env.qbit_user}
HOMEPAGE_VAR_QBIT_PASS=${local.homepage_env.qbit_pass}
EOT

  file_permission = "0600"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 201
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "swap" {
  type    = number
  default = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dashboards Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "dashboards" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "dashboards"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.dashboards.dashboards}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Ensure homepage.env is generated before file sync
  depends_on = [local_sensitive_file.homepage_env]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Dashboards"
  service_description = "Homepage and Dashy dashboard applications with system monitoring"

  service_urls = {
    homepage_internal = "https://homepage.${var.domain_internal}"
    dashy_internal    = "https://dashy.${var.domain_internal}"
    dashy_public      = "https://dashy.${var.domain_public}"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Homepage", port = 3000, info = "Main dashboard" },
    { name = "Dashy", port = 4001, info = "Alternative dashboard" },
    { name = "Glances", port = 61208, info = "System monitoring API" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f homepage
cd /config && docker compose logs -f dashy
```

**Restart services:**
```
cd /config && docker compose restart homepage
cd /config && docker compose restart dashy
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=dashboards` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["dashboards", "homepage", "dashy", "monitoring"]
}

# Homepage route (internal only)
module "homepage_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "homepage"
  backend_url = "http://${module.dashboards.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "homepage.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.dashboards]
}

# Dashy route (internal + public)
module "dashy_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "dashy"
  backend_url = "http://${module.dashboards.ip_address}:4001"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "dashy.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Public route (via Cloudflare tunnel)
  public_domain = "dashy.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.dashboards]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "dashboards_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.dashboards.container_id
  container_ip   = module.dashboards.ip_address
  container_name = "dashboards"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-201"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,dashboards"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["dashboards"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["dashboards"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.dashboards]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.dashboards.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.dashboards.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.dashboards.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    homepage_internal = module.homepage_route.internal_url
    dashy_internal    = module.dashy_route.internal_url
    dashy_public      = module.dashy_route.public_url
    direct_homepage   = "http://${module.dashboards.ip_address}:3000"
    direct_dashy      = "http://${module.dashboards.ip_address}:4001"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    homepage = module.homepage_route.remote_config_path
    dashy    = module.dashy_route.remote_config_path
  }

content.text:
You're right to ask, but actually no - we don't need separate app configurations for each service when using forward auth in **domain mode** (`forward_domain`).

Here's why:

The `authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth` we created uses `mode = "forward_domain"` with `cookie_domain = var.domain_public` (which is `rambtech.dev`). This means:

1. **One provider protects all subdomains** - The cookie is set on the root domain, so it works for `*.rambtech.dev` and `*.homelab.rambtech.dev`
2. **Single sign-on across all services** - Once you authenticate for Homepage, you're automatically authenticated for Dashy (and any other service using the `authentik` middleware)
3. **No per-app configuration needed** - The forward auth middleware just checks if you have a valid session cookie

This is different from OIDC/OAuth providers where each app needs its own client ID, redirect URI, etc.

The only thing each app needs is the `authentik` middleware added to its Traefik route - which we just did for Dashy.

Go ahead and test both URLs - you should see SSO working (login once, access both):
- `https://dashy.homelab.rambtech.dev/` (internal)
- `https://dashy.rambtech.dev/` (public via Cloudflare)

Description:
Complete migration from Authelia to Authentik as the centralized identity provider.

## Overview
Replace Authelia with Authentik to gain:
- Native Google/GitHub OAuth federation
- OIDC provider capabilities for apps with native SSO support
- Forward auth for apps without native OAuth
- Centralized user/group management
- Jellyfin SSO plugin compatibility

### Phase 1: Infrastructure
- Deploy Authentik alongside Traefik in LXC 200

- Homepage, Dashy, Pulse, Arcane, Stirling-PDF
- Prometheus, Alertmanager

### Phase 3: Media & Network Apps (Forward Auth)
- Uptime Kuma, qBittorrent
- Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, SABnzbd

### Phase 4: Native OIDC Apps
- Grafana, OpenWebUI, Paperless-ngx, n8n, Jellyseerr

### Phase 5: Media Apps (Native OIDC)
- Immich, Jellyfin

### Phase 6: Cleanup
- Decommission Authelia

# =============================================================================
# Documents LXC - Paperless-ngx + Stirling-PDF
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 504
# IP: 10.100.5.104
#
# Document management stack:
# - Paperless-ngx: OCR, full-text search, auto-tagging, email consumption
# - Stirling-PDF: PDF manipulation (merge, split, compress, convert, etc.)
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Paperless Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "paperless" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "paperless"
}

locals {
  # Flatten paperless section fields into a map by label
  _paperless_section_fields = merge([
    for s in try(data.onepassword_item.paperless.section, []) : {
      for f in try(s.field, []) : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  paperless = {
    admin_user     = try(data.onepassword_item.paperless.username, "admin")
    admin_password = try(data.onepassword_item.paperless.password, "")
    db_password    = lookup(local._paperless_section_fields, "db_password", "")
    secret_key     = lookup(local._paperless_section_fields, "secret_key", "")
  }
}

# Generate the .env file from 1Password secrets
resource "local_sensitive_file" "documents_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/.env"
  content  = <<-EOT
# Documents Stack Environment
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten

# Paperless-ngx
PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER=${local.paperless.admin_user}
PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${local.paperless.admin_password}
PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD=${local.paperless.db_password}
PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY=${local.paperless.secret_key}
EOT

  file_permission = "0600"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 504
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4  # OCR is CPU intensive
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 8192  # OCR needs memory
}

variable "swap" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64  # Documents can grow large
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Documents Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "documents" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "documents"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.documents}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Ensure .env is generated before file sync
  depends_on = [local_sensitive_file.documents_env]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Documents"
  service_description = "Document management with Paperless-ngx (OCR) and Stirling-PDF (utilities)"

  service_urls = {
    paperless_internal    = "https://docs.${var.domain_internal}"
    paperless_public      = "https://docs.${var.domain_public}"
    stirling_pdf_internal = "https://pdf.${var.domain_internal}"
    stirling_pdf_public   = "https://pdf.${var.domain_public}"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Paperless-ngx", port = 8000, info = "Document management with OCR" },
    { name = "Stirling-PDF", port = 8080, info = "PDF manipulation tools" },
    { name = "PostgreSQL", port = 5432, info = "Paperless database (internal)" },
    { name = "Redis", port = 6379, info = "Paperless cache (internal)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f paperless
cd /config && docker compose logs -f stirling-pdf
```

**Restart services:**
```
cd /config && docker compose restart paperless
cd /config && docker compose restart stirling-pdf
```

**Import documents:**
Place files in `/config/consume/` - they'll be automatically imported.

**Export all documents:**
```
cd /config && docker compose exec paperless document_exporter ../export/
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=documents` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["documents", "paperless", "pdf", "ocr"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "documents_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.documents.container_id
  container_ip   = module.documents.ip_address
  container_name = "documents"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-504"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "PostgreSQL dump (Paperless)"
      command = "docker exec paperless-db pg_dump -U paperless -d paperless --clean --if-exists | gzip > /config/paperless-db-backup.sql.gz"
      timeout = 300
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,documents,paperless"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["documents"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["documents"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.documents]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Paperless-ngx route (internal only)
module "paperless_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "docs"
  backend_url = "http://${module.documents.ip_address}:8000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "docs.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "docs.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - Authelia protected
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.documents]
}

# Stirling-PDF route (internal only)
module "stirling_pdf_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "pdf"
  backend_url = "http://${module.documents.ip_address}:8080"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "pdf.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "pdf.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - Loki + Alloy + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "Observability stack with Loki, Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana           = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus        = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager      = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma       = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"
    ntfy              = "https://ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct_loki       = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100"
    direct_alloy_grpc = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317"
    direct_alloy_http = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Loki", port = 3100, info = "Log aggregation" },
    { name = "Alloy (gRPC)", port = 4317, info = "OTLP gRPC receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy (HTTP)", port = 4318, info = "OTLP HTTP receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy UI", port = 12345, info = "Alloy debug UI" },
    { name = "Prometheus", port = 9090, info = "Metrics storage and alerting" },
    { name = "Grafana", port = 3000, info = "Dashboards and visualization" },
    { name = "Alertmanager", port = 9093, info = "Alert routing" },
    { name = "Uptime Kuma", port = 3001, info = "HTTP monitoring and status page" },
    { name = "ntfy", port = 8080, info = "Push notifications" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Alloy OTLP Endpoints (for Proxmox/Immich)

**OTLP gRPC:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317
**OTLP HTTP:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318

Configure Proxmox metrics server:
```bash
pvesh create /cluster/metrics/server \
  --id homelab-alloy \
  --type opentelemetry \
  --server ${local.lan_ips.monitoring} \
  --port 4317 \
  --proto grpc
```

## Loki Endpoint (for Alloy sidecars)

**Loki URL:** http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100

## Grafana

Default login: admin / (password in 1Password)

## ntfy Topics

- `homelab-alerts` - Prometheus alerts
- `homelab-status` - Uptime Kuma notifications

Subscribe via mobile app or web UI.

## Quick Commands

```bash
# View Alloy logs
docker logs -f alloy

# View Loki logs
docker logs -f loki

# Query logs via Loki API
curl -s "http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/labels" | jq

# Reload Prometheus config
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/-/reload

# Test ntfy notification
curl -d "Test notification" http://localhost:8080/homelab-alerts
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=monitoring` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["monitoring", "loki", "alloy", "prometheus", "grafana"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "monitoring_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    grafana_admin_password = local.op.grafana_admin_password
    uptime_kuma_username   = local.op.uptime_kuma_username
    uptime_kuma_password   = local.op.uptime_kuma_password
    discord_webhook_url    = local.op.discord_webhook_url
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/monitoring.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "monitoring_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.monitoring_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.monitoring.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "grafana_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "grafana"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "grafana.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "prometheus_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "prometheus"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9090"

  internal_domain = "prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "alertmanager_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "alertmanager"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9093"

  internal_domain = "alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "uptime_kuma_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "status"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3001"

  internal_domain = "status.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "ntfy_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "ntfy"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:8080"

  internal_domain = "ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.monitoring.container_id
  container_ip   = module.monitoring.ip_address
  container_name = "monitoring"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-500"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,monitoring"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["monitoring"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["monitoring"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.monitoring.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.monitoring.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.monitoring.ssh_command
}

output "alloy_endpoints" {
  value = {
    grpc = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4317"
    http = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4318"
  }

# =============================================================================
# Traefik LXC - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 200
#
# This deployment uses the docker-lxc module which handles:
#   1. LXC container creation with Docker pre-installed
#   2. File sync via rsync (file-sync module)
#   3. Docker Compose deployment
#   4. Proxmox notes generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# App-specific Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Traefik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 200
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 2048
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 8
}

variable "rootfs_storage" {
  description = "Storage pool for root filesystem"
  type        = string
  default     = "nvme-containers"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "traefik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "traefik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for external access)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.traefik}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # MUST be privileged for binding to ports 80/443
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude migrated routes (managed by traefik-route module), env templates, and .tpl files
  exclude_patterns = ["^migrated-dynamic/", "^\\.env", "\\.tpl$"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Traefik"
  service_description = "Reverse proxy and ingress controller for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
    direct             = "http://${local.traefik_ip}:8080/dashboard/"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "HTTP", port = 80, info = "HTTP entrypoint (redirects to HTTPS)" },
    { name = "HTTPS", port = 443, info = "HTTPS entrypoint with Let's Encrypt" },
    { name = "Metrics", port = 8082, info = "Prometheus metrics endpoint" }
  ]

  custom_notes = file("${path.module}/notes.md")

  tags = ["traefik", "ingress", "reverse-proxy"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "traefik_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    cf_api_token = local.op.cloudflare_api_token
    cf_api_email = local.op.cloudflare_email
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/traefik.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "traefik_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.traefik_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = local.traefik_ip

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.traefik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Alloy Auth Middleware (for Loki/Prometheus push endpoints)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates authenticated endpoints for Alloy agents to push logs and metrics

resource "local_sensitive_file" "alloy_auth_config" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/dynamic/alloy-auth.yml.tpl", {
    htpasswd      = local.op.alloy_telemetry_htpasswd
    domain        = var.domain_internal
    monitoring_ip = local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/alloy-auth.yml"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "alloy_auth_config" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.alloy_auth_config.filename
  destination = "/config/dynamic/alloy-auth.yml"
  host        = local.traefik_ip

  mode = "0644"

  depends_on = [module.traefik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "traefik_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.traefik.container_id
  container_ip   = module.traefik.ip_address
  container_name = "traefik"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-200"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/config/acme.json", "/config/logs/**"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,traefik"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["traefik"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["traefik"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.traefik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.traefik.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.traefik.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.traefik.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
  }
}
