# - Stirling-PDF: PDF manipulation (merge, split, compress, convert, etc.)
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Paperless Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "paperless" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "paperless"
}

locals {
  # Flatten paperless section fields into a map by label
  _paperless_section_fields = merge([
    for s in try(data.onepassword_item.paperless.section, []) : {
      for f in try(s.field, []) : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  paperless = {
    admin_user     = try(data.onepassword_item.paperless.username, "admin")
    admin_password = try(data.onepassword_item.paperless.password, "")
    db_password    = lookup(local._paperless_section_fields, "db_password", "")
    secret_key     = lookup(local._paperless_section_fields, "secret_key", "")
  }
}

# Generate the .env file from 1Password secrets
resource "local_sensitive_file" "documents_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/.env"
  content  = <<-EOT
# Documents Stack Environment
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten

# Paperless-ngx
PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER=${local.paperless.admin_user}
PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${local.paperless.admin_password}
PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD=${local.paperless.db_password}
PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY=${local.paperless.secret_key}
EOT

  file_permission = "0600"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 504
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4  # OCR is CPU intensive
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 8192  # OCR needs memory
}

variable "swap" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64  # Documents can grow large
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Documents Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "documents" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "documents"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.documents}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Ensure .env is generated before file sync
  depends_on = [local_sensitive_file.documents_env]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Documents"
  service_description = "Document management with Paperless-ngx (OCR) and Stirling-PDF (utilities)"

  service_urls = {
    paperless_internal    = "https://docs.${var.domain_internal}"
    paperless_public      = "https://docs.${var.domain_public}"
    stirling_pdf_internal = "https://pdf.${var.domain_internal}"
    stirling_pdf_public   = "https://pdf.${var.domain_public}"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Paperless-ngx", port = 8000, info = "Document management with OCR" },
    { name = "Stirling-PDF", port = 8080, info = "PDF manipulation tools" },
    { name = "PostgreSQL", port = 5432, info = "Paperless database (internal)" },
    { name = "Redis", port = 6379, info = "Paperless cache (internal)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f paperless
cd /config && docker compose logs -f stirling-pdf
```

**Restart services:**
```
cd /config && docker compose restart paperless
cd /config && docker compose restart stirling-pdf
```

**Import documents:**
Place files in `/config/consume/` - they'll be automatically imported.

**Export all documents:**
```
cd /config && docker compose exec paperless document_exporter ../export/
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=documents` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["documents", "paperless", "pdf", "ocr"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "documents_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.documents.container_id
  container_ip   = module.documents.ip_address
  container_name = "documents"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-504"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "PostgreSQL dump (Paperless)"
      command = "docker exec paperless-db pg_dump -U paperless -d paperless --clean --if-exists | gzip > /config/paperless-db-backup.sql.gz"
      timeout = 300
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,documents,paperless"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["documents"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["documents"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.documents]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Paperless-ngx route (internal only)
module "paperless_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "docs"
  backend_url = "http://${module.documents.ip_address}:8000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "docs.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "docs.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - Authelia protected
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.documents]
}

# Stirling-PDF route (internal only)
module "stirling_pdf_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "pdf"
  backend_url = "http://${module.documents.ip_address}:8080"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "pdf.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "pdf.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - Authelia protected
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authelia"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.documents]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.documents.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.documents.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.documents.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    direct_paperless      = "http://${module.documents.ip_address}:8000"
    paperless_internal    = module.paperless_route.internal_url
    paperless_public      = module.paperless_route.public_url

    direct_stirling_pdf   = "http://${module.documents.ip_address}:8080"
    stirling_pdf_internal = module.stirling_pdf_route.internal_url
    stirling_pdf_public   = module.stirling_pdf_route.public_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    paperless    = module.paperless_route.remote_config_path
    stirling_pdf = module.stirling_pdf_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

module "monitoring_sidecars" {

Based on my search, here's what I found about authentik application access control, policy groups, and restricting users per application:

## Key Findings on authentik Access Control

### Application Access with Policy Bindings
Application access can be configured using (Policy) Bindings. Click on an application in the applications list, and select the Policy / Group / User Bindings tab. There you can bind users/groups/policies to grant them access. When nothing is bound, everyone has access.

### Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
In authentik, they provide role-based access control (RBAC), an industry standard for managing access control. By carefully designing roles with appropriate permissions, and then assigning those roles to groups, RBAC provides a fine-tuned approach to controlling user access.

### Entitlements (2024.12 Feature)
Application entitlements can be used through authentik to manage authorization within an application (what areas of the app users or groups can access). Entitlements are scoped to a single application and can be bound to multiple users and/or groups (binding policies is not currently supported), giving them access to the entitlement. An application can either check for the name of the entitlement (via the entitlements scope), or via attributes stored in entitlements.

### 2024.12 Release Improvements
In the application creation wizard, administrators can now configure bindings for an application while they are creating the new app and its provider. This streamlined approach allows you to create bindings to specific policies, or specific users or groups (these bindings determine who and how the application is accessed), while in the workflow of the Wizard instead of needing to separately configure the bindings.

### Groups and Permissions Management
You can assign a role to a group, and then all users in the group inherit the permissions assigned to that role.

### Important Note on Permissions
Global and object permissions only apply to objects within authentik, and not to who can access certain applications (which are access-controlled using policies).

### Backchannel Provider Access Restrictions
Any access restrictions that are configured on an application apply to all of its backchannel providers.

input.prompt: Explain how to restrict which users can access an application using policy bindings, groups, and users. Show the specific steps to limit access.

content.content:
# Restricting Application Access with Policy Bindings

To limit who can access an application in authentik, follow these steps:

1. **Navigate to the application**: Go to **Applications > Applications** and select the specific app you want to restrict.

2. **Access bindings**: Click the **Policy/Group/User Bindings** tab.

3. **Create restrictions**: The documentation explains that "when nothing is bound, everyone has access. Binding a policy restricts access to specific Users or Groups, or by other custom policies."

4. **Configure access rules**: You can bind:
   - Individual users
   - Groups
   - Custom policies (such as time-of-day or geographic restrictions)

5. **Set the policy engine mode**: When multiple bindings exist, choose between:
   - **ALL**: Users must satisfy every binding requirement
   - **ANY**: Users need to satisfy at least one binding

**Key principle**: By default, all users can access applications when no policies are bound. Once you add any bindings, access becomes restricted to only those who meet your specified criteria, providing granular control over application visibility and availability.

Based on my search results, here's what I found about authentik forward auth proxy provider with group policy binding restriction using Terraform:

## Forward Auth Proxy Provider in Authentik

Using forward auth uses your existing reverse proxy to do the proxying, and only uses the authentik outpost to check authentication and authorization.

### Forward Auth Modes

There are two main modes:

1. **Forward auth (single application)**: Single application mode works for a single application hosted on its dedicated subdomain. This has the advantage that you can still do per-application access policies in authentik.

2. **Forward auth (domain level)**: Forward domain mode authenticates at the domain level, allowing users to access all applications on the same domain after a single login.(no content)However, there are some downsides, mainly the fact that you can't restrict individual applications to different users.

## Restricting Access with Policy Bindings

Authorization Application access can be configured using (Policy) Bindings. Click on an application in the applications list, and select the Policy / Group / User Bindings tab. There you can bind users/groups/policies to grant them access.

## Terraform Configuration

### Basic Proxy Provider Example

Lookup flows used by the provider via data resources, then create the proxy provider:

```hcl
data "authentik_flow" "default-authorization-flow" {
  slug = "default-provider-authorization-implicit-consent"
}

resource "authentik_provider_proxy" "name" {
  name               = "test-app"
  mode               = "forward_single"  # or "forward_domain"
  external_host      = "https://app.example.com"
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default-authorization-flow.id
}

resource "authentik_application" "name" {
  name              = "test-app"
  slug              = "test-app"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_proxy.name.id
}
```

### Adding Policy Binding for Group Restriction

To restrict access to a specific group, you would use `authentik_policy_binding` resource. Based on the Terraform provider pattern, you would create something like:

```hcl
resource "authentik_policy_binding" "app_group_access" {
  target = authentik_application.name.uuid
  group  = authentik_group.your_group.id
  order  = 0
}
```

## Managing the Embedded Outpost

A challenge when using Terraform is that the embedded outpost already exists within Authentik, but Terraform doesn't know about it. To manage it with Terraform, you need to import the existing resource.(no content)You can use the import block in Terraform to import existing resources:
```hcl
import {
  id = "8e7ee1c7-e3d1-4198-aa41-a6b60bf0e2db"  # Your actual outpost ID
  to = authentik_outpost.embedded
}
```

## Additional Notes

RBAC support for blueprints and Terraform allows permissions to be assigned and automated using both blueprints and Terraform.(no content)RBAC permissions for global/object level permissions for users/roles can now be managed via blueprints and Terraform. This allows for the automatic configuration of permissions.

For the most up-to-date Terraform resource documentation for `authentik_policy_binding`, I recommend checking the official Terraform registry at https://registry.terraform.io/providers/goauthentik/authentik/latest/docs/resources/policy_binding.

content.text:
Here's what I found about restricting access per-application in Authentik:

## The Challenge with Domain-Level Forward Auth

We're currently using **`forward_domain` mode**, which has a limitation: according to the [Forward Auth docs](https://docs.goauthentik.io/add-secure-apps/providers/proxy/), domain-level forward auth authenticates at the domain level, meaning you **can't restrict individual applications to different users** with this mode.

## Two Approaches for Per-App Access Control

### Option 1: Switch to `forward_single` Mode (Per-App)
Create a **separate proxy provider for each app** that needs different access:

```hcl
# Public apps - accessible to all authenticated users
resource "authentik_provider_proxy" "public_apps" {
  name               = "Public Apps Forward Auth"
  mode               = "forward_single"
  external_host      = "https://dashy.rambtech.dev"
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
}

# Internal apps - restricted to admin group
resource "authentik_provider_proxy" "internal_apps" {
  name               = "Internal Apps Forward Auth"  
  mode               = "forward_single"
  external_host      = "https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev"
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
}

resource "authentik_application" "internal_apps" {
  name              = "Internal Apps"
  slug              = "internal-apps"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_proxy.internal_apps.id
}

# Bind to admin group only
resource "authentik_policy_binding" "internal_admin_only" {
  target = authentik_application.internal_apps.uuid
  group  = authentik_group.admins.id
  order  = 0
}
```

**Downsides**: Requires a separate Traefik middleware per provider, more complex config.

### Option 2: Use Groups + Policy Bindings on Domain Provider
Keep domain mode but use **groups** to control access. Create an application binding:

```hcl
# Create groups
resource "authentik_group" "internal_users" {
  name = "internal-users"
}

resource "authentik_group" "public_users" {
  name = "public-users"
}

# Bind the forward auth app to internal users only
resource "authentik_policy_binding" "forward_auth_internal" {
  target = authentik_application.forward_auth.uuid
  group  = authentik_group.internal_users.id
  order  = 0
}
```

**Downside**: This restricts ALL apps behind forward auth, not individual ones.

### Option 3: Hybrid Approach (Recommended)
Use **two separate forward auth providers**:

1. **Internal forward auth** (`forward_domain` on `homelab.rambtech.dev`)
   - Bound to `internal-users` group
   - Used for Prometheus, Alertmanager, Traefik, etc.

2. **Public forward auth** (`forward_domain` on `rambtech.dev`)
   - Bound to `all-users` group (or no binding = everyone)
   - Used for Dashy, Homepage public routes

This requires two different middleware configurations in Traefik and two outpost configurations.

## Quick Win: Add Users to Groups via SOPS

For now, you could add a `groups` field to your users in `users.sops.yaml`:

```yaml
authentik_users:
  darshan:
    email: darshan@example.com
    name: Darshan
    groups:
      - internal-users
      - admins
  guest_user:
    email: guest@example.com
    name: Guest
    groups:
      - public-users
```

Would you like me to implement Option 3 (separate internal/public forward auth providers)?

Sources:
- [Manage applications | authentik](https://docs.goauthentik.io/add-secure-apps/applications/manage_apps/)
- [Forward auth | authentik](https://docs.goauthentik.io/add-secure-apps/providers/proxy/)
- [authentik_policy_binding | Terraform Registry](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/goauthentik/authentik/latest/docs/resources/policy_binding)

## Forward Auth vs Native OIDC/SSO

**Forward Auth (what we just configured):**
- For apps with **no built-in auth** - Stirling-PDF, Prometheus, Alertmanager, ntfy, Traefik Dashboard
- Traefik intercepts requests, redirects to Authentik, then passes through if authenticated

- For apps **with built-in SSO support** - Immich, Jellyfin, Grafana, etc.
- App directly communicates with Authentik via OIDC protocol
- Users appear in the app, can have roles/permissions within the app
- Better user experience (no redirect dance, deeper integration)

## Apps by Integration Type

| App | Integration | Status |
|-----|-------------|--------|
| **Immich** | Native OIDC | Needs Authentik provider setup |
| **Jellyfin** | Native SSO plugin | Needs Authentik provider setup |
| **Grafana** | Native OIDC | Needs Authentik provider setup |
| **Paperless-ngx** | Native OIDC | Needs Authentik provider setup |
| **n8n** | Native OIDC | Needs Authentik provider setup |
| **Sonarr/Radarr/etc** | Forward Auth | API keys internal, forward auth for UI |
| **Uptime Kuma** | Forward Auth or disable built-in | Needs investigation |

content.text:
Correct! For apps with **native OIDC/SSO integration**, access control is handled **within Authentik's application config**, not through forward auth at all.

## How Native OIDC Access Control Works

When you create an **OAuth2/OpenID Provider application** in Authentik (for Immich, Jellyfin, Grafana, etc.):

1. **Application** - Defines the OIDC client (client_id, redirect_uri, etc.)
2. **Policy Bindings** - Attach directly to the application to control who can access it

```hcl
# Example: Immich OIDC application with restricted access
resource "authentik_application" "immich" {
  name              = "Immich"
  slug              = "immich"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.id
  
  # Policy bindings control access
  # Only users in "family" group can use this app
}

resource "authentik_policy_binding" "immich_family_only" {
  target = authentik_application.immich.uuid
  group  = authentik_group.family.id
  order  = 0
}
```

## Summary

| Integration Type | Access Control Location |
|------------------|------------------------|
| **Forward Auth** | Traefik middleware → Forward Auth Provider → Policy Bindings |
| **Native OIDC** | Authentik Application → Policy Bindings (directly on app) |

So for Immich/Jellyfin/Grafana, you'd:
1. Create the OAuth2 provider + application in Authentik
2. Bind policies directly to that application (groups, user restrictions, etc.)
3. No forward auth middleware involved at all

The hybrid approach (Option 3) only applies to forward auth scenarios. Native OIDC apps have built-in per-app access control through Authentik's application policy bindings.

content.text:
Yes! Groups work across both solutions. Here's how:

## Groups as the Common Layer

```
Authentik Groups
├── internal-users (family, trusted)
└── public-users (extended family, friends)
```

## Linking Groups to Each Solution

### 1. Native OIDC Apps (Immich, Jellyfin, Grafana)

Policy bindings directly on the application:

```hcl
# Immich - internal users only
resource "authentik_policy_binding" "immich_access" {
  target = authentik_application.immich.uuid
  group  = authentik_group.internal_users.id
  order  = 0
}

# Jellyfin - both internal and public users
resource "authentik_policy_binding" "jellyfin_internal" {
  target = authentik_application.jellyfin.uuid
  group  = authentik_group.internal_users.id
  order  = 0
}

resource "authentik_policy_binding" "jellyfin_public" {
  target = authentik_application.jellyfin.uuid
  group  = authentik_group.public_users.id
  order  = 1
}
```

### 2. Forward Auth Apps (Prometheus, ntfy, etc.)

Policy bindings on the **Forward Auth Application** (the proxy provider):

```hcl
# Forward auth app - restrict to internal users only
resource "authentik_policy_binding" "forward_auth_access" {
  target = authentik_application.forward_auth.uuid
  group  = authentik_group.internal_users.id
  order  = 0
}
```

**Limitation**: With single forward auth provider, ALL forward auth apps get same access. To differentiate, you'd need separate forward auth providers (one for internal, one for public).

## Summary

| Aspect | Native OIDC | Forward Auth |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| Group binding location | Per-application | Per-provider (shared across apps) |
| Granularity | Per-app control | All apps behind provider share access |
| Solution for differentiation | Built-in | Multiple forward auth providers |

So yes, **same groups** can be used for both - they're just bound at different levels (application vs provider).

content.text:
Good question. There are two approaches:

## Option A: Centralized in `tofu/apps/authentik/`

```
tofu/apps/authentik/
├── main.tf           # Authentik LXC container
├── providers.tf      # Authentik + Google OAuth source
├── branding.tf       # Custom login flow
├── forward-auth.tf   # Forward auth provider
├── apps/
│   ├── immich.tf     # Immich OIDC provider + application
│   ├── jellyfin.tf   # Jellyfin OIDC provider + application
│   └── grafana.tf    # Grafana OIDC provider + application
```

**Pros**: All identity config in one place, easy to see all apps, single state
**Cons**: Authentik app needs to know about all other apps, coupling

## Option B: Distributed in each app (Recommended)

```
tofu/apps/immich/
├── main.tf           # Immich LXC + Docker
├── authentik.tf      # Immich's OIDC provider + application in Authentik

tofu/apps/jellyfin/
├── main.tf           # Jellyfin LXC + Docker
├── authentik.tf      # Jellyfin's OIDC provider + application
```

**Pros**: 
- App owns its own auth config (self-contained)
- Deploying immich also sets up its Authentik integration
- No coupling - authentik app doesn't need to change when adding new apps
- Matches your existing pattern (apps own their traefik-route config)

**Cons**: Auth config spread across apps (but that's the point - ownership)

---

**Recommendation**: Option B - it follows the same pattern you use for `traefik-route` where each app owns its routing config. Each app would own its Authentik integration too.

# =============================================================================
# Immich LXC - Photo & Video Management
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 304
#
# Self-hosted photo and video management with ML features and GPU acceleration.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file with Immich credentials
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "local_sensitive_file" "immich_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/.env"
  content  = <<-EOT
# Immich Configuration
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten
# https://immich.app/docs/install/environment-variables

# Paths - these match the LXC mount points from main.tf
UPLOAD_LOCATION=/photos
DB_DATA_LOCATION=/var/lib/postgresql/data

# Version - use 'release' for latest stable
IMMICH_VERSION=release

# Database credentials
DB_PASSWORD=qjIYvd2gOMh71CBpgA
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_DATABASE_NAME=immich

# Timezone
TZ=America/New_York

# OpenTelemetry - push metrics to monitoring stack
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://10.100.5.100:4318
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=immich
IMMICH_TELEMETRY_INCLUDE=all
EOT

  file_permission = "0600"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 304
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 6
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 6144
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "immich" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "immich-docker"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for mobile app)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.photos.immich}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.immich}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Enable AMD GPU passthrough for ML acceleration and video transcoding
  enable_gpu = true

  # Mount points for photos and cache
  # These are configured via SSH (null_resource.configure_mount_points) since
  # the API token doesn't have permission for bind mounts (requires root@pam)
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      path   = "/photos"
      volume = "/tank/photos"
    },
    {
      slot   = 1
      path   = "/cache"
      volume = "/tank/cache/immich"
    }
  ]

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Immich"
  service_description = "Self-hosted photo and video management with ML features"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}"
    public   = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.immich}:2283"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Immich Web", port = 2283, info = "Photo management UI" },
    { name = "Immich Server", port = 2283, info = "API server" },
    { name = "Immich ML", port = 3003, info = "Machine learning service" },
    { name = "PostgreSQL", port = 5432, info = "Database" },
    { name = "Redis", port = 6379, info = "Cache" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Storage

**Photos:** `/photos` (mounted from `/tank/photos`)
**Cache:** `/cache` (mounted from `/tank/cache/immich`)
**Database:** Docker volumes (immich_pgdata)

## GPU Acceleration

AMD Radeon 890M passed through for ML acceleration:
- `/dev/dri/card0` - GPU device
- `/dev/dri/renderD128` - Render device

**Check GPU access:**
```bash
ls -la /dev/dri/
docker exec immich_machine_learning rocminfo
```

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose logs -f immich_server
```

**Restart all services:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose restart
```

**Force reprocess ML jobs:**
```bash
docker exec -it immich_server npm run cli -- jobs run all
```

## Database Backup

Backup script runs pre-backup hook for Proxmox vzdump.
Manual backup:
```bash
cd /config && docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dumpall -U postgres > backup.sql
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=immich` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["photos", "immich", "media"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "immich_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.immich.container_id
  container_ip   = module.immich.ip_address
  container_name = "immich-docker"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-304"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "PostgreSQL dump"
      command = "docker exec immich_postgres pg_dump -U postgres -d immich --clean --if-exists | gzip > /config/immich-db-backup.sql.gz"
      timeout = 600
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2", "/cache/**"]

    ntfy_priority = "high"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,immich,rotating_light"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["immich"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["immich"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.immich]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "immich_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "photos"
  backend_url = "http://${module.immich.ip_address}:2283"

  internal_domain = "photos.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "photos.${var.domain_public}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [module.immich]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.immich.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.immich.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.immich.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    internal = module.immich_route.internal_url
    public   = module.immich_route.public_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  value = module.immich_route.remote_config_path
}

# Immich - Self-hosted photo and video management
# https://immich.app/docs/install/docker-compose
# Updated: 2025-12 based on official v1.123+ config

name: immich

services:
  immich-server:
    container_name: immich_server
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    # Hardware transcoding: VAAPI for AMD GPU
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    volumes:
      - ${UPLOAD_LOCATION}:/usr/src/app/upload
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
    env_file:
      - .env
    ports:
      - 2283:2283
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - database
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '4.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  immich-machine-learning:
    container_name: immich_machine_learning
    # Using CPU image since AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) needs ROCm 6.4.4+
    # Immich ROCm image only has 6.3.4
    # Change to :release-rocm if/when Immich updates ROCm version
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learning:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    # Uncomment below and change image tag to :release-rocm when ROCm 6.4.4+ is available
    # devices:
    #   - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    #   - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
    # group_add:
    #   - video
    #   - render
    volumes:
      - model-cache:/cache
    env_file:
      - .env
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '4.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  redis:
    container_name: immich_redis
    image: docker.io/valkey/valkey:8-bookworm
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: valkey-cli ping || exit 1
    restart: unless-stopped

  database:
    container_name: immich_postgres
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_DATABASE_NAME}
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: '--data-checksums'
    volumes:
      - ${DB_DATA_LOCATION}:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    shm_size: 128mb
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    healthcheck:
      test: >-
        pg_isready --dbname="$${POSTGRES_DB}" --username="$${POSTGRES_USER}" || exit
        1; Chksum="$$(psql --dbname="$${POSTGRES_DB}" --username="$${POSTGRES_USER}"
        --tuples-only --no-align --command='SELECT COALESCE(SUM(googlechecksum(googlechecksum(tableoid,
        entity_id))), 0) FROM entity WHERE NOT is_external')"; Prev="$$(cat
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum 2>/dev/null || echo '')"; echo "$${Chksum}" >
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum; test "$${Prev}" = '' -o "$${Prev}" = "$${Chksum}"
      interval: 5m
      start_interval: 30s
      start_period: 5m
    command:
      [
        'postgres',
        '-c',
        'shared_preload_libraries=vchord.so,vectors.so',
        '-c',
        'search_path="$$user", public, vectors',
        '-c',
        'logging_collector=on',
        '-c',
        'max_wal_size=2GB',
        '-c',
        'shared_buffers=512MB',
        '-c',
        'wal_compression=on',
      ]
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  model-cache:

# =============================================================================
# Authentik Providers - OAuth Sources, Forward Auth, OIDC Providers
# =============================================================================
# This file contains all Authentik provider configurations:
#   - Google OAuth source (SSO via Google)
#   - Forward auth provider for Traefik
#   - OIDC providers for apps with native SSO support (future)
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Terraform API Token - Non-expiring
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates a non-expiring API token for Terraform to manage authentik.
# The token value is stored in 1Password and used by the provider.
#
# Bootstrap: Create a short-lived token in UI first, run tofu apply,
# then update 1Password with the new token value from the output.

data "authentik_user" "akadmin" {
  username = "akadmin"
}

resource "authentik_token" "terraform" {
  identifier   = "terraform-api"
  user         = data.authentik_user.akadmin.id
  intent       = "api"
  expiring     = false  # Never expires
  description  = "API token for OpenTofu/Terraform - managed by IaC"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Google OAuth Source - SSO via Google Account
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Allows users to login with their Google account
# Credentials stored in 1Password (authentik item)

data "authentik_flow" "default_source_authentication" {
  slug = "default-source-authentication"
}

resource "authentik_source_oauth" "google" {
  name                = "Google"
  slug                = "google"
  authentication_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_source_authentication.id

  # No enrollment flow - users must be pre-created in authentik
  # This prevents unauthorized users from self-registering
  enrollment_flow = ""

  provider_type   = "google"
  consumer_key    = local.op.authentik_google_client_id
  consumer_secret = local.op.authentik_google_client_secret

  # Match users by email and link OAuth source on first login
  # "email_link" matches by email and creates the link automatically
  user_matching_mode = "email_link"

  # Policy engine mode
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Link Google OAuth to Login Flow
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# NOTE: The Google source must be manually added to the identification stage
# in the authentik admin UI:
#   1. Go to Flows & Stages → Stages
#   2. Edit "default-authentication-identification"
#   3. Add "Google" to the Sources field
#   4. Save
#
# This is required because the stage already exists and can't be recreated
# via Terraform without importing it first.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Forward Auth Provider - For protecting services via Traefik
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates a Proxy Provider in forward auth mode for protecting services
# that don't have native OIDC support. The embedded outpost handles the auth.

data "authentik_flow" "default_authorization" {
  slug = "default-provider-authorization-implicit-consent"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_invalidation" {
  slug = "default-provider-invalidation-flow"
}

resource "authentik_provider_proxy" "forward_auth" {
  name               = "Traefik Forward Auth"
  mode               = "forward_domain"  # Domain mode - protects all subdomains
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
  invalidation_flow  = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id

  # External host - the authentik outpost's external URL for browser redirects
  external_host = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"

  # Cookie settings for SSO across all subdomains
  # Must be the root domain to work with both *.homelab.rambtech.dev and auth.rambtech.dev
  cookie_domain = var.domain_public
}

resource "authentik_application" "forward_auth" {
  name              = "Homelab Forward Auth"
  slug              = "homelab-forward-auth"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id

  meta_description = "Forward authentication for homelab services protected by Traefik"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab Infrastructure"

  # Open to all authenticated users
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# Update the embedded outpost to include the forward auth provider
# Note: The embedded outpost is managed by authentik, we just update its providers
resource "authentik_outpost" "embedded" {
  name               = "authentik Embedded Outpost"
  type               = "proxy"
  protocol_providers = [authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id]

  config = jsonencode({
    # Internal URL for outpost-to-authentik communication
    authentik_host          = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"
    # Browser URL - what users see (HTTPS via Cloudflare)
    authentik_host_browser  = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"
    authentik_host_insecure = false
    log_level               = "info"
  })

  lifecycle {
    # The embedded outpost already exists, we're just updating it
    ignore_changes = [service_connection]
  }
}

Based on my search results, here's what I found about Immich OIDC/OAuth configuration and environment variables:

## Immich OAuth/OIDC Configuration

Immich supports 3rd party authentication via OpenID Connect (OIDC), an identity layer built on top of OAuth2. OIDC is supported by most identity providers. Before enabling OAuth in Immich, a new client application needs to be configured in the 3rd-party authentication server.

### Configuration Method

Once you have a new OAuth client application configured, Immich can be configured using the Administration Settings page, available on the web (Administration -> Settings).(no content)To configure Immich there is one method, using the Web GUI. To configure Immich to utilize Authelia as an OpenID Connect 1.0 Provider, use the following instructions: Login to Immich.

### Environment Variables for OAuth - Current Status

Immich doesn't have an option for that at the moment. Personally I use https://github.com/getsops/sops to encrypt secrets and store them in my homelab git repo.(no content)Some config values, like oauth.clientSecret or smtp.password are sensitive. It would be nice to provide these values using environment variables. That will be useful for declarative Immich setup using gitops.(no content)Because those values are at different levels. DB and redis are required for Immich to start up, OAuth isn't.

### Workarounds

You could use something like envsubst to replace placeholders in the config json, or jq to merge multiple partial config json files, etc.(no content)I use an init container to run envsubst on the config file from the readonly configmap. It outputs the result in an emptyDir volume mounted by both init and main containers. The "templated" configmap is the one I provide to immich main container with the IMMICH_CONFIG_FILE env var.

### Required Redirect URIs

Redirect URIs should contain all the domains you will be using to access Immich. Some examples include: app.immich:///oauth-callback (You MUST include this for iOS and Android mobile apps to work properly).

### Mobile App Configuration

MOBILE REDIRECT URI OVERRIDE: Must be enabled to support proper redirections from Authelia browser login back to the Immich mobile app. MOBILE REDIRECT URI: This is a specific URL provided by Immich, which will open the Immich mobile app if opened. Basically a custom scheme or deep link. It consists of your Immich FQDN and the path /api/oauth/mobile-redirect.

### Key Configuration Values (via Web UI or Config File)

Based on the Authelia integration example:
- Client ID: immich. Client Secret: insecure_secret. Scope: openid profile email. Button Text: Login with Authelia.

In summary, **Immich currently does not natively support setting OAuth/OIDC secrets via environment variables**. The OAuth configuration is done either through the Web GUI or via a JSON configuration file (`immich.json`). For secure handling of secrets in GitOps workflows, the community recommends using tools like `envsubst`, `sops`, or init containers to template the configuration file with secrets from environment variables before Immich starts.

# Immich and Authentik Integration Configuration

## Authentik Provider Setup

To establish the integration, create an OAuth2/OpenID Connect provider with these settings:

**Redirect URIs (Strict mode):**
- `app.immich:///oauth-callback`
- `https://immich.company/auth/login`
- `https://immich.company/user-settings`

**Key values to note:**
- Client ID
- Client Secret
- Provider slug

**Optional Launch URL:** `https://immich.company/auth/login?autoLaunch=1`

**Signing Key:** Select any available option

## Immich Configuration

Navigate to **Administration** > **Settings** > **OAuth Authentication** and enter:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Issuer URL** | `https://authentik.company/application/o/<application_slug>/.well-known/openid-configuration` |
| **Client ID** | (from authentik provider) |
| **Client Secret** | (from authentik provider) |
| **Scope** | `openid email profile` |

## Key Notes

The documentation notes that "only the settings that you need to change from their default values" are specified to avoid causing access issues. Refer to the [Immich OAuth documentation](https://immich.app/docs/administration/oauth) for additional details.

content.content:
# Immich OAuth Configuration Guide

## Configuration Method

The documentation provided covers OAuth setup through the **Administration Settings page** (Administration → Settings) in the web interface. It does not specify configuration via `immich.json` or environment variables like `IMMICH_CONFIG_FILE`.

## Available OAuth Settings

The system offers these configurable parameters:

| Setting | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---------|------|---------|---------|
| Enabled | Boolean | false | Activate/deactivate OAuth |
| Issuer URL | URL | Required | "Self-discovery URL for client" |
| Client ID | String | Required | OAuth application identifier |
| Client Secret | String | Required | OAuth application secret |
| Scope | String | "openid email profile" | Space-delimited permission request |
| Signing Algorithm | String | RS256 | ID token signature method |
| Storage Label Claim | String | preferred_username | User identifier mapping |
| Role Claim | String | immich_role | Admin/user distinction mapping |
| Storage Quota Claim | String | immich_quota | User storage limit mapping |
| Default Storage Quota | Number | 0 | Fallback quota (0 = unlimited) |
| Button Text | String | "Login with OAuth" | Web interface button label |
| Auto Register | Boolean | true | Automatic user creation on first login |
| Auto Launch | Boolean | false | Skip login page, start OAuth immediately |
| Mobile Redirect URI Override | URL | Empty | HTTP(S) alternative for mobile apps |

## Mobile App Redirect URI

The standard mobile URI is `app.immich:///oauth-callback`. If your provider cannot accept custom schemes, "configure an http(s) endpoint to forwards requests to `app.immich:///oauth-callback`" and register that endpoint instead.

## Auto-Registration

When enabled, the system will "automatically register a user the first time they sign in" via OAuth.

Based on my search, here's what I found about configuring Immich with OAuth using the IMMICH_CONFIG_FILE JSON configuration:

## Immich Config File Overview

In JSON format, you create a new config file (e.g., immich.json) and put it in a location that can be accessed by Immich.(no content)The configuration for Immich is stored in the immich.config.json file, and this can be mounted in the container.

## OAuth Configuration

Once you have a new OAuth client application configured, Immich can be configured using the Administration Settings page, available on the web (Administration -> Settings).(no content)Currently, config can be provided via UI or json file. Some config values, like oauth.clientSecret or smtp.password are sensitive.

### Example OAuth JSON Structure

Based on the discussions, the OAuth section in the JSON config file follows this pattern:

"oauth": { ..., "clientSecret": "${IMMICH_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}", ..., }" - though note that Immich should replace clientSecret with the value of the environment variable.

**Important Note:** A closed request means the Immich team is not planning to add official support for environment variable templating in the config file.(no content)The current workaround is templating externally, e.g., with init container before Immich starts or using secrets manager templating capabilities.

## Provider-Specific Examples

### For Authelia (Updated August 2024)

The configuration was updated in 2024-08 to reflect latest configuration changes by Authelia. It works for Immich v1.113.0 and Authelia v4.38.9.(no content)To configure OAuth in Immich: Visit your Immich web instance and login as admin. Then browse the URL /admin/system-settings. You'll find a setting named OAuth Authentication.

Key settings include:
- CLIENT SECRET: This is the client secret as cleartext password. Defined in Authelia's configuration.yml as $pbkdf2 password hash.
- SIGNING ALGORITHM: The signing algorithm to be used. Either RSA256 or HS256. For Authelia, please choose RS256.

### For Authentik

Open your browser and navigate to your immich app and go to: Administration -> Settings -> OAuth Authentication. Then Enable it, and a bunch of settings are shown.

## Important OAuth URLs

The Issuer URL should look something like: `https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration` or `http://localhost:9000/application/o/immich/.well-known/openid-configuration`. The .well-known/openid-configuration part of the url is optional and will be automatically added during discovery.(no content)The redirect URI for the mobile app is `app.immich:///oauth-callback`, which is a Custom Scheme.(no content)For mobile redirect, it consists of your Immich FQDN and the path /api/oauth/mobile-redirect.

Now I have all the info needed. Let me create the Authentik OIDC provider for Immich. The approach will be:

1. Create Authentik OAuth2/OIDC provider + application in the Immich app's terraform
2. Create an immich.json config file that gets synced to the container
3. Store the client secret in 1Password

The Authentik provider is already configured in versions.tf (symlinked). Now let me create the Authentik OIDC integration for Immich. I'll create a new file `authentik.tf` in the immich app directory.

input.content:
# =============================================================================
# Authentik OIDC Integration for Immich
# =============================================================================
# Configures Immich to use Authentik as its identity provider via OIDC.
# Users can log in with their Google account through Authentik.
#
# References:
# - https://integrations.goauthentik.io/media/immich/
# - https://docs.immich.app/administration/oauth/
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Immich OIDC Secret
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate a random client secret and store it (we'll use random for now,
# can be moved to 1Password later if needed)

resource "random_password" "immich_oidc_secret" {
  length  = 64
  special = false
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik OAuth2/OIDC Provider for Immich
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "authentik_certificate_key_pair" "default" {
  name = "authentik Self-signed Certificate"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_authorization" {
  slug = "default-provider-authorization-implicit-consent"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_invalidation" {
  slug = "default-provider-invalidation-flow"
}

# Property mappings for OIDC scopes
data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "openid" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-openid"
}

data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "email" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-email"
}

data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "profile" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-profile"
}

resource "authentik_provider_oauth2" "immich" {
  name               = "Immich"
  client_id          = "immich"
  client_secret      = random_password.immich_oidc_secret.result
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
  invalidation_flow  = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id

  # Redirect URIs - must include mobile app callback
  allowed_redirect_uris = [
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "app.immich:///oauth-callback"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}/auth/login"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}/user-settings"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/auth/login"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/user-settings"
    },
  ]

  # OIDC property mappings
  property_mappings = [
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.openid.id,
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.email.id,
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.profile.id,
  ]

  # Signing key
  signing_key = data.authentik_certificate_key_pair.default.id
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik Application for Immich
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "authentik_application" "immich" {
  name              = "Immich"
  slug              = "immich"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.id

  meta_icon        = "https://immich.app/img/immich-logo.svg"
  meta_description = "Self-hosted photo and video management"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab"
  meta_launch_url  = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/auth/login?autoLaunch=1"

  # Open to all authenticated users (no group restrictions yet)
  # To restrict access, add policy bindings here
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich OIDC Configuration File
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich reads OAuth config from a JSON file or web UI.
# We generate the config file and sync it to the container.

resource "local_sensitive_file" "immich_config" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/immich.json"
  content = jsonencode({
    oauth = {
      enabled                  = true
      autoRegister             = true
      autoLaunch               = false
      buttonText               = "Login with Google"
      clientId                 = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.client_id
      clientSecret             = random_password.immich_oidc_secret.result
      issuerUrl                = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/immich/"
      scope                    = "openid email profile"
      signingAlgorithm         = "RS256"
      profileSigningAlgorithm  = "none"
      storageLabelClaim        = "preferred_username"
      storageQuotaClaim        = "immich_quota"
      defaultStorageQuota      = 0
      mobileOverrideEnabled    = true
      mobileRedirectUri        = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/api/oauth/mobile-redirect"
      timeout                  = 30000
      tokenEndpointAuthMethod  = "client_secret_post"
    }
  })
  file_permission = "0600"
}

# Sync immich.json to the container
resource "filesync_file" "immich_config" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.immich_config.filename
  destination = "/config/immich.json"
  host        = module.immich.ip_address

  mode = "0644"

  depends_on = [module.immich, local_sensitive_file.immich_config]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "oidc_issuer_url" {
  description = "OIDC issuer URL for Immich"
  value       = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/immich/"
}

output "oidc_client_id" {
  description = "OIDC client ID for Immich"
  value       = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.client_id
}

# Immich - Self-hosted photo and video management
# https://immich.app/docs/install/docker-compose
# Updated: 2025-12 based on official v1.123+ config

name: immich

services:
  immich-server:
    container_name: immich_server
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    # Hardware transcoding: VAAPI for AMD GPU
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    volumes:
      - ${UPLOAD_LOCATION}:/usr/src/app/upload
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
    env_file:
      - .env
    ports:
      - 2283:2283
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - database
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '4.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  immich-machine-learning:
    container_name: immich_machine_learning
    # Using CPU image since AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) needs ROCm 6.4.4+
    # Immich ROCm image only has 6.3.4
    # Change to :release-rocm if/when Immich updates ROCm version
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learning:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    # Uncomment below and change image tag to :release-rocm when ROCm 6.4.4+ is available
    # devices:
    #   - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    #   - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
    # group_add:
    #   - video
    #   - render
    volumes:
      - model-cache:/cache
    env_file:
      - .env
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '4.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  redis:
    container_name: immich_redis
    image: docker.io/valkey/valkey:8-bookworm
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: valkey-cli ping || exit 1
    restart: unless-stopped

  database:
    container_name: immich_postgres
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_DATABASE_NAME}
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: '--data-checksums'
    volumes:
      - ${DB_DATA_LOCATION}:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    shm_size: 128mb
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    healthcheck:
      test: >-
        pg_isready --dbname="$${POSTGRES_DB}" --username="$${POSTGRES_USER}" || exit
        1; Chksum="$$(psql --dbname="$${POSTGRES_DB}" --username="$${POSTGRES_USER}"
        --tuples-only --no-align --command='SELECT COALESCE(SUM(googlechecksum(googlechecksum(tableoid,
        entity_id))), 0) FROM entity WHERE NOT is_external')"; Prev="$$(cat
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum 2>/dev/null || echo '')"; echo "$${Chksum}" >
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum; test "$${Prev}" = '' -o "$${Prev}" = "$${Chksum}"
      interval: 5m
      start_interval: 30s
      start_period: 5m
    command:
      [
        'postgres',
        '-c',
        'shared_preload_libraries=vchord.so,vectors.so',
        '-c',
        'search_path="$$user", public, vectors',
        '-c',
        'logging_collector=on',
        '-c',
        'max_wal_size=2GB',
        '-c',
        'shared_buffers=512MB',
        '-c',
        'wal_compression=on',
      ]
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  model-cache:

# =============================================================================
# Authentik OIDC Integration for Immich
# =============================================================================
# Configures Immich to use Authentik as its identity provider via OIDC.
# Users can log in with their Google account through Authentik.
#
# References:
# - https://integrations.goauthentik.io/media/immich/
# - https://docs.immich.app/administration/oauth/
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Immich OIDC Secret
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate a random client secret and store it (we'll use random for now,
# can be moved to 1Password later if needed)

resource "random_password" "immich_oidc_secret" {
  length  = 64
  special = false
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik OAuth2/OIDC Provider for Immich
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "authentik_certificate_key_pair" "default" {
  name = "authentik Self-signed Certificate"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_authorization" {
  slug = "default-provider-authorization-implicit-consent"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_invalidation" {
  slug = "default-provider-invalidation-flow"
}

# Property mappings for OIDC scopes
data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "openid" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-openid"
}

data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "email" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-email"
}

data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "profile" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-profile"
}

resource "authentik_provider_oauth2" "immich" {
  name               = "Immich"
  client_id          = "immich"
  client_secret      = random_password.immich_oidc_secret.result
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
  invalidation_flow  = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id

  # Redirect URIs - must include mobile app callback
  allowed_redirect_uris = [
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "app.immich:///oauth-callback"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}/auth/login"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}/user-settings"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/auth/login"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/user-settings"
    },
  ]

  # OIDC property mappings
  property_mappings = [
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.openid.id,
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.email.id,
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.profile.id,
  ]

  # Signing key
  signing_key = data.authentik_certificate_key_pair.default.id
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik Application for Immich
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "authentik_application" "immich" {
  name              = "Immich"
  slug              = "immich"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.id

  meta_icon        = "https://immich.app/img/immich-logo.svg"
  meta_description = "Self-hosted photo and video management"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab"
  meta_launch_url  = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/auth/login?autoLaunch=1"

  # Open to all authenticated users (no group restrictions yet)
  # To restrict access, add policy bindings here
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich OIDC Configuration File
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich reads OAuth config from a JSON file or web UI.
# We generate the config file and sync it to the container.

resource "local_sensitive_file" "immich_config" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/immich.json"
  content = jsonencode({
    oauth = {
      enabled                  = true
      autoRegister             = true
      autoLaunch               = false
      buttonText               = "Login with Google"
      clientId                 = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.client_id
      clientSecret             = random_password.immich_oidc_secret.result
      issuerUrl                = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/immich/"
      scope                    = "openid email profile"
      signingAlgorithm         = "RS256"
      profileSigningAlgorithm  = "none"
      storageLabelClaim        = "preferred_username"
      storageQuotaClaim        = "immich_quota"
      defaultStorageQuota      = 0
      mobileOverrideEnabled    = true
      mobileRedirectUri        = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/api/oauth/mobile-redirect"
      timeout                  = 30000
      tokenEndpointAuthMethod  = "client_secret_post"
    }
  })
  file_permission = "0600"
}

# Sync immich.json to the container
resource "filesync_file" "immich_config" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.immich_config.filename
  destination = "/config/immich.json"
  host        = module.immich.ip_address

  mode = "0644"

  depends_on = [module.immich, local_sensitive_file.immich_config]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "oidc_issuer_url" {
  description = "OIDC issuer URL for Immich"
  value       = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/immich/"
}

output "oidc_client_id" {
  description = "OIDC client ID for Immich"
  value       = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.client_id
}

# =============================================================================
# Authentik OIDC Integration for Immich
# =============================================================================
# Configures Immich to use Authentik as its identity provider via OIDC.
# Users can log in with their Google account through Authentik.
#
# References:
# - https://integrations.goauthentik.io/media/immich/
# - https://docs.immich.app/administration/oauth/
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Immich OIDC Secret
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate a random client secret and store it (we'll use random for now,
# can be moved to 1Password later if needed)

resource "random_password" "immich_oidc_secret" {
  length  = 64
  special = false
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik OAuth2/OIDC Provider for Immich
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "authentik_certificate_key_pair" "default" {
  name = "authentik Self-signed Certificate"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_authorization" {
  slug = "default-provider-authorization-implicit-consent"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_invalidation" {
  slug = "default-provider-invalidation-flow"
}

# Property mappings for OIDC scopes
data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "openid" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-openid"
}

data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "email" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-email"
}

data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "profile" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-profile"
}

resource "authentik_provider_oauth2" "immich" {
  name               = "Immich"
  client_id          = "immich"
  client_secret      = random_password.immich_oidc_secret.result
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
  invalidation_flow  = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id

  # Redirect URIs - must include mobile app callback
  allowed_redirect_uris = [
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "app.immich:///oauth-callback"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}/auth/login"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}/user-settings"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/auth/login"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/user-settings"
    },
  ]

  # OIDC property mappings
  property_mappings = [
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.openid.id,
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.email.id,
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.profile.id,
  ]

  # Signing key
  signing_key = data.authentik_certificate_key_pair.default.id
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik Application for Immich
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "authentik_application" "immich" {
  name              = "Immich"
  slug              = "immich"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.id

  meta_icon        = "https://immich.app/img/immich-logo.svg"
  meta_description = "Self-hosted photo and video management"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab"
  meta_launch_url  = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/auth/login?autoLaunch=1"

  # Open to all authenticated users (no group restrictions yet)
  # To restrict access, add policy bindings here
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich OIDC Configuration File
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich reads OAuth config from a JSON file or web UI.
# We generate the config file and sync it to the container.

resource "local_sensitive_file" "immich_config" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/immich.json"

      autoRegister             = true

      clientSecret             = random_password.immich_oidc_secret.result

}

# =============================================================================
# Authentik OIDC Integration for Immich
# =============================================================================
# Configures Immich to use Authentik as its identity provider via OIDC.
# Users can log in with their Google account through Authentik.
#
# References:
# - https://integrations.goauthentik.io/media/immich/
# - https://docs.immich.app/administration/oauth/
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Immich OIDC Secret
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate a random client secret and store it (we'll use random for now,
# can be moved to 1Password later if needed)

resource "random_password" "immich_oidc_secret" {
  length  = 64
  special = false
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik OAuth2/OIDC Provider for Immich
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "authentik_certificate_key_pair" "default" {
  name = "authentik Self-signed Certificate"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_authorization" {
  slug = "default-provider-authorization-implicit-consent"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_invalidation" {
  slug = "default-provider-invalidation-flow"
}

# Property mappings for OIDC scopes
data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "openid" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-openid"
}

data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "email" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-email"
}

data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "profile" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-profile"
}

resource "authentik_provider_oauth2" "immich" {
  name               = "Immich"
  client_id          = "immich"
  client_secret      = random_password.immich_oidc_secret.result
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
  invalidation_flow  = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id

  # Redirect URIs - must include mobile app callback
  allowed_redirect_uris = [
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "app.immich:///oauth-callback"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}/auth/login"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}/user-settings"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/auth/login"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/user-settings"
    },
  ]

  # OIDC property mappings
  property_mappings = [
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.openid.id,
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.email.id,
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.profile.id,
  ]

  # Signing key
  signing_key = data.authentik_certificate_key_pair.default.id
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik Application for Immich
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "authentik_application" "immich" {
  name              = "Immich"
  slug              = "immich"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.id

  meta_icon        = "https://immich.app/img/immich-logo.svg"
  meta_description = "Self-hosted photo and video management"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab"
  meta_launch_url  = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/auth/login?autoLaunch=1"

  # Open to all authenticated users (no group restrictions yet)
  # To restrict access, add policy bindings here
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich OIDC Configuration File
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich reads OAuth config from a JSON file or web UI.
# We generate the config file and sync it to the container.

resource "local_sensitive_file" "immich_config" {
  filename = "${path.module}/.terraform/immich.json"
  content = jsonencode({
    oauth = {
      enabled                  = true
      autoRegister             = true
      autoLaunch               = false
      buttonText               = "Login with Google"
      clientId                 = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.client_id
      clientSecret             = random_password.immich_oidc_secret.result
      issuerUrl                = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/immich/"
      scope                    = "openid email profile"
      signingAlgorithm         = "RS256"
      profileSigningAlgorithm  = "none"
      storageLabelClaim        = "preferred_username"
      storageQuotaClaim        = "immich_quota"
      defaultStorageQuota      = 0
      mobileOverrideEnabled    = true
      mobileRedirectUri        = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/api/oauth/mobile-redirect"
      timeout                  = 30000
      tokenEndpointAuthMethod  = "client_secret_post"
    }
  })
  file_permission = "0600"
}

# Sync immich.json to the container
resource "filesync_file" "immich_config" {
  source      = "${path.module}/deploy/immich.json"
  destination = "/config/immich.json"
  host        = module.immich.ip_address

  mode = "0644"

  depends_on = [module.immich, local_sensitive_file.immich_config]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "oidc_issuer_url" {
  description = "OIDC issuer URL for Immich"
  value       = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/immich/"
}

output "oidc_client_id" {
  description = "OIDC client ID for Immich"
  value       = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.client_id
}

# Immich - Self-hosted photo and video management
# https://immich.app/docs/install/docker-compose
# Updated: 2025-12 based on official v1.123+ config

name: immich

services:
  immich-server:
    container_name: immich_server
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    # Hardware transcoding: VAAPI for AMD GPU
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    volumes:
      - ${UPLOAD_LOCATION}:/usr/src/app/upload
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
      - ./immich.json:/config/immich.json:ro
    env_file:
      - .env
    environment:
      # OIDC config file - managed by OpenTofu
      IMMICH_CONFIG_FILE: /config/immich.json
    ports:
      - 2283:2283
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - database
    deploy:

content.text:
With the current configuration, they will be treated as the **same user** because:

1. **`autoRegister: true`** - This allows OAuth users to get accounts
2. **Immich's behavior** - When a user logs in via OAuth, Immich matches by email address

So if you already have an Immich account with `yourname@gmail.com` and you login via Google OAuth with the same email, Immich will link the OAuth login to your existing account.

However, there's one caveat: The first time you login via OAuth, Immich might:
- **Link to existing account** - If the email matches exactly
- **Create a new account** - If there's any mismatch or if your existing account wasn't set up with that email

To be safe, you can verify your existing Immich account has the correct email set in **Account Settings → Account** before testing OAuth login.

If you want to be extra cautious, you could set `autoRegister: false` initially - this would require the Immich admin to manually link OAuth to existing users. But with matching emails, it should just work.

Want me to test the login flow, or would you prefer to test it yourself first?
but with autoRegister as true, will it enable absolutely anyone with gmail email id to sign up on immich or will it still be limited to users setup in authentik?
