# =============================================================================
# Authentik Providers - OAuth Sources, Forward Auth, OIDC Providers
# =============================================================================
# This file contains all Authentik provider configurations:
#   - Google OAuth source (SSO via Google)
#   - Forward auth provider for Traefik
#   - OIDC providers for apps with native SSO support (future)
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Terraform API Token - Non-expiring
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates a non-expiring API token for Terraform to manage authentik.
# The token value is stored in 1Password and used by the provider.
#
# Bootstrap: Create a short-lived token in UI first, run tofu apply,
# then update 1Password with the new token value from the output.

data "authentik_user" "akadmin" {
  username = "akadmin"
}

resource "authentik_token" "terraform" {
  identifier   = "terraform-api"
  user         = data.authentik_user.akadmin.id
  intent       = "api"
  expiring     = false  # Never expires
  description  = "API token for OpenTofu/Terraform - managed by IaC"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Google OAuth Source - SSO via Google Account
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Allows users to login with their Google account
# Credentials stored in 1Password (authentik item)

data "authentik_flow" "default_source_authentication" {
  slug = "default-source-authentication"
}

resource "authentik_source_oauth" "google" {
  name                = "Google"
  slug                = "google"
  authentication_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_source_authentication.id

  # No enrollment flow - users must be pre-created in authentik
  # This prevents unauthorized users from self-registering
  enrollment_flow = ""

  provider_type   = "google"
  consumer_key    = local.op.authentik_google_client_id
  consumer_secret = local.op.authentik_google_client_secret

  # Match users by email and link OAuth source on first login
  # "email_link" matches by email and creates the link automatically
  user_matching_mode = "email_link"

  # Policy engine mode
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Link Google OAuth to Login Flow
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# NOTE: The Google source must be manually added to the identification stage
# in the authentik admin UI:
#   1. Go to Flows & Stages → Stages
#   2. Edit "default-authentication-identification"
#   3. Add "Google" to the Sources field
#   4. Save
#
# This is required because the stage already exists and can't be recreated
# via Terraform without importing it first.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Forward Auth Provider - For protecting services via Traefik
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creates a Proxy Provider in forward auth mode for protecting services
# that don't have native OIDC support. The embedded outpost handles the auth.

data "authentik_flow" "default_authorization" {
  slug = "default-provider-authorization-implicit-consent"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_invalidation" {
  slug = "default-provider-invalidation-flow"
}

resource "authentik_provider_proxy" "forward_auth" {
  name               = "Traefik Forward Auth"
  mode               = "forward_domain"  # Domain mode - protects all subdomains
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
  invalidation_flow  = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id

  # External host - the authentik outpost's external URL for browser redirects
  external_host = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"

  # Cookie settings for SSO across all subdomains
  # Must be the root domain to work with both *.homelab.rambtech.dev and auth.rambtech.dev
  cookie_domain = var.domain_public
}

resource "authentik_application" "forward_auth" {
  name              = "Homelab Forward Auth"
  slug              = "homelab-forward-auth"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id

  meta_description = "Forward authentication for homelab services protected by Traefik"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab Infrastructure"

  # Open to all authenticated users
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# Update the embedded outpost to include the forward auth provider
# Note: The embedded outpost is managed by authentik, we just update its providers
resource "authentik_outpost" "embedded" {
  name               = "authentik Embedded Outpost"
  type               = "proxy"
  protocol_providers = [authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id]

  config = jsonencode({
    # Internal URL for outpost-to-authentik communication
    authentik_host          = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"
    # Browser URL - what users see (HTTPS via Cloudflare)
    authentik_host_browser  = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"
    authentik_host_insecure = false
    log_level               = "info"
  })

  lifecycle {
    # The embedded outpost already exists, we're just updating it
    ignore_changes = [service_connection]
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Authentik Forward Auth Integration for n8n
# =============================================================================

# forwardAuth middleware with Authentik. The hooks.js file handles user

# This uses the same forwardAuth provider as other protected services

}

resource "authentik_application" "n8n" {
  name              = "n8n"
  slug              = "n8n"
  protocol_provider = data.authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id

  meta_icon        = "https://n8n.io/favicon.ico"
  meta_description = "Workflow automation platform"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab"
  meta_launch_url  = "https://n8n.${var.domain_internal}"

}

# =============================================================================
# Authentik Forward Auth Integration for n8n
# =============================================================================
# n8n Community Edition doesn't support native OIDC, so we use Traefik's
# forwardAuth middleware with Authentik. The hooks.js file handles user
# auto-provisioning based on the X-authentik-* headers.
#
# References:
# - https://github.com/PavelSozonov/n8n-community-sso
# - https://docs.goauthentik.io/docs/providers/proxy/forward_auth
# =============================================================================

# Note: We use the existing forwardAuth provider from tofu/apps/authentik/providers.tf
# The "authentik" middleware in Traefik is already configured to use it.

# Create an application entry for n8n in Authentik's app launcher
# This uses the same forwardAuth provider as other protected services
data "authentik_provider_proxy" "forward_auth" {
  name = "Traefik Forward Auth"
}

resource "authentik_application" "n8n" {
  name              = "n8n"
  slug              = "n8n"
  protocol_provider = data.authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id

  meta_icon        = "https://n8n.io/favicon.ico"
  meta_description = "Workflow automation platform"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab"
  meta_launch_url  = "https://n8n.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Open to all authenticated users
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# =============================================================================
# Authentik Forward Auth Integration for n8n
# =============================================================================
# n8n Community Edition doesn't support native OIDC, so we use Traefik's
# forwardAuth middleware with Authentik. The hooks.js file handles user
# auto-provisioning based on the X-authentik-* headers.
#
# References:
# - https://github.com/PavelSozonov/n8n-community-sso
# - https://docs.goauthentik.io/docs/providers/proxy/forward_auth
# =============================================================================

# Note: We use the existing forwardAuth provider from tofu/apps/authentik/providers.tf
# The "authentik" middleware in Traefik is already configured to use it.
# n8n is protected at the Traefik layer via forwardAuth - the hooks.js file
# reads the X-authentik-* headers and auto-provisions users in n8n.

# Look up the existing forward auth application to get its provider ID
data "authentik_application" "forward_auth" {
  slug = "homelab-forward-auth"
}

# Create an application entry for n8n in Authentik's app launcher
# This is a convenience entry - n8n actually uses the forward_auth provider
resource "authentik_application" "n8n" {

  slug              = "n8n"

  meta_description = "Workflow automation platform"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab"
  meta_launch_url  = "https://n8n.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Open to all authenticated users
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# =============================================================================
# Authentik OIDC Integration for Immich
# =============================================================================
# Configures Immich to use Authentik as its identity provider via OIDC.
# Users can log in with their Google account through Authentik.
#
# References:
# - https://integrations.goauthentik.io/media/immich/
# - https://docs.immich.app/administration/oauth/
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Immich OIDC Secret
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate a random client secret and store it (we'll use random for now,
# can be moved to 1Password later if needed)

resource "random_password" "immich_oidc_secret" {
  length  = 64
  special = false
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik OAuth2/OIDC Provider for Immich
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "authentik_certificate_key_pair" "default" {
  name = "authentik Self-signed Certificate"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_authorization" {
  slug = "default-provider-authorization-implicit-consent"
}

data "authentik_flow" "default_invalidation" {
  slug = "default-provider-invalidation-flow"
}

# Property mappings for OIDC scopes
data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "openid" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-openid"
}

data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "email" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-email"
}

data "authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope" "profile" {
  managed = "goauthentik.io/providers/oauth2/scope-profile"
}

resource "authentik_provider_oauth2" "immich" {
  name               = "Immich"
  client_id          = "immich"
  client_secret      = random_password.immich_oidc_secret.result
  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
  invalidation_flow  = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id

  # Redirect URIs - must include mobile app callback
  allowed_redirect_uris = [
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "app.immich:///oauth-callback"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}/auth/login"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_internal}/user-settings"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/auth/login"
    },
    {
      matching_mode = "strict"
      url           = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/user-settings"
    },
  ]

  # OIDC property mappings
  property_mappings = [
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.openid.id,
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.email.id,
    data.authentik_property_mapping_provider_scope.profile.id,
  ]

  # Signing key
  signing_key = data.authentik_certificate_key_pair.default.id
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik Application for Immich
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "authentik_application" "immich" {
  name              = "Immich"
  slug              = "immich"
  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.id

  meta_icon        = "https://immich.app/img/immich-logo.svg"
  meta_description = "Self-hosted photo and video management"
  meta_publisher   = "Homelab"
  meta_launch_url  = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/auth/login?autoLaunch=1"

  # Open to all authenticated users (no group restrictions yet)
  # To restrict access, add policy bindings here
  policy_engine_mode = "any"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich OIDC Configuration File
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich reads OAuth config from a JSON file or web UI.
# We generate the config file and sync it to the container.

resource "local_sensitive_file" "immich_config" {
  filename = "${path.module}/.terraform/immich.json"
  content = jsonencode({
    oauth = {
      enabled                  = true
      autoRegister             = true
      autoLaunch               = false
      buttonText               = "Login with Google"
      clientId                 = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.client_id
      clientSecret             = random_password.immich_oidc_secret.result
      issuerUrl                = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/immich/"
      scope                    = "openid email profile"
      signingAlgorithm         = "RS256"
      profileSigningAlgorithm  = "none"
      storageLabelClaim        = "preferred_username"
      storageQuotaClaim        = "immich_quota"
      defaultStorageQuota      = 0
      mobileOverrideEnabled    = true
      mobileRedirectUri        = "https://photos.${var.domain_public}/api/oauth/mobile-redirect"
      timeout                  = 30000
      tokenEndpointAuthMethod  = "client_secret_post"
    }
  })
  file_permission = "0600"
}

# Sync immich.json to the container
resource "filesync_file" "immich_config" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.immich_config.filename
  destination = "/config/immich.json"
  host        = module.immich.ip_address

  mode = "0644"

  depends_on = [module.immich, local_sensitive_file.immich_config]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "oidc_issuer_url" {
  description = "OIDC issuer URL for Immich"
  value       = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/immich/"
}

output "oidc_client_id" {
  description = "OIDC client ID for Immich"
  value       = authentik_provider_oauth2.immich.client_id
}

content.content:
proxmox-homelab-45r: Epic: Migrate from Authelia to Authentik
Status: in_progress
Priority: P1
Type: epic
Created: 2025-12-21 00:15
Updated: 2025-12-21 01:16

Description:
Complete migration from Authelia to Authentik as the centralized identity provider.

## Overview
Replace Authelia with Authentik to gain:
- Native Google/GitHub OAuth federation
- OIDC provider capabilities for apps with native SSO support
- Forward auth for apps without native OAuth
- Centralized user/group management
- Jellyfin SSO plugin compatibility

## Phases

### Phase 1: Infrastructure
- Deploy Authentik alongside Traefik in LXC 200
- Configure Google OAuth source
- Setup forward auth middleware in Traefik

### Phase 2: Dashboard & Utility Apps (Forward Auth)
- Homepage, Dashy, Pulse, Arcane, Stirling-PDF
- Prometheus, Alertmanager

### Phase 3: Media & Network Apps (Forward Auth)
- Uptime Kuma, qBittorrent
- Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, SABnzbd
- AdGuard, Traefik Dashboard, ntfy

### Phase 4: Native OIDC Apps
- Grafana, OpenWebUI, Paperless-ngx, n8n, Jellyseerr

### Phase 5: Media Apps (Native OIDC)
- Immich, Jellyfin

### Phase 6: Cleanup
- Decommission Authelia

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All services authenticated via Authentik
- [ ] Google OAuth login working for all users
- [ ] Authelia fully decommissioned
- [ ] All configuration managed as code (OpenTofu/Ansible)

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] All services authenticated via Authentik
- [ ] Google OAuth login working for all users
- [ ] Authelia fully decommissioned
- [ ] All configuration managed as code (OpenTofu/Ansible)

# =============================================================================
# Jellyfin LXC - Media Server
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 401

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file with Jellystat credentials
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "local_sensitive_file" "jellyfin_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/.env"
  content  = <<-EOT
# Jellyfin Stack Environment Variables
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten

# Jellystat PostgreSQL credentials
JELLYSTAT_DB_PASSWORD=st4dnS0X75gJTlATNXYBWQawJ4OzYQ
JELLYSTAT_JWT_SECRET=69z87jUXLPJxIkao3EGXW8QF51ZTM5uSSucwJaw6I
EOT

  file_permission = "0600"
}

module "jellyfin" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "jellyfin"
  container_id = 401
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for DLNA/casting)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.media.jellyfin}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.jellyfin}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  cores  = 4
  memory = 8192
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = 32

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Enable AMD GPU passthrough for hardware transcoding
  enable_gpu = true

  # Mount point for media library
  # This is configured via SSH (null_resource.configure_mount_points) since
  # the API token doesn't have permission for bind mounts (requires root@pam)
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      path   = "/data/library"
      volume = "/tank/data/library"
    }
  ]

  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  service_name        = "Jellyfin"
  service_description = "Media server for movies, TV shows, and music"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://jellyfin.${var.domain_internal}"
    public   = "https://jellyfin.${var.domain_public}"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.jellyfin}:8096"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Jellyfin", port = 8096, info = "Media server UI" },
    { name = "Jellyseerr", port = 5055, info = "Media request management" },
    { name = "Jellystat", port = 3000, info = "Statistics dashboard" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Quick Commands
**View logs:** cd /config && docker compose logs -f jellyfin
**Restart:** cd /config && docker compose restart jellyfin
EOT

  tags = ["jellyfin", "media"]
}

module "jellyfin_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "jellyfin"
  backend_url = "http://${module.jellyfin.ip_address}:8096"

  internal_domain = "jellyfin.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "jellyfin.${var.domain_public}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.jellyfin]
}

# Jellystat - Jellyfin statistics dashboard
module "jellystat_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "jellystat"
  backend_url = "http://${module.jellyfin.ip_address}:3000"

  internal_domain = "jellystat.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Has built-in auth, only need security headers and internal access
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "internal-only"]

  depends_on = [module.jellyfin]
}

# Jellyseerr/Requests - Media request management
module "requests_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "requests"
  backend_url = "http://${module.jellyfin.ip_address}:5055"

  internal_domain = "requests.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "requests.${var.domain_public}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["public-security"]

  depends_on = [module.jellyfin]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "jellyfin_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.jellyfin.container_id
  container_ip   = module.jellyfin.ip_address
  container_name = "jellyfin"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-401"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "PostgreSQL dump (Jellystat)"
      command = "docker exec jellystat-db pg_dump -U jellystat -d jellystat --clean --if-exists | gzip > /config/jellystat-db-backup.sql.gz"
      timeout = 300
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,jellyfin,jellystat"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["jellyfin"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["jellyfin"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.jellyfin]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" { value = module.jellyfin.container_id }
output "ip_address" { value = module.jellyfin.ip_address }
output "ssh_command" { value = module.jellyfin.ssh_command }
output "urls" {
  value = {
    jellyfin  = { internal = module.jellyfin_route.internal_url, public = module.jellyfin_route.public_url }
    jellystat = { internal = module.jellystat_route.internal_url }
    requests  = { internal = module.requests_route.internal_url, public = module.requests_route.public_url }
  }
}

# Jellyfin Media Server Stack
# Includes: Jellyfin, Jellyseerr, Jellystat + PostgreSQL

name: jellyfin

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellyfin - Media Streaming Server
  # ==========================================================================
  jellyfin:
    image: jellyfin/jellyfin:10.11.5
    container_name: jellyfin
    user: 1000:1000
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    ports:
      - "8096:8096"
    volumes:
      - jellyfin-config:/config
      - jellyfin-cache:/cache
      - /data/library:/data/library:ro
    # AMD GPU passthrough for hardware transcoding (VA-API)
    group_add:
      - "44"   # video group for GPU access
      - "104"  # render group for GPU access
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
      - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 8192m
          cpus: '4.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8096/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellyseerr - Media Request Management (Overseerr fork for Jellyfin)
  # ==========================================================================
  jellyseerr:
    image: fallenbagel/jellyseerr:2.7.3
    container_name: jellyseerr
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - LOG_LEVEL=info
    ports:
      - "5055:5055"
    volumes:
      - jellyseerr-config:/app/config
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:5055/api/v1/status || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellystat - Statistics and Analytics for Jellyfin
  # ==========================================================================
  jellystat:
    image: cyfershepard/jellystat:1.1.6
    container_name: jellystat
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - POSTGRES_USER=jellystat
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${JELLYSTAT_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_IP=jellystat-db
      - POSTGRES_PORT=5432
      - JWT_SECRET=${JELLYSTAT_JWT_SECRET}
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - jellystat-data:/app/backend/backup-data
    depends_on:
      jellystat-db:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # PostgreSQL - Database for Jellystat
  # ==========================================================================
  jellystat-db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    container_name: jellystat-db
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=jellystat
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${JELLYSTAT_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=jellystat
    volumes:
      - jellystat-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    shm_size: 128mb
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U jellystat"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  jellyfin-config:
  jellyfin-cache:
  jellyseerr-config:
  jellystat-data:
  jellystat-pgdata:

# Jellyfin and Authentik SSO Integration Guide

## Overview

"Jellyfin is a free and open source media management and streaming platform for movies, TV shows, and music." The integration supports two authentication methods: LDAP and OIDC.

## Two Integration Approaches

**LDAP Method** requires deploying an LDAP outpost within your authentik infrastructure. This approach uses directory services for user authentication.

**OIDC Method** leverages OAuth2/OpenID protocols for modern SSO functionality without needing an outpost.

## OIDC Configuration (Recommended)

### Authentik Setup
1. Create an OAuth2/OpenID Provider with:
   - Name: `jellyfin`
   - Redirect URI: `https://jellyfin.company/sso/OID/redirect/authentik`
   - Record the client ID and secret
2. Create an application using the jellyfin provider
3. Set launch URL to `https://jellyfin.company/sso/OID/start/authentik`

### Jellyfin Plugin Installation
1. Access Admin Dashboard > Plugins > Repositories
2. Add repository: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/9p4/jellyfin-plugin-sso/manifest-release/manifest.json`
3. Install SSO-Auth plugin from Catalog
4. Restart Jellyfin

### Plugin Configuration
1. Configure Provider Settings:
   - Provider name: `authentik`
   - OID Endpoint: `https://authentik.company/application/o/jellyfin/.well-known/openid-configuration`
   - Enter Client ID and Secret
   - Enable both checkboxes
2. Optionally configure role-based access using the `groups` claim
3. Add SSO button to login page via Branding section

## Key Considerations

- The LDAP approach requires a bind user with appropriate permissions
- OIDC provides a more modern, streamlined authentication experience
- Both methods require proper certificate handling (self-signed certificates need verification disabled)
- Username-based login is required; email authentication won't work with LDAP

content.content:
# Jellyseerr and Authentik OIDC Integration Guide

## Overview

"Jellyseerr is a free and open source application for managing requests in your media library" that works with media servers like Jellyfin, Plex, and Emby.

## Prerequisites

- Jellyseerr FQDN: `jellyseerr.company`
- Authentik FQDN: `authentik.company`
- Jellyseerr must use the `preview-OIDC` Docker tag (OIDC support is currently in preview)

## Authentik Setup

1. Log into Authentik as administrator
2. Navigate to **Applications > Applications** and select **Create with Provider**
3. Configure the application with a descriptive name and slug
4. Select **OAuth2/OpenID** as the provider type
5. Set the redirect URI to: `https://jellyseerr.company/login?provider=authentik&callback=true`
6. Record the **Client ID** and **Client Secret**
7. Save the application/provider pair

## Jellyseerr Configuration

1. Log in as an administrator
2. Go to **Settings > Users**
3. Enable **OpenID Connect Sign-In** and click the configuration icon
4. Select **Add OpenID Connect Provider** and enter:
   - **Provider Name:** `authentik`
   - **Issuer URL:** `https://authentik.company/application/o/jellyseerr/`
   - **Client ID & Secret:** From Authentik setup
   - **Scopes:** `openid profile email groups`
   - **Allow New Users:** Enabled
5. Save changes

## Verification

Log out and attempt login using the Authentik button to confirm proper integration.

Jellyseerr OAuth support is currently in preview, and you need to use the `preview-OIDC` Docker tag to access this feature.

### Key Information:

1. **Docker Image**: The `preview-OIDC` tag is available on Docker Hub at `fallenbagel/jellyseerr:preview-OIDC`.

2. **Building Manually**: If you want to build the image yourself, you can use the command:
   ```bash
   docker build --build-arg "COMMIT_TAG=$(git show --pretty=format:"%h" --no-patch)" --build-arg "BUILD_VERSION=preview-OIDC" --build-arg "BUILD_DATE=$(date --iso-8601=seconds)" -t jellyseerr:preview-OIDC .
   ```

3. **Docker Hub Tag Updates**: Some users noted that the `preview-OIDC` tag on Docker Hub didn't include more recent commits to the OIDC PR, so they built the Docker image manually to get the latest changes.

4. **Recent Community Activity** (December 2025): A recent discussion on the Authentik GitHub (December 13, 2025) noted that "Jellyseerr has OAuth support in a specific docker tag they provide (preview-OIDC), and Authelia has covered how to integrate with it."

### Integration with Identity Providers:

- **Authelia**: Authelia provides a step-by-step guide to configuring Jellyseerr with OpenID Connect 1.0 for secure SSO.

- **Authentik**: To configure with Authentik, you navigate to Settings > Users, toggle on "Enable OpenID Connect Sign-In," click on the cogwheel icon, then click "Add OpenID Connect Provider" and configure the required settings.

### Common Setup Tips:

- Make sure that your OIDC scopes are space-separated (not comma-separated), and if you're behind a reverse proxy like Cloudflare, enable "Proxy Support" in network settings so Jellyseerr trusts the headers.

- For users of the latest version of Authelia, you need to add `token_endpoint_auth_method: 'client_secret_post'` to the configuration file.

# Jellyfin Media Server Stack
# Includes: Jellyfin, Jellyseerr, Jellystat + PostgreSQL

name: jellyfin

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellyfin - Media Streaming Server
  # ==========================================================================
  jellyfin:
    image: jellyfin/jellyfin:10.11.5
    container_name: jellyfin
    user: 1000:1000
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    ports:
      - "8096:8096"
    volumes:
      - jellyfin-config:/config
      - jellyfin-cache:/cache
      - /data/library:/data/library:ro
    # AMD GPU passthrough for hardware transcoding (VA-API)
    group_add:
      - "44"   # video group for GPU access
      - "104"  # render group for GPU access
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
      - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 8192m
          cpus: '4.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8096/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellyseerr - Media Request Management (Overseerr fork for Jellyfin)
  # ==========================================================================
  jellyseerr:
    image: fallenbagel/jellyseerr:2.7.3
    container_name: jellyseerr
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - LOG_LEVEL=info
    ports:
      - "5055:5055"
    volumes:
      - jellyseerr-config:/app/config
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:5055/api/v1/status || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellystat - Statistics and Analytics for Jellyfin
  # ==========================================================================
  jellystat:
    image: cyfershepard/jellystat:1.1.6
    container_name: jellystat
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - POSTGRES_USER=jellystat
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${JELLYSTAT_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_IP=jellystat-db
      - POSTGRES_PORT=5432
      - JWT_SECRET=${JELLYSTAT_JWT_SECRET}
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - jellystat-data:/app/backend/backup-data
    depends_on:
      jellystat-db:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # PostgreSQL - Database for Jellystat
  # ==========================================================================
  jellystat-db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    container_name: jellystat-db
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=jellystat
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${JELLYSTAT_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=jellystat
    volumes:
      - jellystat-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    shm_size: 128mb
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U jellystat"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  jellyfin-config:
  jellyfin-cache:
  jellyseerr-config:
  jellystat-data:
  jellystat-pgdata:

# SSO Login Button Examples for Jellyfin

Based on the documentation, here are the key components for adding an SSO login button:

## HTML Form

The plugin recommends placing this in the "Login disclaimer" section under Jellyfin's Branding settings:

```html
<form action="https://jellyfin.example.com/sso/OID/start/PROVIDER_NAME">
  <button class="raised block emby-button button-submit">
    Sign in with SSO
  </button>
</form>
```

Replace `PROVIDER_NAME` with your actual provider identifier and update the domain accordingly.

## CSS Styling

Add this to the "Custom CSS code" section in Jellyfin's admin interface:

```css
a.raised.emby-button {
  padding: 0.9em 1em;
  color: inherit !important;
}

.disclaimerContainer {
  display: block;
}
```

## Key Points

- The form uses a POST action directing to either `/sso/OID/start/` for OpenID or `/sso/SAML/start/` for SAML protocols
- The CSS ensures proper styling and layout within Jellyfin's existing design system
- No additional JavaScript is required; the plugin handles authentication flow server-side
- "This only works on the web UI" according to the documentation

For more detailed configuration examples with role-based access, refer to the SAML and OpenID sections in the plugin's documentation.

Let me check if there's a way to configure Jellyfin to use HTTPS for the redirect URI. The SSO plugin has a setting for this.

In the **Jellyfin SSO-Auth plugin settings**, look for a field called **"Scheme Override"** or similar. Set it to `https` to force the plugin to use HTTPS in the redirect URI.

Alternatively, check if there's a checkbox like **"Enable scheme override"** and set the scheme to `https`.

If that setting doesn't exist in your plugin version, you may need to configure Jellyfin itself to recognize it's behind a reverse proxy. Check if there's a **"Known Proxies"** or **"Published Server URL"** setting in:

**Admin Dashboard → Networking**

This tells Jellyfin that external requests come via HTTPS, so it should use `https://` in its redirect URIs.

in the published server uri, if we use https://jellyfin.homelab.rambtech.dev then it wont work with https://jellyfin.rambtech.dev right?

Correct - Jellyfin only allows one Published Server URI, so it would only work for one domain.

There are a few options:

1. **Use Scheme Override in the SSO plugin** (best option) - The SSO-Auth plugin should have a "Scheme Override" field where you can enter `https`. This forces the plugin to use HTTPS regardless of what Jellyfin thinks the scheme is.

2. **Use forwardAuth instead** - Like we did with n8n, protect Jellyfin with Authentik's forwardAuth middleware at the Traefik level. This bypasses the OIDC complexity entirely. Users authenticate at Traefik before reaching Jellyfin.

3. **Pick one domain** - Use the internal domain (`jellyfin.homelab.rambtech.dev`) as the Published Server URI since that's your primary access method.

Do you see a "Scheme Override" or "Override Redirect URI Scheme" option in the SSO-Auth plugin settings? That's the cleanest fix. If not, option 2 (forwardAuth) would be the most reliable approach - it worked well for n8n.

## Jellyseerr + Authentik OIDC Configuration

### Official Authentik Integration Guide

Jellyseerr OAuth support is currently in preview, so you need to use the `preview-OIDC` Docker tag.

**Configuration Steps:**

1. Log in to Jellyseerr with an administrator account. Navigate to Settings > Users. Toggle on Enable OpenID Connect Sign-In and click on the cogwheel icon next to it. Click Add OpenID Connect Provider and configure the settings, then click Save Changes.

2. In Authentik, set a Strict redirect URI to `https://jellyseerr.company/login?provider=authentik&callback=true`. Select any available signing key. Configure Bindings (optional) to manage the listing and access to applications. Click Submit to save the new application and provider.

3. To verify that authentik is correctly set up with Jellyseerr, log out of Jellyseerr and try logging back in using the authentik button.

### User Experience Reports

From the GitHub discussion on OIDC support:

- Users have been successfully using Authentik as their SSO provider. One user imported themselves as a Plex user first, then other users were created by connecting through Authentik. Accounts can be linked to both Plex and Authentik.

- For scopes, users configure `openid email profile` in Jellyseerr with those scopes checked in Authentik.

### Known Issues

- Some users report redirect URI issues where the URI returned from Jellyseerr is in HTTP format instead of HTTPS, which can break the regex on Authentik.

- There may be case matching issues with usernames. If a Jellyfin username is "Kris" but the Authentik username is "kris" (lowercase), Jellyseerr may treat them as different users.

### Feature Request Status

Authentication providers like Authelia, Auth0, Authentik, Keycloak, etc. make managing user permissions across self-hosted services much easier. Users want to configure custom OIDC providers for logins that appear on the Jellyseerr login page.

For the most up-to-date and detailed configuration instructions, I recommend checking the official Authentik integration documentation at https://integrations.goauthentik.io/media/jellyseerr/.

# Jellyseerr with Authentik OIDC Configuration

## Key Requirements

**Docker Image Tag:** Use the `preview-OIDC` tag, as "Jellyseer OAuth support is currently in preview."

**Redirect URI:** Configure a strict redirect to `https://jellyseerr.company/login?provider=authentik&callback=true`

**Required Scopes:** The integration needs `openid profile email groups`

## Configuration Steps Summary

1. **In Authentik:** Create an OAuth2/OpenID provider with the redirect URI noted above. Record the Client ID and Client Secret.

2. **In Jellyseerr:** Enable OpenID Connect sign-in and add a new provider with these settings:
   - Provider Name: `authentik`
   - Issuer URL: `https://authentik.company/application/o/jellyseerr/`
   - Input the Client ID and Secret from Authentik
   - Apply the specified scopes in Advanced Settings
   - Enable "Allow New Users"

3. **Verification:** Log out and attempt login using the Authentik button to confirm proper integration.

# Jellyfin Media Server Stack
# Includes: Jellyfin, Jellyseerr, Jellystat + PostgreSQL

name: jellyfin

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellyfin - Media Streaming Server
  # ==========================================================================
  jellyfin:
    image: jellyfin/jellyfin:10.11.5
    container_name: jellyfin
    user: 1000:1000
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    ports:
      - "8096:8096"
    volumes:
      - jellyfin-config:/config
      - jellyfin-cache:/cache
      - /data/library:/data/library:ro
    # AMD GPU passthrough for hardware transcoding (VA-API)
    group_add:
      - "44"   # video group for GPU access
      - "104"  # render group for GPU access
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
      - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 8192m
          cpus: '4.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8096/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellyseerr - Media Request Management (Overseerr fork for Jellyfin)
  # ==========================================================================
  # SSO is handled via "Jellyfin Sign-In" - users authenticate with Jellyfin
  # which uses Authentik SSO. No direct OIDC integration needed.
  jellyseerr:
    image: fallenbagel/jellyseerr:2.7.3
    container_name: jellyseerr
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - LOG_LEVEL=info
    ports:
      - "5055:5055"
    volumes:
      - jellyseerr-config:/app/config
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:5055/api/v1/status || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellystat - Statistics and Analytics for Jellyfin
  # ==========================================================================
  jellystat:
    image: cyfershepard/jellystat:1.1.6
    container_name: jellystat
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - POSTGRES_USER=jellystat
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${JELLYSTAT_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_IP=jellystat-db
      - POSTGRES_PORT=5432
      - JWT_SECRET=${JELLYSTAT_JWT_SECRET}
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - jellystat-data:/app/backend/backup-data
    depends_on:
      jellystat-db:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # PostgreSQL - Database for Jellystat
  # ==========================================================================
  jellystat-db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    container_name: jellystat-db
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=jellystat
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${JELLYSTAT_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=jellystat
    volumes:
      - jellystat-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    shm_size: 128mb
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U jellystat"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  jellyfin-config:
  jellyfin-cache:
  jellyseerr-config:
  jellystat-data:
  jellystat-pgdata:

# =============================================================================
# Media Management LXC - Download & Library Management
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 402
# IP: 192.168.1.227
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Download clients and library managers with VPN protection.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 402
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 8192
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Media Management Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "media_management" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "media-management"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.media.media_management}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Privileged for VPN TUN device access
  unprivileged = false

  # Mount data directory (for hardlinks to work)
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      path   = "/data"
      volume = "/tank/data"
    }
  ]

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Media Management"
  service_description = "Download clients and library managers with VPN protection"

  service_urls = {
    qbittorrent = "https://qbittorrent.${var.domain_internal}"
    sonarr      = "https://sonarr.${var.domain_internal}"
    radarr      = "https://radarr.${var.domain_internal}"
    lidarr      = "https://lidarr.${var.domain_internal}"
    prowlarr    = "https://prowlarr.${var.domain_internal}"
    bazarr      = "https://bazarr.${var.domain_internal}"
    sabnzbd     = "https://sabnzbd.${var.domain_internal}"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Gluetun", port = 0, info = "VPN gateway (NordVPN WireGuard)" },
    { name = "qBittorrent", port = 8080, info = "BitTorrent client (via VPN)" },
    { name = "SABnzbd", port = 8085, info = "Usenet download client" },
    { name = "Prowlarr", port = 9696, info = "Indexer manager (via VPN)" },
    { name = "FlareSolverr", port = 8191, info = "Cloudflare bypass (via VPN)" },
    { name = "Sonarr", port = 8989, info = "TV show management" },
    { name = "Radarr", port = 7878, info = "Movie management" },
    { name = "Lidarr", port = 8686, info = "Music management" },
    { name = "Bazarr", port = 6767, info = "Subtitle management" },
    { name = "Recyclarr", port = 0, info = "TRaSH Guides sync (scheduled)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Storage (TRaSH Guides Compliant)

**Data Directory:** `/data` (mounted from `/tank/data`)
- `/data/torrents/movies` - Movie downloads
- `/data/torrents/tv` - TV show downloads
- `/data/torrents/music` - Music downloads
- `/data/library/movies` - Movie library (hardlinks from downloads)
- `/data/library/tv` - TV show library (hardlinks from downloads)
- `/data/library/music` - Music library (hardlinks from downloads)

## VPN Protection

All torrent traffic routes through Gluetun (NordVPN WireGuard):
- qBittorrent, Prowlarr, FlareSolverr use VPN network
- Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Bazarr use host network

**Check VPN status:**
```bash
docker exec gluetun wget -qO- ifconfig.me
```

## Quick Commands

**View all logs:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose logs -f
```

**Restart VPN:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose restart gluetun
```

**Check qBittorrent connectivity:**
```bash
docker exec qbittorrent curl -s ifconfig.me
```

## TRaSH Guides Sync

Recyclarr runs on schedule to sync quality profiles:
```bash
docker exec recyclarr recyclarr sync
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=media-management` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["media", "downloads", "arr"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "qbittorrent_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "qbittorrent"
  backend_url = "http://${module.media_management.ip_address}:8080"

  internal_domain = "qbittorrent.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.media_management]
}

module "sonarr_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "sonarr"
  backend_url = "http://${module.media_management.ip_address}:8989"

  internal_domain = "sonarr.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.media_management]
}

module "radarr_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "radarr"
  backend_url = "http://${module.media_management.ip_address}:7878"

  internal_domain = "radarr.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.media_management]
}

module "lidarr_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "lidarr"
  backend_url = "http://${module.media_management.ip_address}:8686"

  internal_domain = "lidarr.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.media_management]
}

module "prowlarr_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "prowlarr"
  backend_url = "http://${module.media_management.ip_address}:9696"

  internal_domain = "prowlarr.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.media_management]
}

module "bazarr_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "bazarr"
  backend_url = "http://${module.media_management.ip_address}:6767"

  internal_domain = "bazarr.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.media_management]
}

module "sabnzbd_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "sabnzbd"
  backend_url = "http://${module.media_management.ip_address}:8085"

  internal_domain = "sabnzbd.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.media_management]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "media_management_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.media_management.container_id
  container_ip   = module.media_management.ip_address
  container_name = "media-management"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-402"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,media-management"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["media-management"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["media-management"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.media_management]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.media_management.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.media_management.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.media_management.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    qbittorrent = module.qbittorrent_route.internal_url
    sonarr      = module.sonarr_route.internal_url
    radarr      = module.radarr_route.internal_url
    lidarr      = module.lidarr_route.internal_url
    prowlarr    = module.prowlarr_route.internal_url
    bazarr      = module.bazarr_route.internal_url
    sabnzbd     = module.sabnzbd_route.internal_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    qbittorrent = module.qbittorrent_route.remote_config_path
    sonarr      = module.sonarr_route.remote_config_path
    radarr      = module.radarr_route.remote_config_path
    lidarr      = module.lidarr_route.remote_config_path
    prowlarr    = module.prowlarr_route.remote_config_path
    bazarr      = module.bazarr_route.remote_config_path
    sabnzbd     = module.sabnzbd_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "media-management"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.media.media_management}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Privileged for VPN TUN device access
  unprivileged = false

  # Mount data directory (for hardlinks to work)
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      path   = "/data"
      volume = "/tank/data"
    }
  ]

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Media Management"
  service_description = "Download clients and library managers with VPN protection"

  service_urls = {
    qbittorrent = "https://qbittorrent.${var.domain_internal}"
    sonarr      = "https://sonarr.${var.domain_internal}"
    radarr      = "https://radarr.${var.domain_internal}"
    lidarr      = "https://lidarr.${var.domain_internal}"
    prowlarr    = "https://prowlarr.${var.domain_internal}"
    bazarr      = "https://bazarr.${var.domain_internal}"
    sabnzbd     = "https://sabnzbd.${var.domain_internal}"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Gluetun", port = 0, info = "VPN gateway (NordVPN WireGuard)" },
    { name = "qBittorrent", port = 8080, info = "BitTorrent client (via VPN)" },
    { name = "SABnzbd", port = 8085, info = "Usenet download client" },
    { name = "Prowlarr", port = 9696, info = "Indexer manager (via VPN)" },
    { name = "FlareSolverr", port = 8191, info = "Cloudflare bypass (via VPN)" },
    { name = "Sonarr", port = 8989, info = "TV show management" },
    { name = "Radarr", port = 7878, info = "Movie management" },
    { name = "Lidarr", port = 8686, info = "Music management" },
    { name = "Bazarr", port = 6767, info = "Subtitle management" },
    { name = "Recyclarr", port = 0, info = "TRaSH Guides sync (scheduled)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Storage (TRaSH Guides Compliant)

**Data Directory:** `/data` (mounted from `/tank/data`)
- `/data/torrents/movies` - Movie downloads
- `/data/torrents/tv` - TV show downloads
- `/data/torrents/music` - Music downloads
- `/data/library/movies` - Movie library (hardlinks from downloads)
- `/data/library/tv` - TV show library (hardlinks from downloads)
- `/data/library/music` - Music library (hardlinks from downloads)

## VPN Protection

All torrent traffic routes through Gluetun (NordVPN WireGuard):
- qBittorrent, Prowlarr, FlareSolverr use VPN network
- Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Bazarr use host network

**Check VPN status:**
```bash
docker exec gluetun wget -qO- ifconfig.me
```

## Quick Commands

**View all logs:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose logs -f
```

**Restart VPN:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose restart gluetun
```

**Check qBittorrent connectivity:**
```bash
docker exec qbittorrent curl -s ifconfig.me
```

## TRaSH Guides Sync

Recyclarr runs on schedule to sync quality profiles:
```bash
docker exec recyclarr recyclarr sync
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=media-management` to update.
EOT

}

# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - Loki + Alloy + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "Observability stack with Loki, Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana           = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus        = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager      = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma       = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"
    ntfy              = "https://ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct_loki       = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100"
    direct_alloy_grpc = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317"
    direct_alloy_http = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Loki", port = 3100, info = "Log aggregation" },
    { name = "Alloy (gRPC)", port = 4317, info = "OTLP gRPC receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy (HTTP)", port = 4318, info = "OTLP HTTP receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy UI", port = 12345, info = "Alloy debug UI" },
    { name = "Prometheus", port = 9090, info = "Metrics storage and alerting" },
    { name = "Grafana", port = 3000, info = "Dashboards and visualization" },
    { name = "Alertmanager", port = 9093, info = "Alert routing" },
    { name = "Uptime Kuma", port = 3001, info = "HTTP monitoring and status page" },
    { name = "ntfy", port = 8080, info = "Push notifications" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Alloy OTLP Endpoints (for Proxmox/Immich)

**OTLP gRPC:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317
**OTLP HTTP:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318

Configure Proxmox metrics server:
```bash
pvesh create /cluster/metrics/server \
  --id homelab-alloy \
  --type opentelemetry \
  --server ${local.lan_ips.monitoring} \
  --port 4317 \
  --proto grpc
```

## Loki Endpoint (for Alloy sidecars)

**Loki URL:** http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100

## Grafana

Default login: admin / (password in 1Password)

## ntfy Topics

- `homelab-alerts` - Prometheus alerts
- `homelab-status` - Uptime Kuma notifications

Subscribe via mobile app or web UI.

## Quick Commands

```bash
# View Alloy logs
docker logs -f alloy

# View Loki logs
docker logs -f loki

# Query logs via Loki API
curl -s "http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/labels" | jq

# Reload Prometheus config
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/-/reload

# Test ntfy notification
curl -d "Test notification" http://localhost:8080/homelab-alerts
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=monitoring` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["monitoring", "loki", "alloy", "prometheus", "grafana"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "monitoring_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    grafana_admin_password = local.op.grafana_admin_password
    uptime_kuma_username   = local.op.uptime_kuma_username
    uptime_kuma_password   = local.op.uptime_kuma_password
    discord_webhook_url    = local.op.discord_webhook_url
    # Grafana OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
    grafana_oauth_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.grafana.client_id
    grafana_oauth_client_secret = random_password.grafana_oidc_secret.result
    grafana_oauth_auth_url      = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/authorize/"
    grafana_oauth_token_url     = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/token/"
    grafana_oauth_api_url       = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/userinfo/"
    grafana_oauth_signout_url   = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/grafana/end-session/"
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/monitoring.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "monitoring_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.monitoring_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.monitoring.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "grafana_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "grafana"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "grafana.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "prometheus_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "prometheus"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9090"

  internal_domain = "prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "alertmanager_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "alertmanager"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9093"

  internal_domain = "alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "uptime_kuma_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "status"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3001"

  internal_domain = "status.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "ntfy_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "ntfy"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:8080"

  internal_domain = "ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.monitoring.container_id
  container_ip   = module.monitoring.ip_address

# =============================================================================
# Network Services LXC - AdGuard + Cloudflared + DDNS
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 101
#
# Core network infrastructure: DNS (AdGuard Home), Cloudflare tunnel, DDNS.
# Tailscale runs as systemd service (requires kernel access).
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 101
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "cloudflare_ddns_domains" {
  type    = string
  default = "homelab.rambtech.dev"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Network Services Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "network_services" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "network-services"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for DNS service)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.core.network_services}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.network_services}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Privileged for Tailscale kernel access
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude AdGuard config - managed separately via templating for dns_mode toggle
  exclude_patterns = ["AdGuardHome\\.yaml$", "\\.tpl$"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Network Services"
  service_description = "Core network infrastructure: DNS, tunnels, and VPN"

  service_urls = {
    adguard_internal = "https://dns.${var.domain_internal}"
    adguard_direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.network_services}:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "AdGuard Home", port = 53, info = "DNS server with ad blocking" },
    { name = "AdGuard UI", port = 3000, info = "Web management interface" },
    { name = "Cloudflared", port = 0, info = "Cloudflare tunnel (outbound only)" },
    { name = "Tailscale", port = 41641, info = "Mesh VPN (systemd service)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Tailscale Management

Tailscale runs as a systemd service (not Docker) because it requires kernel-level network access.

**Check status:**
```bash
systemctl status tailscaled
tailscale status
```

**Restart if needed:**
```bash
systemctl restart tailscaled
```

## Docker Services

**View logs:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose logs -f <service>
```

**Restart all services:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose restart
```

## DNS Testing

**Test AdGuard (port 53):**
```bash
dig @${local.lan_ips.network_services} google.com
```

**Test internal DNS rewrites:**
```bash
dig @${local.lan_ips.network_services} traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=network-services` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["network-services", "dns", "adguard", "cloudflare"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "network_services_env" {
  content = <<-EOT
# Network Services Environment Variables
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten

# Cloudflare Tunnel Token
CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN=${local.op.cloudflare_tunnel_token}

# Cloudflare API Token for DDNS
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=${local.op.cloudflare_api_token}

# Domains to update with DDNS
CLOUDFLARE_DDNS_DOMAINS=${var.cloudflare_ddns_domains}
EOT

  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/network-services.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "network_services_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.network_services_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.network_services.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.network_services]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AdGuard Home Configuration (DNS Mode Toggle)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generates AdGuard config based on dns_mode variable:
# - home: Uses LAN IPs (192.168.1.x) - works on home network without Tailscale
# - travel: Uses container IPs (10.100.x.x) - routes through Tailscale, avoids subnet conflicts

locals {
  # Select IP based on dns_mode
  adguard_traefik_ip = var.dns_mode == "travel" ? local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik : local.lan_ips.traefik
}

resource "local_file" "adguard_config" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/adguard/conf/AdGuardHome.yaml.tpl", {
    dns_mode   = var.dns_mode
    traefik_ip = local.adguard_traefik_ip
  })

  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/AdGuardHome.yaml"
  file_permission = "0644"
}

resource "filesync_file" "adguard_config" {
  source      = local_file.adguard_config.filename
  destination = "/config/adguard/conf/AdGuardHome.yaml"
  host        = module.network_services.ip_address

  mode = "0644"

  depends_on = [module.network_services]
}

# Restart AdGuard when config changes
resource "null_resource" "restart_adguard" {
  triggers = {
    config_hash = local_file.adguard_config.content_md5
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      "docker restart adguard || true"
    ]

    connection {
      type        = "ssh"
      user        = "root"
      host        = module.network_services.ip_address
      private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }
  }

  depends_on = [filesync_file.adguard_config]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tailscale Service Management via Ansible
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ensures Tailscale daemon is running and connected after deployment

resource "ansible_navigator_run" "manage_tailscale" {
  depends_on = [module.network_services]

  # Re-run when container is rebuilt or network config changes
  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
    lan_ip       = local.lan_ips.network_services
  }

  execution_environment = {
    enabled = false  # Run ansible directly on host
  }

  ansible_options = {
    private_keys = [{
      name = "homelab"
      data = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }]
  }

  playbook = <<-EOT
    - name: Manage Tailscale service on network-services
      hosts: lxc
      gather_facts: no
      vars:
        app_name: network-services

      tasks:
        # =====================================================================
        # Tailscale Service Management
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Ensure Tailscale daemon is running
          ansible.builtin.systemd:
            name: tailscaled
            state: started
            enabled: true
          register: tailscale_service

        - name: Wait for Tailscale to initialize
          ansible.builtin.pause:
            seconds: 3
          when: tailscale_service.changed

        # =====================================================================
        # Verify Tailscale Status
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Check Tailscale connection status
          ansible.builtin.command:
            cmd: tailscale status --json
          register: tailscale_status
          changed_when: false
          failed_when: false

        - name: Parse Tailscale status
          ansible.builtin.set_fact:
            tailscale_info: "{{ tailscale_status.stdout | from_json }}"
          when: tailscale_status.rc == 0

        - name: Display Tailscale connection info
          ansible.builtin.debug:
            msg: |
              Tailscale Status: {{ 'Connected' if (tailscale_info.BackendState | default('')) == 'Running' else 'Not Connected' }}
              Tailnet IP: {{ tailscale_info.Self.TailscaleIPs[0] | default('N/A') }}
              Hostname: {{ tailscale_info.Self.HostName | default('N/A') }}
          when: tailscale_status.rc == 0

        - name: Warn if Tailscale not connected
          ansible.builtin.debug:
            msg: "WARNING: Tailscale is not connected. Check authentication status with 'tailscale status'"
          when: tailscale_status.rc != 0 or (tailscale_info.BackendState | default('')) != 'Running'
  EOT

  inventory = yamlencode({
    lxc = {
      hosts = {
        "network-services" = {
          ansible_host = module.network_services.ip_address
          ansible_user = "root"
        }
      }
    }
  })
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "adguard_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "dns"
  backend_url = "http://${module.network_services.ip_address}:3000"

  internal_domain = "dns.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = ""  # DNS admin UI should not be public

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.network_services]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "network_services_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.network_services.container_id
  container_ip   = module.network_services.ip_address
  container_name = "network-services"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup

    namespace = "lxc-101"
